543972|2026-06.headline: Aeroflex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72.4% YoY to INR145.97 crore, with EBITDA margin at 23.04% and SFN skid assemblies contributing INR32.4 crore (~23%).
543972|2026-06.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR145.97 crore (+72.4% YoY), with EBITDA up 116% to INR33.5 crore and margin up 468 bps to 23.04%. PAT rose 162% to INR18.79 crore (about 13% margin). Growth came from flexible hoses (+41% YoY), assemblies and value-added products (faster), and the new SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies for data centres. Management said sequential margin dipped due to ramp-up manpower costs for Taloja and Chakan facilities and West Asia-related logistics costs.

financial_highlights.change: more than +100% YoY; margin +278 bps YoY

segments.name: Flexible hoses and assemblies
segments.commentary: Hoses grew 41% YoY and assemblies grew faster. Mix was 63% fittings/assemblies and 37% plain hose; hose-only margins are 16-20% and assembly margins 22-26%.

segments.name: SFN skid assemblies (data centre liquid cooling)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.4 crore on 1,040 units in Q1, about 23% of revenue. Capacity expanded from 6,000 to 9,000 units/yr; target 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27. Management says skid margin is in line with company average.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR3 crore in Q1. Management expects an uptick over the next two quarters; bellows utilisation is not yet at optimum.

segments.name: Hyd-Air
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR7 crore in Q1. Used internally for hose-assembly components, not sold to third parties; capex plan under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Company EBITDA margin target of 25% over the next few years; management says it is on track, but gave no quarterly margin guidance.
Flexible hose capacity to rise from 17.5 million m/yr to 20 million m/yr, to be completed by Q3 FY27; hose-related capex budget ~INR54 crore, with the remainder spent in FY27.
SFN skid capacity to reach 15,000 units/yr by expected Q3 FY27 (October-November, dependent on machine supplier delays); total skid capex budgeted at INR48 crore.
Q4 FY27 skid exit run-rate guided at ~60-65% utilisation on the 15,000-unit capacity (about 750 skids/month per analyst), which management said remains intact.
Optimal skid utilisation of ~80% expected in FY28, after a full year at 15,000 units.
Management cited a peak-utilisation potential of INR650-675 crore top line for flexible hose plus assemblies, assuming 70% of sales from assemblies.
Management said the SFN share of revenue would be discussed at year end, not quarterly; it did not reiterate the 25% share target.
capex_capacity: Flexible hoses: 17.5 to 20 million m/yr by Q3 FY27; current utilisation 65-66%.
SFN skids: 9,000 units/yr now, targeting 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27; some machines already commissioned, others arriving Q2 and Q3.
New Chakan (Pune) plant under setup; a new facility for hose assemblies for an international customer was also set up.
Hyd-Air capex plan for FY27 under discussion; to be announced once finalised.
Skid machines are largely fungible and can be redeployed to bellows or other flow-control applications (HVAC, ports, terminals).
demand_pricing: Export growth was 43% YoY; Europe (Italy, Spain, France, UK) and the US grew, including hose assemblies for European data-centre applications.
Skid assembly pricing varies by design. Management said the average value per skid is not a valid price metric and that margins are costed per design.
International skid competitors named: Senior and Parker, plus local players in the US and Europe. Management declined to name domestic competitors.
Largest US customer is the source of the fire-hose assembly for data centres, expected to be commercialised by end-Q1 FY28 with international supply; margin 23-26%.
Management said about 40-odd skids go into 1 MW of liquid-cooled IT load.
Customer dispatch schedules come about 2 months ahead; tentative Q3 project lists are also shared.
Logistics costs rose sharply due to the West Asia crisis, which began in mid-March and worsened through Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the flexible hose assembly business, and is it on track for 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Hose-only margins are 16-20% and assemblies 22-26%. The 25% target is for the whole company's blended EBITDA margin, not hose alone. Mix is 63% assemblies and 37% hose, so blended is about 22-23%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SFN average price per skid decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price per skid depends on design (piping length and content), so per-unit value is not a valid metric. It said margins are unaffected because each skid is costed separately.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the skid expansion from 9,000 to 15,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Total budgeted skid capex is INR48 crore for the expansion from 2,000 to 15,000. Some machines have arrived, others are planned for Q1 and Q2 FY28, and ancillary machines are used from day one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 exit run-rate of about 750 skids a month still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60-65% utilisation guidance on the 15,000-unit capacity remains intact, but the final Q4 plan depends on Q3 visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall 80 bps QoQ when skid volumes doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to added skid-team headcount, the new hose-assembly facility for an international customer, and higher logistics costs from the West Asia crisis. It asked to be judged on a YoY basis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 employee-cost deleverage is one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the costs relate to ramp-up manpower at Taloja (SFN) and Chakan, and that bellows utilisation is still below optimum, so margins should improve as those ramp up.

risks_watch: SFN 9,000 to 15,000 units/yr expansion depends on machine supplier delays; commissioning guided to Oct-Nov (expected Q3 FY27), with some machines still to arrive in Q2 and Q3.
Q4 FY27 skid utilisation guide of 60-65% on 15,000-unit capacity is only 'intact' for now; final Q4 plan depends on Q3 visibility. Design approvals by end customers can delay production.

Margin dilution: QoQ EBITDA margin fell 80 bps on added skid-team and Taloja/Chakan ramp-up manpower costs, plus West Asia logistics costs. Management asked to be judged YoY, and gave no quarterly margin guidance.
Fire-hose assembly for largest US data-centre customer (23-26% margin) expected to be commercialised by end-Q1 FY28 or start of Q2; realisation size not quantified.

Management declined to quantify SFN share of revenue (25% year-end target not reiterated), skid margins, Q2 delivery schedule, international skid volumes and further capex beyond 15,000 units. Hyd-Air capex plan still under discussion.

Skid revenue visibility is short: dispatch schedules come about 2 months ahead, with tentative Q3 project lists only; per-skid value varies widely by design, so average price per skid is not a usable metric.
key_quotes: So, these are mostly the costs related to -- so we have setting up of the plant at Chakan in Pune.

So, some of these cost of the employees, if you see the employee cost has increased because of the ramp-up in manpower that we have done both at the facility for SFN in Taloja and also the new facility coming up in Chakan.

So, I keep mentioning that quarter-on-quarter, it's -- I would want everyone to look at it or definitely look at our business not from a quarter-on-quarter basis, but from how we see it on a year-on-year basis
Well, I think I would talk about this at the end of the year because like I mentioned, it is the plan for the end of the year.
So as of now, how the things are playing up, we feel that, that is intact.
543972|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, scale-up and the 25% blended EBITDA target over several years, but evasive on specifics. Management declined to give skid-level margins, SFN share of revenue, Q2 schedules, domestic competitor names and the size of the fire-hose opportunity. It repeatedly redirected quarterly questions to a YoY or annual view.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Blended EBITDA margin 23.04% in Q1 (up 468 bps YoY but down 80 bps QoQ) with 25% target 'in next few years'; margin should recover as Taloja/Chakan manpower ramps and bellows reaches optimum, but no quarterly guidance was given and West Asia logistics costs are a drag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Flexible hose capacity 17.5 to 20 mn m/yr and SFN skid capacity 9,000 to 15,000 units/yr are under construction with budgeted capex of INR54 cr and INR48 cr, both guided for completion by start of Q3 FY27, though skid timing depends on machine vendor delays.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Hose utilisation is 65-66% and skid exit utilisation guided at 60-65% on 15,000 units (~750 skids/month) in Q4 FY27; Q1 revenue grew 72.4% YoY with flexible hoses +41% and exports +43%, but Q4 plan depends on Q3 visibility.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: after FY27 year-end, on Hyd-Air plan finalisation
rows.why: Hyd-Air capex plan for FY27 is under discussion and will be announced once finalised; hose and skid capex (INR54 cr and INR48 cr) is already committed, and utilisation at 65-66% does not yet force a new capex round.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not raise any numeric guidance, declined to quantify SFN share or skid margins and redirected quarterly questions to YoY/annual views; the 25% margin target was only 'held'.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Skid expansion depends on machine supplier delays (commissioning Oct-Nov, some machines arriving Q2 and Q3), the Q4 60-65% utilisation is only 'intact' pending Q3 visibility, and QoQ margin fell 80 bps on ramp-up manpower and West Asia logistics costs.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fire-hose assembly for the largest US data-centre customer, at 23-26% margin, is expected to be commercialised by end-Q1 FY28 with international supply; realisation size not quantified.

rows.label: SFN skid demand at ~60-65% Q4 utilisation
rows.why: Q1 SFN revenue INR32.4 cr on 1,040 units (~23% of revenue); Q4 exit guided at ~750 skids/month on 15,000 capacity, 'intact' but dependent on Q3 visibility.

rows.label: Export and European data-centre hose assemblies
rows.why: Exports grew 43% YoY with Europe (Italy, Spain, France, UK) and US growing, including hose assemblies for European data-centre applications; not quantified in INR.

rows.label: Logistics cost relief from West Asia crisis
rows.why: Logistics costs rose sharply from mid-March and worsened through Q1 with no relief timing given, so it remains a margin headwind.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, scale-up and the 25% blended margin target over several years, but evasive on specifics such as skid margins, SFN revenue share, Q2 schedules and the size of the fire-hose opportunity; analysts pushed on the QoQ margin dip and the per-skid price decline.

543972|2026-09.headline: Aeroflex Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR200 crores for the first time, with total income of INR207.68 crores, up 87% YoY, and PAT of INR36.56 crores.
543972|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 total income of INR207.68 crores (up 87% YoY), EBITDA of INR50.34 crores (up 94%, margin 24.27%) and PAT of INR36.56 crores (up 157%, margin 17.6%). H1 FY27 total income was INR353.66 crores (up 81%), with H1 EBITDA of INR83.83 crores and PAT of INR55.35 crores, already close to full-year FY26 performance. The company changed depreciation from WDV to SLM from 1 April 2026, reducing depreciation by INR8.41 crores in both Q2 and H1. It also announced a total capex of INR202 crores for capacity expansion and the merger of wholly owned subsidiary Hyd-Air Engineering into Aeroflex.

financial_highlights.metric: Depreciation impact of WDV to SLM change
financial_highlights.value: INR8.41 crores lower in Q2 and in H1
Q2 INR6 crores; Q1 INR3 crores; H1 INR9 crores
financial_highlights.change: Q2 vs INR3 crores in prior quarter

segments.name: Metal flexible hoses
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 40% YoY, supported by end-user industries and international customers. Current SS hose capacity utilisation is about 80%.

segments.name: Assemblies and other value-added products
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 44% YoY, reflecting demand for high-precision engineered flow solutions.

segments.name: Liquid cooling (skid assemblies)
segments.commentary: Contributed 24% of H1 FY27 revenue; management cited skids at upwards of 30% of total revenue. Average realisation per skid was INR3.39 lakhs in Q2. FY27 skid revenue target raised to INR150-200 crores from an initial INR125 crores.

segments.name: Vertical mix
segments.commentary: Data center is now the largest vertical. Ports and terminals is the next growth area, followed by oil and gas and steel. Combined, these verticals are about 26-27% of business, and firefighting plus steel, oil and gas about 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total sales growth of about 60%, with revenue of INR715-725 crores at least.
Skid utilisation expected to reach 40-50% in FY27. Skid capacity is 15,000 units per annum (12,000 commissioned); expansion to 30,000 units per annum by March 2028.
SS hose capacity to rise from 20 million to 30 million meters per annum by March 2028; peak hose-assembly revenue estimated at INR850-900 crores, assuming 70-75% of capacity for assemblies.
Incremental capacity expected to generate INR500-550 crores of revenue per year at peak utilisation; peak utilisation expected in FY30.
FY30 top line guided at about INR1,500 crores versus earlier FY29 target of INR1,000 crores, with EBITDA margins of about 25% and slightly upward.
Hyd-Air merger expected to add at least a couple of percentage points to margins through cost savings; no quantified figure yet. Hyd-Air turnover is about 3% of quarterly Aeroflex turnover.
capex_capacity: Total capex of INR202 crores: INR124 crores for SS flexible flow capacity (brownfield at Taloja plus a proposed new hose-assembly facility) and INR78 crores for skids.
SS flexible flow capacity: 20 million meters per annum completed; further 10 million meters per annum to reach 30 million, due by March 2028.
Skid capacity: 15,000 units per annum expansion due December 2026, with 12,000 units already commissioned; further expansion to 30,000 units by March 2028.
Funding: internal accruals first, then bridge and long-term debt; equity raise only if needed.
Welding automation: two lines added to reduce manual work, raise capacity and reduce rejections. Patent granted for automated 3D CAD model generation of braided hose assemblies.
demand_pricing: Liquid cooling: exclusive arrangement with one large US multinational for the Indian market; no direct bidding to data center end-users. Global liquid cooling market is about $4-5 billion, growing more than 30% YoY; Vertiv is the largest player globally and in India. Indian market size not disclosed.
Visibility: confirmed pipeline of about 3 months (frozen for the current and start of next quarter); longer-term view is an estimate only.

International: advanced-stage sampling and pricing with the same customer, with no timeline given; other international prospects are at an early stage. Realisation expected to be higher than India, not quantified.
Freight and forwarding costs rose significantly on international shipping cost increases. There was no Q1-to-Q2 revenue shift.

qa_highlights.question: Expected cost savings and margin expansion from the Hyd-Air merger?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific number yet; management expects at least a couple of percentage points of margin gain from cost savings, with exact figures after the merger completes.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental capacity exclusive to the Indian customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Exclusivity for India remains. Capacity is earmarked for customers irrespective of plant, and the remaining capacity is fungible for exports or other customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the skid utilisation outlook for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is expected to reach 40-50% of total skid capacity in FY27, with projections revised monthly or quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY30 and margin targets after the expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line of about INR1,500 crores by FY30, with EBITDA margin of about 25% and slightly upward, balancing scale benefits against pricing pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and skid outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales growth of about 60% (INR715-725 crores at least); skid revenue of INR150-200 crores against the initial INR125 crores target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables grew more slowly than sales, and trade receivable days fell in Q2 and H1 versus last year.

risks_watch: International liquid cooling supply has no timeline; audits, controls and design differences for each country may delay conversion.
Freight and shipping costs have risen sharply and are a major expense driver.
Pricing pressure as the company scales in verticals, which management cites as offsetting scale benefits.
Capex of INR202 crores relies on internal accruals and bridge debt, with equity raise possible if needed.
Skid realisation per unit varies widely (INR1.5 lakhs to INR5 lakhs), so the quarterly average is not a reliable trend.
Management declined to give details on a potential acquisition for products adjacent to SFN, and on the parent company's sanitary valves acquisition.

Management often gave ranges and said figures would follow later.

543977|2026-03.headline: Rishabh Instruments FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 161% to INR1,264 mn (16.3% margin); 20% dividend declared and FY27 EEI growth guided at 20-25%.
543977|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7.6% to INR7,751 mn in FY26 and 9.3% to INR2,049 mn in Q4, while consolidated EBITDA more than doubled to INR1,264 mn and PAT rose 292% to INR823 mn. Standalone gross margin expanded to 54% from 48.6%, driven by product mix and sourcing. Lumel Alucast (HPDC) turned adjusted EBITDA positive at INR33 mn from a loss of INR150 mn, but its revenue fell 9.6% as loss-making contracts were exited. Management declared a 20% dividend (INR2 per INR10 share) and reported net cash of INR1,276 mn.

segments.name: Standalone Rishabh Instruments
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR788 mn (+15.2% YoY) with EBITDA INR161 mn (20.4% margin); FY26 PAT INR417 mn (+78.2%). US business grew about 50% to roughly USD3 mn, with a 40-50% growth target for FY27.

segments.name: Lumel SA (Poland, electronics)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR585 mn (+35.9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA INR167 mn (28.6% margin); FY26 PAT INR419 mn (+19.5%). A new SMT line was commissioned, 40% funded by EU funds.

segments.name: Lumel Alucast (HPDC, Poland)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR575 mn (-22.8% YoY) with Q4 PAT loss of INR58 mn; FY26 PAT loss INR41 mn vs INR252 mn in FY25. Management targets no losses in FY27 and double-digit margins in FY28.

segments.name: Smaller entities (Shanghai V&A, Sifam Tinsley US and UK)
segments.commentary: Growth of 53% (US), 25% (UK) and 23% (China) on top line; together they are 13% of the EEI business and all three are EBITDA positive.

segments.name: Solar inverters (within EEI)
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO launched in H2 FY25 and now operationally profitable; FY27 target about INR24-25 crore, roughly double FY26.

guidance_outlook: EEI segment FY27 top-line growth guided at 20-25% (around 20-22% in the blended view), with EBITDA margin guided at 20-22%; management said margin could be higher.
Solar inverter sales target about INR24-25 crore in FY27; the new building can scale to about INR100 crore with incremental capex.
US business targeted at 40-50% growth in FY27 with a longer-term aim of about INR100 crore in 3-4 years.
Lumel Alucast FY27 revenue expected to be flat to slightly down, roughly INR180 crore in euro terms, with no losses; double-digit margin expected in FY28.
Asked about FY28 (March 2028), management said INR1,000 crore revenue may be close but not guaranteed, with EBITDA around INR200 crore if guidelines hold; for FY27 it cited INR150-160 crore EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Nashik expansion capex complete; two manufacturing facilities almost ready and under commissioning, expected to effectively double production capacity. Commissioning expected by June-July 2026.
Current transformer capacity being expanded from 6,000 to 10,000 units per day with additional lines, equipment and manpower.
Lumel SA commissioned an advanced SMT electronics assembly line in FY26, 40% funded by EU funds.
New building: one full floor dedicated to solar manufacturing, with assembly lines added as volume grows.
Medium-voltage CTs, PTs and VTs: 4-5 new products expected by end FY27, with sales from FY28; no plans for high-voltage products.
demand_pricing: Management expects Europe to be subdued, with US, Southeast Asia and Africa seeing rising power and automation investment.
Solar: Chinese SKD-based competitors are cheaper; management says about half of the product range is now cost-competitive. Europe solar is declining, so Middle East is the preferred next market.
Alucast: qualification cycles are long (volume arrives about one year after order booking); European HPDC competitors are closing and some business is shifting to India and China.
Pricing: management said it passes on material and cost increases in EEI because it owns its brands and prices.
Data centre and sectoral marketing (Sify repeat projects, UK and Ireland): the company is bundling products with software and hiring specification specialists.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin should be expected for the EEI business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 20-25% top-line growth (about 20-22% blended) and 20-22% EBITDA margin; Rishabh and Lumel are each expected to grow about 20%, with smaller entities around 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Alucast's FY27 margin guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a transition year with no losses and no big margin targets; double-digit margin is expected in FY28, not FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will Alucast be demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no decision has been taken; a demerger is a possibility, but nothing is concrete and the company will inform the market at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: Is solar inverter cost-competitive with Chinese products, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is close but not yet fully competitive, with about half of the range competitive. FY27 target is INR24-25 crore, with OEM supply to assemblers and own-brand sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US revenue and the long-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue reached about USD3 mn in FY26 (from USD2 mn), with 40-50% growth planned for FY27 and about INR100 crore targeted in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cross INR1,000 crore revenue and INR200 crore EBITDA by March 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is possible if guidelines hold but would not commit; the EEI business at INR560 crore growing 20% would reach about INR670 crore, while Alucast stays flat.

risks_watch: Alucast volume recovery: FY27 revenue could fall below INR200 crore (about INR180 crore in euro terms); breakeven depends on winning new projects and their qualification timelines.
Solar inverter profitability: management said margins are 15-20% gross, and cost competitiveness vs Chinese imports is incomplete.
Geopolitical and energy risk: management flagged West Asia war, oil shortages and tariffs as risks to FY27 guidance; rupee depreciation affects euro-based Lumel and Alucast figures.
Timing of the Nashik capacity commissioning (June-July 2026) and the medium-voltage product launches expected by end FY27.
Dividend sustainability: 20% dividend (INR2 per INR10 share) declared; an analyst asked about future payouts of 20% or more.

543977|2026-06.headline: Rishabh Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 4.2% to INR1,983 mn, with EBITDA up 17.3% to INR333 mn at a 16.8% margin.
543977|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR1,983 mn (+4.2% YoY) and EBITDA INR333 mn (+17.3% YoY, 16.8% margin), after a INR20 mn ESOP/SAR charge; reported PAT was INR194 mn (-1.4% YoY) due to a INR20 mn rise in depreciation. The EEI segment was the engine: management cited 34% revenue growth and roughly 24% EBITDA margin, ahead of its ~20% top-line and 20-22% EBITDA guidance. Lumel Alucast remained a planned revenue decline (-41.2%) and was at operating breakeven with adjusted EBITDA of -6.4%. The company stayed net debt-free with net cash of INR1,606 mn.

segments.name: EEI (Electrical & Electronics Instrumentation)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 34% YoY with EBITDA margin around 24%, above the 20-22% guidance; management calls it the group's primary growth and profitability engine.

segments.name: Rishabh India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR776 mn (+25.6%), EBITDA margin 22.9%; growth attributed to current transformers, data centres, solar and exports. Solar is under 5% of total and was about INR8-9 crore last year.

segments.name: Lumel S.A. (Poland)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR639 mn (+39%), adjusted EBITDA INR153 mn (24%), contributing about 50% of consolidated bottom line; one German grid-upgrade customer is roughly 20-25% of its sales.

segments.name: Lumel Alucast (HPDC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR443 mn (-41.2%) as a planned decline; adjusted EBITDA -INR28 mn (-6.4%), at operating breakeven. Management targets adjusted EBITDA breakeven by end FY27 and double-digit margin over the medium term.

segments.name: US / UK / China and other international
segments.commentary: US and UK grew over 40% YoY and China 20.3%; US is about INR30 crore last year with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years on an organic basis. Management says these remain on a small base.

segments.name: Solar inverters
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO (up to 5 kW) reached operational profitability; 3-phase iNEO launched up to 12 kW this quarter, with up to 50 kW due by end FY27 and hybrid inverters in development. FY27 solar target is INR24-25 crore, rising to INR250-300 crore next year per management.

guidance_outlook: EEI guidance held at about 20% top-line growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for the full year; management said it will try to beat this but did not raise it.
Lumel Alucast expected to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven for full-year FY27; management sees a path to double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years.
US organic revenue target INR45 crore this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years.
Nashik plant to be fully finished in about 1-2 months; management targets more than 2.5x production over the next 4-5 years.
Mumbai and Delhi TMI Experience Centres to be operational by end of FY27; ~15 new products launched over two years with more than 15 planned for FY27.
CT capacity to rise from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage CTs to follow.
capex_capacity: New Nashik manufacturing facility partially commissioned; both buildings complete, with full completion expected in about 1-2 months.
Current transformer capacity being raised from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day (near-doubling), with added machinery already ordered.
Three SMT lines in PCB/EMS operations; latest is high-end and an older line is being upgraded. A fourth line will be added once the three run on three shifts.
Dedicated automated floor for solar inverter manufacturing in the new facility.
Lumel Alucast capacity is underutilised; management is filling it with higher-value orders.
demand_pricing: Domestic order bookings in Q1 were about 20% above last year, but billing lagged, leaving a backlog to be worked off.
Data-centre wins: first win announced, then 3-4 more; about 10 more quotes outstanding.

Lumel S.A. growth comes from product spread, German grid upgrades (EUR5 mn order executed; EUR3 mn follow-on running to year-end) and radiation-detection gates, with Poland security demand after the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Lumel Alucast: RFQs in advanced stages of commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management is prioritising value over volume.
Solar inverter pricing is competitive with Chinese imports; EPC contractors are moving away from Chinese-sourced units over after-sales and warranty concerns.
Contribution margin is about 45% on average; solar and EMS run at 15-20%, while other products run at 40-75%.

financial_highlights.value: INR382 mn (24.8% margin, EEI basis as described)

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and cash equivalents (30 June 2026)

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the 34% EEI growth, versus the 20-25% guidance, and is there lumpiness that will moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is spread across Rishabh India (current transformers, data centres, solar), Lumel S.A. (product spread, German grid upgrades) and new products, not one lumpy item. It reiterated EEI guidance of around 20% top-line and 20-22% EBITDA margin, saying it will try to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: How fast can the US business scale, and are there inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue went from about INR20 crore to INR30 crore last year, with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years organically. Actions include more sales staff, Mexico/Canada focus, UL/ANSI product redesigns, and a couple of inorganic opportunities under review.

qa_highlights.question: Lumel Alucast: what is the pipeline for returning to INR180-230 crore revenue and double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: RFQs are in advanced commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management sees double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years and says costs have been cut substantially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quarterly EEI growth trajectory continue, and what about AI/data-centre traction in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is almost comparable to last year's Q4 and the company wants to beat guidance rather than raise it, citing seasonality in Europe and Diwali. Data-centre wins are one announced plus 3-4 more, with about 10 quotes outstanding; domestic bookings were about 20% higher YoY but billing lagged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Lumel S.A. and India growth came from the German customer and from solar inverters?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EUR5 mn German order is already executed; the EUR3 mn follow-on runs to year-end, estimated at 20-25% of Lumel S.A. sales. Solar is under 5% of total, about INR8-9 crore last year, targeted at INR24-25 crore this year and INR250-300 crore next year; EEI contribution margin for solar and EMS is 15-20% versus about 45% average.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and adjacencies: CT capacity, PCB/EMS, battery systems and M&A size?
qa_highlights.answer: CT capacity is moving from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage to follow. Three SMT lines run PCB/EMS, with a fourth once they hit three shifts. Battery systems will be indirect via hybrid inverters. Acquisitions considered in the INR50-200 crore range; about 4-5 targets under review, none at a serious stage.

risks_watch: EEI growth sustainability: management held guidance at about 20% top line and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite 34% Q1 growth; watch whether Q2-Q4 deliver and whether seasonality (European summer and winter holidays, Diwali) bites.
Lumel Alucast: still EBITDA-negative (-6.4% adjusted) with revenue down 41.2%; breakeven targeted by end FY27 and double-digit margin in about 2 years depends on RFQ conversion and a 6-month ramp.
Domestic billing lag: bookings about 20% above last year but billing has not caught up, leaving a backlog to work off.
Customer concentration: one German grid-upgrade customer is estimated at 20-25% of Lumel S.A. sales, with the EUR3 mn follow-on running only to year-end.

Solar scale-up risk: FY27 target of INR24-25 crore and next-year INR250-300 crore depends on iNEO 3-phase up to 12 kW and 50 kW models due by end FY27, plus hybrid inverters still in development; pricing is competitive with Chinese imports.
Margin and PAT pressure: consolidated PAT fell 1.4% YoY on a INR20 mn rise in depreciation, and ESOP/SAR costs of INR20 mn per quarter continue for about three more years.
key_quotes: So we see the growth coming out of multiple factors actually.
And this quarter, we have delivered more than that on the EEI business. And it will be around that or more throughout the year.
We want to keep our guidelines, which are already kind of aggressive, and we want to beat them by performance rather than giving guidelines which are a bit risky.
So any addition to the top line will very quickly reflect into the bottom line.
We're almost doubling our capacity, close to doubling our capacity.
543977|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on EEI and Lumel S.A., with management repeatedly describing growth as broad-based and sustainable. Noticeably cautious on guidance, declining to raise the 20% top-line target and saying it prefers to beat guidance rather than give aggressive numbers. Lumel Alucast and US timelines were framed as a process needing time, and several answers on inorganic plans and forward numbers were deliberately non-committal.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EEI margin ran about 24% in Q1 against 20-22% guidance, Lumel S.A. adjusted EBITDA margin rose 1,190 bps to 24%, and Lumel Alucast is guided to adjusted EBITDA breakeven by end FY27, though solar and EMS run at only 15-20% contribution margin versus about 45% average.

rows.when: Q2 FY27 (Nashik full completion in about 1-2 months)
rows.why: Nashik facility is partially commissioned with both buildings complete and full completion in 1-2 months, and CT capacity is being lifted from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 units/day with machinery already ordered.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic order bookings were about 20% above last year, US target is INR45 crore this year versus about INR30 crore last year, and solar is targeted at INR24-25 crore from under 5% of total, though consolidated revenue grew only 4.2% in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it is almost doubling capacity, with CT capacity near-doubling and a fourth SMT line planned once three lines hit three shifts, and acquisitions in the INR50-200 crore range with 4-5 targets under review.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: EEI grew 34% in Q1 against about 20% full-year guidance, but management held guidance and said it prefers to beat rather than raise, citing European and Diwali seasonality.

rows.why: Q1 EEI growth of 34% is unlikely to persist at that pace given seasonality, Lumel S.A. depends on one German customer at 20-25% of sales with the EUR3 mn follow-on only to year-end, and Lumel Alucast revenue is down 41.2% with adjusted EBITDA at -6.4%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans more than 15 new products in FY27 after about 15 over two years, 3-phase iNEO up to 50 kW due by end FY27, and hybrid inverters in development.

rows.label: US business scale-up to INR45 crore this year
rows.why: US revenue rose from about INR20 crore to INR30 crore last year, with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years, supported by more sales staff and Mexico/Canada focus.

rows.label: Lumel Alucast RFQ conversion and return to growth
rows.why: RFQs are in advanced commercial negotiation, ramp-up takes about 6 months after award, and revenue is down 41.2% to INR443 mn, so breakeven by end FY27 depends on conversion.

rows.label: Solar inverter ramp to INR250-300 crore next year
rows.why: FY27 solar target is INR24-25 crore from about INR8-9 crore last year, and the FY28 jump depends on 50 kW iNEO models due by end FY27 and hybrid inverters still in development, against competitive Chinese pricing.

543978|2026-03.headline: Ratnaveer guides FY27 top line of ~1,350-1,500 crore and FY28 consolidated 2,500 crore incl. 750 crore from new CCL plant; FY26 standalone OCF negative ~48 crore.
543978|2026-03.overview: Management reiterated a growth plan built around a new copper-clad laminate (CCL) plant in Gujarat, with first line targeted for November 2026 production and five lines over about two years. FY26 top line was 1,078 crore against a 1,350 crore target for the current year, with stainless/fastener business guided at about 25% CAGR. Cash flow questions drew a contested answer: an analyst cited FY26 standalone operating cash flow of about negative 48 crore, while management attributed the low cash generation to capex advances, depreciation and QIP funds held as FDs. Receivables rose sharply (analyst cited about 65 crore to 175 crore), which management attributed to new product launches and longer credit to new customers.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue grew from 419 crore three years earlier

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 standalone operating cash flow (analyst-cited, disputed in detail)

financial_highlights.change: Mgmt said partly reclassified from finance cost
Falls to about 42-43% after 330 crore QIP

segments.name: Stainless steel fasteners and washers (existing business)
segments.commentary: Management guided 25% CAGR, with 1,350 crore target for the current year and about 1,800 crore in three years. Company claims largest SKU count for stainless washers in India and serves 31 countries.

segments.name: Copper-clad laminate (CCL, new)
segments.commentary: Five-line plant with 338 crore ECMS approval; first line targeted November 2026. Individual CCL business guided at about 20% EBITDA and 13% PAT, with 750 crore revenue at 69% utilisation targeted for FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line: management said 1,350-1,400 crore is the base case, and that it remains on track for about 1,500 crore after an analyst flagged a downgrade from earlier 1,500 crore guidance.
FY28 consolidated target of about 2,500 crore revenue, 13-13.5% EBITDA and about 10.5% PAT, including 750 crore from CCL.
CCL first line production targeted November 2026; machine dispatch from China around July 2026; installation August-October 2026.
Remaining four CCL lines to be installed over the next two years depending on first-line performance; utilisation of 80-85% targeted by 2028, with 69% assumed conservatively.
Expected PLI and state incentives (about 50% of capex from central and state schemes, power cost exemption, interest subsidy) cited, with disbursement in about 4-5 months after project completion.
Planned 330 crore fundraise (QIP or equivalent) targeted for completion by September 2026; remaining warrant balance to be converted by about September 2027.
Proposed acquisition of a European precision components company: management said due diligence will take about 10-12 more months.
capex_capacity: CCL plant: 5 lines in total under ECMS (338 crore approval); project cost about 351 crore plus about 46 crore solar; split about 70% plant and machinery (turnkey), 80% building, and 12% miscellaneous (as stated).
Machinery ordered from a Chinese technology partner; advance paid January 2026 and second tranche paid; second-round inspection completed; civil and PV work in progress.
Technology agreement signed December 2025; partner to supply machinery, install, train staff and provide 1.5-2 years of quality support. Management said no royalty is payable.
Plant is in Gujarat; land already owned by the company.
Capex 1, Capex 2 and Capex 2A referenced as ongoing for the existing business.
demand_pricing: Management claims no anti-dumping duty currently on CCL imports and states 10-13% price competitiveness versus imports; Indian PCB makers receive 2% cash subsidy for buying indigenous material (as stated).
Management says the five lines would be about 2% of Indian CCL demand, which it says is growing 30-35% (or 35-40% CAGR per another comment).
Soft confirmations received from PCB companies; no firm pre-orders yet. Management said one or two customers may be ready to buy the first line.
Management said the Iran war (about 45-60 days) has not affected demand; oil and gas and consumable costs rising, and management said these can be passed on to customers.
Customer concentration: top 5 washer customers about 2-5% of sales; top finishing-line customers about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the warrants at 159 due for conversion and will they be forfeited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25% was already paid, the balance can be converted, and the 18-month window runs to about September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for CCL, technical tie-up terms and competition from China and Korea?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the partner is paid through machinery purchase, with no royalty; the plant is fully automated and it claims 10-13% price advantage versus imports.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated FY28 2,500 crore plan and FY26 revenue base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1,078 crore in FY26 and 1,350 crore target this year, with the existing business growing 25% CAGR to 1,800 crore and CCL adding 750 crore in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Negative operating cash flow and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Ajay Panchal said net cash flow of 203 crore was inflated by QIP funds held as FDs, and that advances to capex suppliers and depreciation drove the weak FY26 operating cash flow; the analyst's 48 crore figure was not directly rebutted.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rising from 65 crore to about 175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables rose on new products, new customers and launch credit, and expects normalisation as the business matures; no quantified timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: PLI incentive quantum and timing on 70 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of eligible capex (25% central plus 25% state) would be reimbursed, received within about 3-6 months of completion, and power, logistics and interest subsidies also apply.

risks_watch: CCL execution: Chinese machinery arrival around July 2026, monsoon impact on civil works, and first production target November 2026.
Funding gap: 330 crore raise targeted by September 2026 to fund CCL project and working capital; execution risk on fundraise timing.
Cash flow and receivables: negative operating cash flow reported by analyst for FY26, and receivables growth well above revenue growth.
Warrant conversion and dilution: promoter stake may fall from about 47-48% to 42-43% after QIP and warrants.
Management statements on CCL demand (soft confirmations only, no firm orders) and the European acquisition (10-12 months to close) are unverified.
Some management answers were unclear or inconsistent (e.g., CCL CAGR quoted as both 30-35% and 35-40%; guidance changed between 1,350 and 1,500 crore for FY27).
543978|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the CCL opportunity and growth targets, but evasive on cash flow and receivables, and inconsistent on several figures and guidance numbers.
key_quotes: So, we have been tied up with the Chinese company for the technological partner, and tail up to the installation, commissioning, and quality of the product should be coming out.
Total, we are getting the 338 crores of the approval from the ECMS scheme of Central Government of India.
No, dear. Sanjay, there is no, royalty would be that, but yes, we have an internal agreement that we have been buying the machine from them.
So, in 2028, we can definitely give the full utilization of this plant. So, the 750 crores would be a definitely achievable figure.

rows.why: Machinery advances paid Jan 2026, technology agreement signed Dec 2025, dispatch from China ~July 2026 and installation Aug-Oct 2026 with first production targeted November 2026; 351 crore project cost, with 4 more lines planned over ~2 years depending on line 1 performance.

rows.why: Existing stainless fastener/washer business guided ~25% CAGR to ~1,800 crore, and CCL adds 750 crore at 69% utilisation (80-85% target by 2028), though FY26 revenue was 1,078 crore and CCL demand has no firm orders.

rows.why: Management guided 4 further CCL lines over two years and a 330 crore fundraise by Sept 2026 to fund the project; existing-business utilisation is not disclosed, but CCL line 1 utilisation is targeted at 80-85% by 2028, which implies follow-on capex.

rows.why: Receivables reportedly rose from about 65 crore to 175 crore and FY26 standalone OCF was about negative 48 crore (analyst-cited, not rebutted), with management giving no quantified timeline for normalisation.

543980|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15.1% to INR387.8 crores and FY26 total income reached INR1,499.8 crores, with Dombivli opened ahead of schedule.
543980|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR387.8 crores (up 15.1%), EBITDA of INR89.2 crores (23% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crores (up 11.5%). For FY26, total income was INR1,499.8 crores (up 15.2%), EBITDA INR343.3 crores (up 14.4%, 22.9% margin) and PAT INR194.2 crores. Dombivli, the first greenfield hospital since listing, was inaugurated in February 2026, about two months before the call. Management outlined a pipeline taking capacity from about 1,200 to nearly 3,000 beds, including a 400-bed BKC hospital, with funding planned from internal accruals and debt capped at 3x EBITDA.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 75%; growth expected to be inflation-linked at current capacity, with an expansion awaiting final approvals.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy close to 65% with headroom to grow; Pune South is on track to open in calendar 2028.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy 45-50% after last year's added capacity; ramp-up driven by occupancy and case mix; second phase of 111 beds to be triggered when occupancy nears 60%.

segments.name: Dombivli (new, greenfield)
segments.commentary: Opened February 2026 with 750,000 sq ft built, 500-bed superstructure and about 300 beds fitted out; expected EBITDA burn INR2-3 crores per month on average in FY27, with breakeven targeted by end of calendar 2027/2028; INR9.4 crores Dombivli contribution is included in Q4 results.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month on average for the full year; EBITDA breakeven expected at end of two years of operation (calendar 2027-28).
Dombivli insurance tie-ups expected in 6-12 months, linked to NABH accreditation that needs about six months of operating data.
Pune South to open in calendar 2028; Mira Road expected to start excavation by end of calendar 2026.
Thane expansion approvals expected in FY27; scope and scale to be disclosed once final approvals are received.
Land payment for BKC: 25% of land cost paid; management said the remainder would be paid within this financial year.
Capacity target of about 1,700 new beds in this cycle, taking long-term capacity to nearly 3,000 beds at an average capex of about INR1.5 crores per bed.
Funding: internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt capped at 3x EBITDA considered sufficient; detailed calculations to follow.
Base business growth: Thane inflation-linked; Pune inflation plus occupancy; Indore occupancy, inflation and case mix. Management declined to quantify growth given inflation uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Dombivli opened February 2026, ahead of the Q1 FY27 target, on time and on budget with no cost escalation.
BKC: 400-bed quaternary care hospital on over 1 lakh sq ft in BKC; land allotted by MMRDA, with regulatory clearance and possession formalities underway.
Mira Road: architectural drawings complete, regulatory clearances in progress, excavation expected by end of calendar 2026.
Pune South on track for calendar 2028 opening; all projects are greenfield, full-scale hubs in Mumbai and Pune on owned real estate.
Indore phase two (111 beds) on hold until occupancy reaches around 60%.
demand_pricing: ARPOB rose 11.7% YoY to INR67,700 in Q4; drivers cited were Indore case-mix maturity and insurance renewals (roughly every two years) giving price increases plus inflation.
Insurance is 55.4% of revenue; government 1%. Insurance renewals are rolling with no single season.
International medical tourism is very small; management said it is not a focus and is not margin accretive, preferring domestic and local demand within a 45-minute drive radius.
Cost watch items: depreciating rupee and capex cost inflation; doctor costs and consumables not yet materially impacted by global supply chain disruption.
Management referred to a current war situation as a factor limiting inflation visibility.

qa_highlights.question: How is Dombivli ramping in occupancy and revenue, and when will the major insurance tie-up happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about two months of operations, so occupancy is too early to quantify; insurance tie-ups are linked to NABH accreditation and are likely in 6-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and funding for the expansion to about 2,900 beds be managed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals over the next 5 years plus some debt, with a self-imposed ceiling of 3x EBITDA, should cover it.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy and ARPOB by unit, and can the base business grow more than 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Thane about 75% occupancy, Pune close to 65%, Indore 45-50%. Growth is inflation-linked plus occupancy and case mix; no numeric guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ARPOB increase during the year?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination of Indore maturing with better case mix, and insurance renewals after a two-year cycle giving price increases plus inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will Dombivli add fixed costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, more fixed costs are expected as doctor hiring continues over the next couple of years for a large facility.

qa_highlights.question: Share of revenue from foreign patients and the government's medical tourism push?
qa_highlights.answer: Very little foreign revenue; management is not focused on international medical tourism and does not see it as margin accretive.

risks_watch: Dombivli ramp-up: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month and rising fixed costs until breakeven; insurance empanelment and NABH accreditation timing.
Funding load from BKC and the wider pipeline (about 1,700 beds, average INR1.5 crores per bed); rupee depreciation and capex cost inflation.
Indore: occupancy still 45-50%, and the second phase depends on occupancy reaching about 60%.
Regulatory approvals for Thane expansion and BKC/Mira Road site clearances (MMRDA possession formalities) remain pending, with no firm dates.

543984|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose to INR 1,279 crore with 12.3% revenue growth; net debt/EBITDA ~3x (3.07x) and FY27 revenue guided at 10-11%.
543984|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue growth was 12.3% against a 9-11% guidance band, with same-store RevPAR up 9.5%, despite several one-off disruptions that cut revenue by an estimated INR 45-52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA rose 8.8% to INR 463 crore at a 36.2% margin, and the GST slab change weighed on H2 margins. Q4 EBITDA fell 6% YoY to about INR 120 crore, which management attributes to GST, FF&E charges, pre-opening costs and the Middle East conflict hitting March revenue. Net debt fell to INR 1,450 crore after the GIC infusion, and a deferred tax credit of about INR 330 crore lifted reported PAT to about INR 567 crore. Management guided FY27 same-store revenue growth of 9-10% and total revenue growth of 10-11%, and a 38%-plus group margin.

Includes ~INR 330 crore deferred tax income in Q4 and ~INR 83 crore impairment reversal; includes gain on Caspia Delhi sale

segments.name: Core markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, Delhi NCR)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 76% of asset income in FY26. Delhi NCR same-store RevPAR declined about 9%; management expects mid-teens growth there in FY27 as Hyatt Place Gurgaon renovation completed by end-Q3 FY26.

segments.name: Upscale and upper-upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Upscale hotels run at upwards of 42-43% margins; Holiday Inn Express margins at 41-42%. Incremental pipeline is weighted to upscale, limiting exposure to sub-INR 7,500 room rates.

segments.name: Asset recycling and non-core hotels
segments.commentary: Monetised 4 non-core hotels for INR 210 crore at about 20x EV/EBITDA over three years. Target now INR 200-250 crore over the next two years; Caspia Delhi was sold for INR 63 crore with EBITDA of about INR 1.5-2 crore.

segments.commentary: Acquired 70% stake in a curated platform of 73 hotels and about 1,000 rooms; under discussion for affiliation with Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy.

Group EBITDA margin guided at about 38%, with 38%-plus maintained through the year; management says margins should reach 40%-plus on a normalised basis over time.
GST impact is permanent in absolute terms and has been about INR 7.5 crore YoY in Q3 and about INR 10 crore in Q4; normalises from Q3 FY27 on a YoY basis.
FY27 interest expense about INR 127 crore on existing debt; guided at INR 135-140 crore including a 15-20 bps rate-hardening assumption.
Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise at about 2.5x in 12-18 months; currently 3.07x.
FY27 capex INR 250-270 crore (about INR 150 crore for W Hyderabad, opening at end-FY27); FY28 similar run-rate, mainly Westin Bangalore. Total pipeline capex about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
capex_capacity: W Hyderabad (HITEC City) to open at end-FY27; expected to add about 6-7% revenue growth on a run-rate basis from FY28.
Pipeline openings: Tribute Bangalore Whitefield at end-FY28; Westin Bangalore Whitefield, Ingka Noida (162 rooms, variable lease) and Marriott Stiperumbudur (135 rooms, Chennai) in FY29-FY30.
Navi Mumbai 700-room Westin and Fairfield project announced; One Financial District Hyderabad (260 rooms) under development. Management excluded both from revenue and EBITDA forecasts.
GIC platform: INR 750 crore for a 35% stake in a 1,000-room upscale platform; INR 600 crore received, INR 150 crore balance over about two years linked to Westin Tribute Bangalore capex.
Over five years FY27-FY31, free cash of about INR 1,550 crore (flat base) plus about INR 1,000 crore from same-store growth; more than INR 3,000 crore cumulative after new openings, per management.
demand_pricing: QTD revenue growth (April-May 2026) is double-digit; April was flattish and May strong, against a weak May 2025 base affected by Operation Sindoor.

Q4 revenue growth ran about 12% through February before the Middle East conflict pulled March to below -1%; interrupted by the India-Pakistan conflict (May), August floods, December airline disruption and March Middle East conflict.
One-off disruptions cut FY26 revenue by INR 45-52 crore; management says underlying growth would have been 16-17%.
Management says inbound and long-haul travel is recovering (including US); repricing expected to restart as business rebalances. Occupancy described as strong.
Bangalore: about 17,000-18,000 rooms; supply growth about 5-5.5% CAGR, with more than half of future supply concentrated on the airport-Hebbal corridor where SAMHI has no presence.

Median flow-through about 55%, with 55%-plus expected; a Q4 margin drag came from a low-margin outdoor and corporate catering contract at Hyatt Regency Pune (about INR 13-14 crore), which management says ends from May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and May trending, and what is FY27 like-for-like growth after a favourable FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: QTD growth is double-digit: April flattish, May strong against a weak May 2025 base. Management expects YoY growth to stay in double digits through Q1 FY27 despite the Gulf crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST be a permanent margin reduction, and what margins are expected in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: GST impact is permanent in absolute terms, but management expects about 38% group margin, 38%-plus through the year, as pipeline is upscale with few rooms below INR 7,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is there construction delay risk, and will the focus shift to acquisitions or asset recycling?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating and growth teams are separate. Acquisitions stay opportunistic, guided by discount-to-replacement-cost, mid-teens ROCE and no long-lead greenfield. Asset recycling will continue with a few more candidates identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook including new openings, and the interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Same-store growth of 9-10% plus about 3-4% incremental from renovated assets; total about 14% if no crisis. Guided at 10-11% for caution. Interest guided at INR 135-140 crore including rate hardening.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve in Q4 and what is the GST drag and lease accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a low-margin catering contract (INR 13-14 crore revenue) that ends from May. GST drag is about INR 3 crore on a YoY basis per management's arithmetic. Variable lease payments (1.5-2% of revenue) go through P&L; lease-treatment impact on EBITDA margins is about 150-170 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE target, net debt/EBITDA path and capex funding for FY31?
qa_highlights.answer: Current asset pool can deliver 14-15% ROCE. Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise around 2.5x in 12-18 months. Free cash base of about INR 310 crore assumed flat; management assumes no operating leverage and no EBITDA from Navi Mumbai or One Financial District; W Hyderabad and Ingka expected to add INR 400-500 crore EBITDA by FY31.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: March revenue fell below -1% YoY and the effect is still continuing into April; management says it may keep affecting Q1 FY27 absolute numbers.
GST slab change (12% with input credit to 5% without) is permanent; margin dilution persists and sub-INR 7,500 room sales could rise in crisis periods.
Interest-rate hardening: management has assumed 15-20 bps rise; currency weakness is cited as a risk.
Bangalore supply: heavy Outer Ring Road and airport-Hebbal supply could pressure occupancy, which management says has already taken a hit over recent quarters.
Execution risk on pipeline (W Hyderabad end-FY27, Tribute and Westin Bangalore, Navi Mumbai greenfield) and capex of about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
Capital allocation: a Board-level discussion on buybacks or shareholder returns is ongoing with no commitment; asset recycling could extend to minority dilution at asset level (not committed).
Deferred tax income of about INR 330 crore is non-cash; reported PAT is inflated by one-offs and is not a run-rate measure.

We're running really strong capacity utilization across the group.
Notwithstanding the share price or the discount Viraj, we are under a fiduciary obligation to create sharcholder value and allocate capital
But I think the discipline will decide what we do in future.
So I think structurally, the company will secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins.

543984|2026-06.headline: SAMHI Q1 FY27: same-store RevPAR up 9.6% to Rs 5,220 at 79.3% occupancy, while reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on a one-time base and GST impact.
543984|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 7.3% YoY to Rs 308.3 crore reported, or 10.8% on a comparable basis after excluding Rs 9.3 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base. Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

financial_highlights.change: +7.3% YoY reported; +10.8% comparable (ex Rs 9.3 crore one-time income in base)

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 100 crore (per analyst's math, not stated as a figure by management)
financial_highlights.change: down about 4% YoY reported; comparable margin about 12.1%

financial_highlights.value: about 3.2x TTM; about 2.4x for operating assets excluding growth capital

financial_highlights.change: about 300 bps lower than at IPO
unchanged since last upgrade in FY26

segments.name: Upper upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy 78.4% in Q1 with RevPAR growth below mid-scale; management says the raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across all segments.

segments.name: Mid-scale portfolio
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.7% with occupancy at 81.3%, outperforming the broader upscale portfolio in the quarter.

segments.name: RARE India (asset-light leisure)
segments.commentary: 75 hotels, 1,046 rooms across 15 states; management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years, against about Rs 47 crore invested to date.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew about 3.7-4% YoY against room revenue growth of about 14%, attributed to a shift to domestic guests, a Bangalore restaurant renovation and event cancellations moved into July-August.

guidance_outlook: Long-term same-store revenue growth expectation of 9%-11% reiterated; management says the same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5% sits within this range.

Business plan targets revenue from about Rs 1,200 crore to about Rs 3,000 crore and cumulative free cash flow of over Rs 3,000 crore over FY27-FY31 (the call says Rs 2,000 crore once in error, corrected to Rs 3,000 crore).
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from about 40%-41% today to about 60% by FY30.
Net debt/EBITDA of about 2.4x expected by FY28, not by end FY27 as an analyst assumed.
GST margin drag to be lower in H2 than H1; YoY GST impact of about Rs 9 crore to be removed from Q3 onward.
Early July trends described as ahead of Q1 exit, with growth split about evenly between rate and occupancy; management cautioned that one month is not representative.
capex_capacity: Seven new hotels in the committed pipeline total 1,660 rooms, mostly upper upscale and upscale; about 450 rooms are being rebranded from upper midscale to upscale.
W Hyderabad targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 (or calendar 2027); management flagged possible regulatory delays.
Courtyard Pune: back-office and MEP renovation under way; public area and guest room renovation deferred to about April 2027, taking 5-6 months.
Navi Mumbai (100% SAMHI-owned, outside the GIC JV): on-site start targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build; capex to stay small through FY28 and ramp in FY29-FY30.

Uttarakhand (Binsar, Almora) 8-acre estate Itmenaan acquisition for about Rs 12 crore; total leisure capital including RARE around Rs 60 crore, with management expecting leisure to stay near 10% of capital allocation.
demand_pricing: Office absorption in core markets about 11 million sq ft in Q1, against about 58 million sq ft for FY26; Bangalore, Hyderabad and Pune were over 65% of GCC leasing.
Passenger traffic was roughly flat YoY in Q1 after an early-quarter dip tied to geopolitics and Gulf carrier limits; the latter half recovered.
Domestic guests rose to 82% of room nights sold from 78% a year ago; 36% of days had occupancy above 90%.
Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel was idle for about a year and a half after owners moved to Canada and was delisted from RARE; it expects relisting and repricing toward Rs 20,000-40,000 rates in Kumaon. Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate is soft because inbound international travel fell, and it focuses on same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5%, within the 9%-11% long-term range. In July, total revenue growth split about half rate and half occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Gianani (MC Research): Does the annual enabling resolution overhang equity, and how is ROCE on acquisitions in a costlier market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such provisions are common among capital-intensive peers and no debt-equity mix has been decided. It said acquisitions still target operationally distressed assets, even at market peaks, with renovation, rebranding and asset management as the value levers.

qa_highlights.question: Ashish (Leo Capital): What is the Navi Mumbai status, timeline and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy issues are resolved, with statutory approvals expected in the next few months and design work to be presented next quarter. On-site start is targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build, capex small through FY28, and main spend in FY29-FY30.

risks_watch: Rate softness from lower international inbound mix: rate growth is expected to recover only in H2 FY27, and July's split is one month of data.

EBITDA trajectory: Q1 reported EBITDA was down about 4% YoY; the one-time Rs 9 crore base item and about Rs 9.2 crore GST drag should fall out from Q2 and Q3, but management has not guided EBITDA figures.
Leverage path: management says about 2.4x net debt/EBITDA is reached by FY28, not end-FY27, and disputes an analyst's assumption of 2.5x by year-end.
Equity dilution overhang from the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution, which management says will be taken annually; no use or debt-equity mix defined.
Project execution: W Hyderabad could slip past 2H FY28 due to regulatory approvals; Courtyard Pune renovation timeline depends on April 2027 start; Navi Mumbai on-site start in April 2027.
RARE execution: Marriott Outdoor Collection sign-ups (about 40 of 75 hotels) and RARE's shift to fee income with limited disclosure of RARE RevPAR.
key_quotes: Same-store RevPAR grew 9.6% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 5,220, with portfolio occupancy at 79.3%, which was up from 74.2% in the year-ago quarter.
Put simply, every new upscale key we now add brings in more revenue per key and a better margin than the midscale it often replaces or sits alongside.
We didn't say 2.5x by end of FY 2027. We think we will get there by FY 2028, both because of EBITDA.
Navi Mumbai, we were originally planning to be on-site, hit the ground by end of this fiscal year.

543985|2026-03.headline: Zaggle FY26 standalone revenue rose about 42% to INR1,853 crores, but FY27 standalone growth guidance slows to 25-30% as DICE moves to an asset purchase.
543985|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results, with standalone revenue of about INR1,853 crores (up 42%) and PAT of about INR133 crores (up 52%). Management withheld EBITDA guidance until integration completes, and cash flow is now the top priority, with operating cash flow about minus INR6 crores in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR34 crores in FY25 to about INR74 crores in FY26 (up 118%). EBITDA rose from about INR5.4 crores to about INR18 crores and PAT from about INR1.6 crores to INR11 crores, driven by UPI volumes and new bank partners.

segments.name: GreenEdge
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR36.5 crores in FY25 to about INR103.7 crores in FY26 (up about 184%). EBITDA rose from about INR3.4 crores to about INR11 crores and PAT from INR2.1 crores to about INR8.1 crores. Standalone revenue growth of 40-50% is projected for FY27.

segments.name: Zagg.money (formerly Rio.Money)

segments.name: TaxSpanner (to be rebranded Z.tax)

segments.name: DICE (asset purchase)
segments.commentary: Acquired as a spend management suite, IP and enterprise contracts for about INR68 crores excluding GST, against an original INR123 crores share-purchase valuation. DICE was loss-making in FY25 and likely in FY26; FY25 revenue was about INR10 crores, with FY26 described as significantly higher. Around 100-plus team members join.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at about 25-30%; consolidated growth at about 40%.
EBITDA guidance deferred to 'the next few months' until DICE integration completes, since DICE costs now sit on the standalone P&L.
Medium-term guidance of 14-15% over five years is maintained, with margin ramp of roughly 1 percentage point a year expected to be temporarily disrupted.
Five-year goal of INR500 crores revenue and INR65 crores EBITDA reiterated.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in coming quarters; cash flow named the top priority, followed by revenue growth and margin expansion.
US operations now targeted by fiscal year-end (FY27), pushed back from June 2026; UAE expansion on hold pending regional peace.
Propel margin expected to return to about 5.5% in coming years.
Employee and other costs likely to rise in the next quarter as DICE staff are onboarded.

Management says the 2026 credit card business is growing faster than initial expectations, with card acquisition the lead indicator before spend-led revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capitalised development costs nearly doubled, and does free cash flow better reflect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only new product development is capitalised, not maintenance, and it will track operating and free cash flow more closely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Propel margins fall from about 10% to 4% YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the full-year margin of about 6% and said it is exiting redemption-heavy Propel models that absorb cash, sacrificing some margin; it expects about 5.5% in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 standalone growth guided at 25-30% after 42% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the much larger base (about 5-6x since IPO) and a deliberate cash-flow focus that may slow Propel Points growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR40 crores to INR129 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split receivables by business, said the net receivable position was negative about INR33-34 crores at end-September and is now close to breakeven, and cited trade receivables as one cash lever.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated operating cash flow about minus INR52 crores versus about minus INR6 crores standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiaries are nascent businesses recently acquired, with investments made and efficiency gains to come.

qa_highlights.question: Does DICE dilute the EBITDA run rate and the 11-12% margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DICE's impact is no worse than originally envisaged, with costs now on standalone P&L; it was loss-making and EBITDA guidance will follow integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is Propel worth keeping given its low net revenue and working-capital use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Propel is a feeder for cross-sell and stickiness, about 90% of spend sits in program fees, and cash and ROCE optimisation is under way.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow remains negative (about minus INR6 crores standalone; about minus INR52 crores consolidated) and receivables have risen sharply.
DICE integration may lift employee and other costs in the next quarter, with EBITDA guidance still pending.
Propel margin compression and cutbacks in cashback and redemption models could slow growth and affect customer retention.

CFO role is interim after Aditya Kumar Grandhi's departure; a permanent CFO is expected soon.

543985|2026-06.headline: Zaggle Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR423 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% from 10.1% on DICE costs and expensed capitalisation.
543985|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to about INR423 crore, while stand-alone revenue grew 18% to about INR390 crore against a soft seasonal Q1. Adjusted EBITDA was about INR34.7 crore (8.2% margin vs 10.1% a year ago), pressured by DICE integration and relocation costs (about INR3 crore in the last two months of the quarter, before any DICE revenue), one-time expenses, a moderation of capitalisation, annual increments and Zagg.Money costs. Management said DICE revenue starts from July 1 (Q2 FY27), reiterated the 40% consolidated growth guidance and a 25% stand-alone target, and pivoted the stated focus to cash flow and calibrated capitalisation. Analysts pressed on the sharp growth slowdown, margin volatility and the lack of explicit EBITDA guidance.

segments.name: Save and Zoyer (stand-alone SaaS and programs)
segments.commentary: Post new income tax regime, wallet additions and per-user wallet increases for new and existing corporates; 73% of new users came from existing corporates. Large retail chain Zoyer rollout: about 2,000 of roughly 19,000 stores onboarded.

segments.name: Propel
segments.commentary: Consolidated Propel margin 7.1%, stand-alone about 5%, including spillover of overriding commissions realised in Q1. Signed Saint Gobain, Supreme Pipes and Phoenix India during the quarter.

segments.name: Fleet (CDG)
segments.commentary: Transactions up 43% YoY and transaction value up 5.8% YoY; annualised spend run-rate about INR100 crore. First contract with an OMC (HPCL, 5-year aggregator agreement for DT Plus).

segments.name: Zagg.Money (Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: Annualised new card acquisition run-rate raised to about 84,000 from 36,000 a quarter earlier; management cited about INR2.5 crore loss on the business. Co-brand launches with PNB and AU Small Finance Bank.

segments.commentary: Acquired as asset purchase for about INR68 crore excl. GST (from INR123 crore initial valuation). About 100 staff relocated from Pune to Hyderabad; revenue from novated contracts only from Q2 FY27. FY26 DICE revenue about INR12 crore; FY27 target INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (rebranding to Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR80 lakh, +65% YoY; B2B business expected to grow about 120%. Management says on track to breakeven this financial year.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: About INR8 crore invested in Unobanc (moneyHOP), which holds an RBI Authorised Dealer Category-II licence for cross-border payments and forex cards.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of about 40% for FY27 reiterated; stand-alone growth target about 25% retained, despite Q1 at 18%.
No explicit EBITDA margin guidance; management said it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 14-15% framed over 5-7 years.
