qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth slowed sharply from the 40-50% run-rate, and is the 40% consolidated guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is about 18% of the full year and growth is expected to rise; SaaS revenue from DICE only starts in Q2 while costs were incurred in Q1. Management moved some high working-capital banks' customers to other banks to prioritise cash flow, which slows program fees. Management said it is not moving away from the 40% consolidated guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give EBITDA margin guidance, and how should margins trend from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin is about 8.2% and it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. About INR3 crore of DICE cost came in over the last two months of Q1 with no revenue, since revenue starts July 1.

qa_highlights.question: What were the expensed items that were previously capitalised, and why are they only partly expensed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no selective capitalisation; the company is moving toward expensing more over time, subject to auditor agreement. One immediate client-required product cost about INR6 crore was fully expensed in Q1, and some infra and product development costs are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Has DICE payment-rail integration been completed and will payments revenue come from DICE from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority of integration is done; the last part is due by August 31 or at latest September 10. Management said payments-related DICE revenue from Q3 is certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is revenue per customer, and what is the program fee growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue per customer is about INR10.6 lakh (INR423 crore over about 4,000 customers). Management called the roughly 10% program fee growth 'by design' and said it expects improvement in coming months, with cash flow and calibrated capitalisation prioritised over the program fee number.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 13-15% EBITDA margin target still stand, and when will margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins have been in the 9-10% range for the last eight quarters and the 14-15% target is a 5-7 year aspiration. Cash flow turnaround to positive would take about 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: When will AI become a meaningful revenue driver, and what is the DICE revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal AI use helped cut about 12.5% of the FY26 cost base and reduced feature launch timelines by up to 50%. DICE FY26 revenue was about INR12 crore; FY27 target is INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

543988|2026-03.headline: Nuvama FY26 operating PAT crossed INR1,000 crore; Q4 operating PAT up 5% YoY to INR269 crore, with wealth and asset services driving growth.

Capital markets (IB and IE) softened, with QIP volumes down and ECM subdued in Q4. Q4 firm revenue was about INR825 crore (+7% YoY; +13% excluding IE and IB), and firm ROE was 28%. qa_highlights.question: Is the asset services yield at risk as rates fall, and what drove the higher cash share?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% wealth productivity gain from AI or from mix, and how do clients per RM evolve?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for transactional revenue in FY27 and the insurance commission trend?

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income ratios evolve in Wealth?

Q4 was weak: revenue from operations fell 14% YoY to INR 1,890 mn and EBITDA fell 46% to INR 126 mn, driven by West Asia conflict cancellations and deferrals of MICE and international group bookings into FY27. Management said Q1 FY27 run rates are about 20% above Q4 and expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger, while reiterating a medium-term 20% RLSC and 30% adjusted EBITDA CAGR.

segments.commentary: FY26 gross bookings INR 16,578 mn, up 27%; room nights 1,936,000, up 16%; gross booking margin INR 1,534 mn, up 37%, with margin rising from 8.60% to 9.25%. Standalone hotel margin rose from 7.7% to nearly 9%, and standalone hotels grew about 32% YoY.

Higher airfares also raised costs on Europe MICE. Q1 FY27 run rate is about 20% above Q4, with growth in Southeast Asia and domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to IT services in B2E and AI risk?
qa_highlights.answer: IT services were about 10-11% of B2E business, and about 7% of total B2E including Globe and MICE. The share was about 20% at IPO in FY24.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the air discount rising and what is the take-rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said enterprise customers spend about 50% more per ticket than B2C, so airlines pay better realisation on enterprise. Net take rate is improving. Discount-to-gross-take was about 61% in FY23-24 and about 47-48% in FY25-26.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 tracking better than Q1 FY26, and is the 20% growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20-30 model is a 2-3 year CAGR view, not hard guidance. Q1 will be muted, with recovery expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Hotel realisation and discount trends?

qa_highlights.question: MICE competition from listed or DRHP-filed MICE companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organised MICE is about 10% of a roughly INR 35,000 crore market, and that Yatra is about the second-largest organised player. It cited exception handling and DMC partnerships as moats. MICE is 10-15% of installed base revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why run B2C at all, and will B2C be split out?

qa_highlights.question: Corporate credit card initiative and its effect on take rate and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Product expected within a quarter or two. Airline partnerships are needed to offset card fees, or the net take rate and numerator would suffer. Hotel virtual card is already live.

qa_highlights.question: Holding company (THCL) restructuring status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Cayman and Cyprus layer collapse is still in progress across India, Cyprus, Singapore and Cayman. THCL sold about 1.8% in Feb 26 to fund legal costs, and management does not expect further sales.

543992|2026-06.headline: Yatra Q1 FY27 gross bookings rose 17% to INR21,007 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 39% to INR151 million on MICE disruption and Kanoo build-out costs.
543992|2026-06.overview: Gross bookings grew about 17% YoY to INR21,007 million and gross margin rose 6.1% to INR1,227 million, while revenue from operations fell 10.4% to INR1,879 million as MICE top line dropped about INR300 million. Adjusted EBITDA declined 39.4% to INR151 million (12.29% of gross margin) and PAT was INR3.4 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to temporary MICE disruption, air margin pressure from delayed Middle East airline PLB deals, and pre-revenue people and platform costs for the Kanoo partnership. No FY27 guidance was issued; management said it expects to provide guidance next quarter.

543994|2026-09.headline: JSW Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell 11% to INR328 crore on forex losses and Fujairah's nil contribution.
543994|2026-09.overview: Consolidated operating revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore and operating EBITDA rose 11% to INR674 crore in Q2 FY27. Port EBITDA was flat at INR594 crore, with margin compressing to 49.4% from 53.1%, as Fujairah contributed nothing and coal terminals diluted mix. Logistics EBITDA more than tripled to INR81 crore, with the rail rake fleet raised to 78 from 42. PBT fell to INR431 crore from INR463 crore on unrealised forex losses and higher depreciation, and PAT fell to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Management held the FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore, while revising logistics EBITDA margin guidance up to 28% from 24%.

rows.why: Jatadhar cargo handling starts end-March or April 2027 with Cape-size in Q3 FY28, and Jaigarh LPG berth operations by March 2027, but these are port capacity starts rather than discrete product launches.

rows.label: Fujairah restart in early November 2026
rows.why: Eight tanks are under FOIS commissioning with final permission expected around 29 October, but storage demand has fallen sharply, so Fujairah volumes restart is uncertain versus ~INR250 crore FY26 EBITDA.

rows.label: Interest income on QIP proceeds
rows.why: About INR6,400 crore net QIP proceeds held in mutual funds and FDs generate other income that persists until drawn for capex, against cash of INR1,693 crore; this supports PBT offsetting higher depreciation (INR175 crore vs INR149 crore) and finance cost (INR108 crore vs INR99 crore).

rows.label: Keni environment clearance
rows.why: Keni is awaiting environment clearance, expected in about 3-4 months, which may delay that project; Oman bids are due mid-November 2026 with work from Q4 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on the held INR2,950-3,000 crore consolidated EBITDA target and the rake ramp to 110, but cautious on Fujairah and deferred FY28 logistics margins to Q3 or Q4 results; analysts pushed on rake margin and revenue scaling, Fujairah restart and demand, and the other income jump.

543996|2026-03.headline: Updater Services FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR2,960 crores, but adjusted EBITDA margin was 5.9% after the Avon provisioning hit; no formal FY27 guidance given.
543996|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY to INR750 crores and EBITDA was INR49 crores (6.6% margin), with PAT of INR27 crores. For FY26, IFM grew 10% to INR1,995 crores and BSS grew 1% to INR966 crores, while adjusted EBITDA was INR176 crores after absorbing the Avon receivables provision of about INR23 crores. Management said standalone UDS PAT fell on front-loaded IFM costs, provisions, lower interest income and a one-time wage-code charge, and framed FY27 as a clean year. Management declined formal FY27 guidance and said acquisition talks are still live but not assured.

financial_highlights.change: +3% YoY (vs INR726 crores in Q4 FY25)

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 adjusted EBITDA (after Avon one-time hit)

financial_highlights.value: INR966 crores, EBITDA margin 8.8% (adjusted INR85 crores EBITDA per Amitabh, ~9%)

segments.name: IFM
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,995 crores (+10% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.5%; Global Flight Handling EBITDA rose to 6% from 3%, Fusion margin ~6% to ~8%, Washroom Hygiene margin steady at 37-38%. Management says IFM growth is ahead of peers.

segments.name: BSS - Denave
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR590 crores (+11% YoY), EBITDA INR26 crores (~4.5% margin); Q4 revenue +15% and EBITDA +~70% with margin 5.5%+. Added 49 new logos; new and existing enterprise business grew 21%.

segments.name: BSS - Athena
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR116.8 crores vs INR136 crores in FY25; EBITDA INR23-24 crores vs INR35 crores, margin ~20-21%. BFSI concentration fell to 81% from 86%; 4 new logos added, no new customer losses in FY26.

segments.name: BSS - Matrix
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR128.6 crores; EBGC (background verification) revenue fell 11% on IT/ITES hiring softness, Audit & Assurance grew 5.8%. EBITDA INR14.9-15 crores, margin ~12%.

segments.name: Avon
segments.commentary: Avon took about INR23 crores of provisions (INR3 crores in Q2, balance in Q3) on logistics and freight brokerage receivables, fully provided; legal action underway. Core mail room and integrated support business grew 9%. Avon Transport has been shut.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance; management expects to grow ahead of the Indian industry (industry grew under 6% in FY26).
Management expects a clean FY27 start, with the one-time wage-code, front-loaded cost and provisioning items not repeating.
Visibility on FY27 revenue of 85-90% from existing contracts, per management.
Management said it hopes to indicate the FY27 year-end direction on the Q1 FY27 call.
Early April-May signs are encouraging, and several large IFM logos are signed or pending approval.
capex_capacity: All 23 Global Flight Handling airports are now operational and generating revenue.
Denave is scaling AI-led digital workforce pilots, which were run with 4 customers in FY26, and plans to scale them meaningfully in FY27.
Athena is in POC stages on agentic AI with 3-4 customers and won 2 Agentic AI contracts recently.
Management said it will invest in technology and AI, and talent, from its cash pool.
Shared services across finance, procurement and payroll are planned to drive cost optimisation.
demand_pricing: IFM: 30 new logos added in FY26 across industrial, technology and commercial sectors, with higher wallet share from existing clients.
Management cites demand tailwinds from the new labour codes (effective November 2025), GCC growth and outcome-linked contracts.
Matrix A&A won 12 large clients across FMCG, retail, quick commerce and manufacturing; one large customer reduced spend.
EBGC demand is soft due to IT and ITES hiring and some softness in BFSI hiring.
Athena: losses of 2 major customers and a downsizing by another in FY25 and earlier drove the revenue decline; diversifying into healthcare, retail and real estate.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~INR450 crore cash pile be deployed, including acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisitions remain the primary use, alongside organic investment in technology and talent and shareholder rewards. The Board will decide the split, and some form of reward is expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early recovery at Athena, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Major customer losses have stopped; EBITDA margin has stabilised at about 19-20%. Key priorities are customer diversification and scaling agentic AI, which is at POC stage with 3-4 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS revenue fall sharply and margins rise, and what drove IFM's PAT decline and the other opex drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Athena revenue fell about INR25 crores and Avon Transport (INR40 crores last year) was shut. Denave grew 11%, Global 30%, Avon Solutions 11%, and Matrix was flat. Standalone UDS PAT fell about INR19 crores: roughly INR12-13 crores from front-loaded costs and ECL/EPC provisions, INR4 crores from wage-code liabilities, and the rest from lower interest income, after a INR9 crore non-operating gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is returns on capital low despite revenue growth, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IFM growth is ahead of peers (IFM +10%, group +7%). It attributed the margin drop to one-time items that will not repeat and said interest income is a capital-allocation outcome that will rise with treasury management.

qa_highlights.question: Why no buyback given the net cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash is earmarked for organic growth, acquisitions and shareholder rewards, with the format (buyback or dividend) to be a Board decision and some reward expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 revenue is already visible, and what is the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Visibility is 85-90% from existing contracts. Management declined formal guidance and expects to give an indication on the Q1 FY27 call.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the pending acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The deal is still on; due diligence is almost closed, but other negotiating items remain and completion cannot be guaranteed. Management is cautiously hopeful.

risks_watch: Avon receivables recovery: about INR23 crores fully provided, with legal action underway; any recovery would be upside.
IFM margin: segment EBITDA margin was 4.4% in Q4 and 4.5% for FY26; front-loaded contract costs need to unwind as management expects.
Athena revenue continues to shrink, and the agentic AI POCs have not yet converted to scaled revenue.
EBGC/Matrix is exposed to IT, ITES and BFSI hiring softness.
Acquisition outcome is uncertain, and cash deployment (M&A vs buyback vs dividend) is undecided.
Management reported a decline in standalone PAT in FY26 and is expecting a clean FY27, which should be verified against Q1 FY27 results.

Management was candid on the Avon provisions and the standalone PAT decline, and attributed them to one-time items.
key_quotes: We're taking all necessary steps, including legal action to recover these amounts.
Being prudent and conservative, we have already fully provided for the entire INR23 crores.
I would avoid a formal guidance in terms of where we are going to go.
So it is still on. The conversations have taken longer than what we had envisaged.

rows.why: Denave plans to scale AI-led digital workforce pilots (run with 4 customers in FY26) meaningfully in FY27, and Athena has 2 recent Agentic AI contracts with 3-4 POCs.

rows.why: About INR450 crores of cash; management expects some form of shareholder reward this year (buyback or dividend, Board to decide), while acquisition talks are live but completion not guaranteed.

rows.label: Large IFM logos signed or pending approval
rows.why: Management says several large IFM logos are signed or pending approval and early April-May signs are encouraging, though no order values were given.

rows.label: Avon receivables recovery
rows.why: About INR23 crores fully provided on logistics and freight brokerage receivables with legal action underway; any recovery would be upside, but timing is unclear.

tone.note: Management was confident on IFM growth, cash generation and FY27 visibility of 85-90%, but cautious on numbers, declining formal guidance and deferring to Q1 FY27; analysts pushed on the standalone PAT decline, low returns on capital, lack of buyback and the Athena and EBGC drags.

543996|2026-06.headline: Updater Services Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR42 crore (5.5% margin) and PAT of INR30.3 crore.
543996|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with IFM up 11% to INR525 crore and BSS up 7% to INR253 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was INR42 crore at a 5.5% margin, with IFM at 4.5% (about INR24 crore) and BSS at 7.5% (about INR19 crore). Management declared an interim dividend of INR1 per share, about INR7 crore of cash outflow, and said it remains a net cash company. Management gave no formal guidance and pointed to Q1 as the indicator.

financial_highlights.change: +9% YoY vs INR700 crore in Q1 FY26
IFM PAT INR20.7 crore vs INR19.9 crore a year ago

segments.name: IFM (Integrated Facility Management, incl. Global and Avon)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 crore, up 11% YoY, with 6 new significant logos added. EBITDA about INR24 crore at 4.5% margin, with management noting this is stable and it does not expect further decline. Global reported its highest-ever EBITDA margin of 9% (vs 5% last year), and all 23 airports are operational. Avon core mailroom revenue grew 10% YoY after the transport business was fully shut off.

segments.name: BSS: Denave (sales enablement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR161 crore, up 18% YoY, with EBITDA INR7 crore at 4.3% margin. Margin pressure came from a mix shift toward low-margin field marketing and budget timing at one large customer.

segments.name: BSS: Athena (BFSI customer engagement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28 crore with EBITDA INR5 crore, an 18% margin. Won 2 new clients that started in July on 2-year tenures, and started its first agentic AI engagement in May-June.

segments.name: BSS: Matrix (Audit & Assurance and EBGC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2% YoY and was flat QoQ. EBITDA rose about 76%, and margin improved to 13.1% from 7.6% (EBITDA INR4.2 crore vs INR2.4 crore). EBGC revenue grew 9% YoY to INR12.5 crore with gross margin about 21%. Audit & Assurance revenue fell about 2% as large audits slipped from May into June and July.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management said Q1 numbers can serve as an indicator.
Management expects IFM and BSS each to grow low double digits, roughly 9-12%, so the 67:33 IFM:BSS mix should hold.
Matrix Audit & Assurance results are expected in H2 FY27 as deferred audits land.
EBGC volumes and margins are expected to be sustainable through this year.
Cash of upwards of INR300 crore to be deployed across inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment and shareholder returns.
capex_capacity: Global: all 23 airports operational and generating revenue; expanding into training and aviation support services, including security training and regulatory certification.
Athena: another agentic AI project has customer approval and is expected to go live in August 2026.
Matrix: a dedicated sales team was built for Audit & Assurance to target large multinational audits and food and automobile sectors.
Acquisition: a pending deal is on hold over valuation differences; management said it is also reviewing a wider pipeline.
Labour: recruitment teams in Eastern and Northeast India redeploy workers to labour-short states such as Gujarat, parts of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR.
demand_pricing: IFM demand: strong commercial real estate, GCC expansion and enterprise outsourcing; management sees clients favouring single strategic partners. Management says its GCC exposure is limited (low commercial, no residential).
BSS demand: clients are prioritising projects with faster ROI and sales productivity; spending is selective in some global markets.
EBGC: volumes are recovering after subdued banking and BPO hiring; the company describes margins as volume-driven with a flat cost base.
Contracts are largely pass-through, and labour shortages in several states did not visibly hit Q1 results.
Seasonality: Q1 is seasonally weak for catering; Q2 and Q3 are festive peaks for consumer-linked IFM and BSS work.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Matrix margin improvement sustainable, and has IFM margin moderation from headcount additions ended?
qa_highlights.answer: EBGC revenue went from INR11.4 crore (Q1 FY26) to INR11.7 crore (Q4 FY26) to INR12.5 crore (Q1 FY27), and gross margin from about 12% to 21%. Management says cost structure is flat, so volume drives margin, and it expects this to hold. IFM EBITDA was INR23.6 crore vs INR23.1 crore YoY, with some cost and contract front-loading.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and are buybacks planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is above INR300 crore across three buckets: inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment, and shareholder rewards. The INR1 interim dividend is the first step. There is no buyback proposal before the Board, though management did not rule one out.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IFM:BSS mix change over 2-3 years, and can agentic AI matter for Athena?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 67:33 mix to hold, since both segments can grow 9-12%. Agentic AI is in use for outbound lead qualification and inbound repetitive queries. Management said it does not see wholesale replacement of human agents in BFSI near term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS margin fall from 11.5% in Q4 to 7.5% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a Q4 FY26 Avon restatement that added revenue to last year's Q4. Excluding it, Q4 BSS EBITDA was INR19.1 crore vs INR18.9 crore in Q1, so margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the rise in other expenses and the tax-expense swing quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose because of restructuring costs and transport provisions taken in FY26. Tax fell on a manpower-linked tax benefit in a couple of group entities, and the mix is also a factor because Matrix gets no such benefit. Management said the full-year effective tax rate is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the SIS share purchases and the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no discussion with SIS beyond public knowledge; it reads the purchases as a treasury investment. The promoter family holds 59.1%. The acquisition is on hold over valuation.

risks_watch: Matrix EBGC margin (gross margin about 21%) rests on volume growth and flat cost base; hiring in banking and BPO is still subdued and management could not give a timeline for recovery.
Audit & Assurance timing: large audits slipped from May into June and July, and management expects these results only in H2 FY27; watch whether they land.
Labour shortages in Gujarat, parts of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR; management says contracts are pass-through but the shortage is real and customer cost pressure could follow.
Athena agentic AI: approval cycles run about 2-3 months, and management does not see wholesale replacement of BFSI agents near term; watch conversion of the August go-live into revenue.
Denave margin pressure from field marketing mix and one large customer's budget timing; the 4.3% margin is below the BSS segment average and management has not quantified recovery.
Pending acquisition is on hold over valuation; SIS share purchases continue with no stated intent, and a buyback is not proposed but not ruled out.
key_quotes: We normally don't give formal guidance. So I think we will continue with that.
At this margin level, we do believe that we will not decline any further.
Right now, there is no proposal to buy back shares on -- in front of the board, and there is not a discussion on it.
We are not reading too much into it. There is no deal on the table.
543996|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on IFM margin stability, Global (9% EBITDA margin) and Matrix EBGC recovery, but cautious and non-committal on guidance (no formal guidance, Q1 as the only indicator). Evasive on the SIS share purchases and on whether a buyback is coming, and deflected some tax and expense questions to the CFO's technical explanation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: IFM EBITDA margin held at about 4.5% (INR24 crore vs INR23.1 crore YoY) and management says it does not expect further decline; BSS margin rose to 7.5% from 6.9%, and Matrix margin improved to 13.1% from 7.6% on EBGC gross margin of about 21% (from about 12%), but Denave is at 4.3% and no group-level margin expansion was guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Global's 23 airports are already operational and no new plant, line or branch was announced; the call gave no capacity timeline beyond Athena's August go-live, which is a software project, not capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects IFM and BSS each to grow roughly 9-12% (midpoint about 10.5%), backed by Q1 revenue growth of 11% in IFM (INR525 crore) and 7% in BSS (INR253 crore), 6 new IFM logos and 2 new Athena clients starting July.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed, so there is no utilisation figure to support a capex call; cash above INR300 crore is earmarked for inorganic growth, brownfield investment and shareholder returns with no specific project named.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given and management pointed only to Q1 as the indicator; the 9-12% growth view is an expectation, not a raised target, and the Audit & Assurance deferral and Denave margin pressure cut against an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Matrix Audit & Assurance revenue fell about 2% as large audits slipped from May into June and July, and the recovery is only expected in H2 FY27; labour shortages in Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR could pressure customer costs even though Q1 was not visibly hit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Athena's second agentic AI project has customer approval and is expected to go live in August 2026, after the first engagement started in May-June; Global is also expanding into training and aviation support services with no date given.

rows.label: Athena new BFSI clients and agentic AI go-live
rows.why: 2 new Athena clients started in July on 2-year tenures and a second agentic AI project with customer approval goes live in August 2026, though approval cycles run 2-3 months and BFSI replacement of agents is not expected near term.

rows.label: Buyback or inorganic deal from cash above INR300 crore
rows.why: Cash above INR300 crore is earmarked for inorganic, brownfield and shareholder returns, with no buyback before the Board but not ruled out, and the pending acquisition is on hold over valuation.

rows.label: Matrix Audit & Assurance deferred audits landing
rows.why: Large audits slipped from May into June and July, and management expects these results in H2 FY27, which would recover the about 2% revenue decline in Audit & Assurance.

tone.note: Management was confident on IFM margin stability, Global's 9% EBITDA margin and the Matrix EBGC recovery, but cautious on guidance and evasive on the SIS share purchases and buyback; analysts pushed on margin moderation, the BSS margin drop from Q4, tax swings and cash deployment.

544004|2026-03.headline: IRM Energy FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 1,066.66 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR 112.25 crore; management guides FY27 volume above 250 MMSCM.
544004|2026-03.overview: FY26 volume reached 223.67 MMSCM (+9% YoY), with PAT of INR 56.89 crore (+21% YoY, standalone) and CNG stations crossing 150 (up from 111). Q4 PBT was about INR 17.7 crore against INR 22 crore in Q3, as management attributed INR 4.2 crore of one-time items (JV receivable provision INR 1.34 crore and bank charges INR 2.86 crore) to the decline and said both would be reversed or resolved in Q1 FY27. Gas sourcing was disrupted after the Gulf conflict, with Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 55-65% of contracts before recovering to 80%. Management guided to gross margin and per-SCM EBITDA improvement of 10-15% and double-digit volume growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Total debt incl. lease liability (end FY26)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 22 crore in Q3 FY26 per analyst
guided INR 5.3-5.5 per SCM next year

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at 61% of FY26 operational revenue; station network reached 150 (from 111, +26% YoY) with 39 added in FY26 and 36 targeted in FY27. About 40% of CNG volume is sourced from APM/NWG gas, with HPHT gas for the balance; management says 4% of CNG was spot purchase in FY26.

segments.name: PNG Domestic
segments.commentary: Added 83,262 domestic connections in FY26; Diu and Gir Somnath has crossed 10,000 domestic PNG connections.

segments.name: PNG Commercial and Industrial
segments.commentary: Added 496 commercial and 223 industrial connections in FY26. Industrial volume is affected by the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order and gas cuts; management expects industrial growth of 23-24% in FY27 if the order is implemented.

segments.name: GA-wise: Banaskantha (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue and 47% of volume, with about INR 420 crore invested; CNG-centric with higher margins.

segments.name: GA-wise: Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab)
segments.commentary: About 36% of FY26 revenue (mainly industrial PNG) and 39% of volume, with about INR 200 crore invested.

segments.name: GA-wise: Namakkal and Trichy (Tamil Nadu)
segments.commentary: About INR 257 crore gross block invested to date; FY27 capex planned at INR 150-180 crore. Management expects around 90% CNG volume mix initially, moving toward 70:20 CNG to PNG over one to two years. 71 TNSTC PNG buses running with 50 more due in May 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected at 30%+ over FY26 in management's words, with volume crossing 250 MMSCM 'or maybe much more'; the CEO also said 'double-digit' growth, and the CFO said 14-15% was not out of line.
EBITDA per SCM to improve 10-15% in FY27 from current levels of more than INR 5 per SCM; CFO guided to INR 5.3-5.5 per SCM.
Gross margin and EBITDA margin expected to be maintained in the 25-26% gross margin range, subject to how the Gulf situation unfolds.
Peak debt for FY27 expected at INR 70-80 crore, against about INR 49 crore of term loans at end March 2026 and a INR 45 crore sanctioned term loan.
Namakkal and Trichy capex funded from IPO proceeds (about INR 194 crore available at end March 2026); other GAs funded from internal accruals plus the term loan.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 184.35 crore, including INR 81.33 crore in Q4 FY26 alone.
Cumulative investment to date: Banaskantha about INR 420 crore, Fatehgarh Sahib about INR 200 crore, Namakkal and Trichy INR 257 crore gross block.
FY27 target: 36 new CNG stations (39 added in FY26); Namakkal and Trichy capex of INR 150-180 crore.
Network of 6,695 inch-km pipeline as of FY26; about 35% of the cascade fleet is Type 3 cylinders. Trichy bus stand CNG station planned.
First LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram (Namakkal and Trichy GA).
demand_pricing: Gas cost pressure from APM ceiling rising to USD 7/MMBTU (from USD 6.75) and higher NWG-linked prices; management says the increase was passed through to CNG, industrial and commercial customers from April.
HPHT gas price via IGX reduced from USD 9.72 to USD 8.92 per MMBTU, offsetting some cost pressure.
CNG sales for April 2026 were in line with budget after the price pass-through, per management.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 80%, then 65% and 55% of contracted quantity during the Gulf disruption, now restored to 80%; demand destruction is occurring in industrial.

Namakkal and Trichy: CNG demand nearly doubled YoY after the OMC CNG model rollout; 92-95% of new three-wheeler sales are CNG; CNG share of passenger vehicle additions above 15% in that GA (vs over 40% in Banaskantha).
Management says EV penetration in its GAs is negligible; CNG auto and taxi demand continues to grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given the Gulf crisis and sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin of 25-26% has risen YoY; management expects margins to hold in that range, depending on how the situation unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall from Q3 to Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision (Ni Hon Cylinders) and a INR 2.86 crore bank charge, both expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. The analyst noted PBT of about INR 17.7 crore in Q4 vs INR 22 crore in Q3, still a gap after adding back these items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the NGT order for Fatehgarh Sahib be implemented?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not pushing for immediate enforcement given demand destruction and gas cuts; it will press PPCB and CPCB once supply stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 volume and EBITDA per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth expected above 30% (to above 250 MMSCM); EBITDA per SCM to rise 10-15% from current levels of more than INR 5.

qa_highlights.question: How much CNG is spot-sourced?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 4% of CNG volume was spot purchase in FY26; about 40% comes from APM/NWG gas, and the rest from long-term contracts and HPHT bids.

qa_highlights.question: What funds the Namakkal and Trichy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: IPO proceeds of about INR 194 crore at end March 2026; other GAs are funded through internal accruals and a term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury income and cash flow treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income from liquid and overnight funds was about INR 68 lakh in Q4 FY26, per management, versus about INR 2 crore cited by the analyst as the quarter figure.

risks_watch: Gas sourcing: APM ceiling increase, NWG price rise and Gulf supply disruption could pressure margins if pass-through slows; management says CNG and domestic are insulated.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial volumes: NGT-linked restrictions, demand destruction and gas cuts; implementation timing is uncertain.
Q1 FY27 must show reversal of the INR 1.34 crore JV provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge, as management stated.
Execution of 36 CNG station additions and INR 150-180 crore Namakkal and Trichy capex; the new Tamil Nadu government's policy stance was flagged as a source of difficulty.
Employee cost rise (headcount from 214 to 256) and a INR 60 lakh labour code provision; license fee at 2% of net revenue.
Management declined to give firm numeric guidance, citing an evolving situation; several outlook figures were given as ranges and 'maybe' targets.

Management was defensive when questioned on the Q4 profit decline, attributing it to one-time items, and gave a hedged, range-based outlook.

rows.label: Peak debt capped at INR 70-80 crore in FY27

rows.why: Management said the INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge would be reversed or resolved in Q1 FY27, which would lift the INR 17.7 crore Q4 PBT against INR 22 crore in Q3.

rows.label: Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order implementation

544004|2026-06.headline: IRM Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 326 crore, with EBITDA ex-other income up 139% YoY to INR 62 crore and PAT of INR 34 crore.

Margin expansion was attributed to sourcing (HPHT and long-term contracts priced below spot), price realisations, and cost control, with management stating there were no one-time items. 544008|2026-03.headline: Max Estates FY26 presales hit INR5,305 crore, second straight year above INR5,000 crore, with Q4 bookings of INR3,300 crore the strongest quarter ever.

544021|2026-06.headline: Protean Q1FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR251 crore, but EBITDA fell 38% to INR28 crore (10% margin) on an INR18 crore upfront RFP cost.
544021|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 19% YoY to INR251 crore, driven by core businesses and new initiatives. EBITDA fell to INR28 crore from INR45 crore, with margin at 10% versus 18.7% a year ago, mainly due to about INR18 crore of upfront implementation costs on RFP mandates plus geopolitical-driven hardware and technology price inflation. Management says normalised EBITDA would have been INR46 crore (17.2%). PAT was INR6 crore (2.2% margin), and the company remains debt-free with over INR800 crore in cash and marketable securities. This was the first earnings call for new MD and CEO Ajay Rajan, who set out a shift from volume-led growth to solution-led, higher-margin DPI offerings.

544022|2026-03.headline: ASK Automotive Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 35.3% YoY, EBITDA Rs 140 Cr (+31.1%), margin 12.1% hit by aluminium pass-through lag.

EBITDA was Rs 140 Cr (+31.1%) with a 12.1% margin, which management says would have been 80 bps higher without the aluminium pass-through lag, and PAT was Rs 72 Cr (+24.2%). For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 16.2% (about 20.1% underlying), EBITDA was Rs 551 Cr (+24.1%) at a 13.1% margin, and EPS was Rs 15.08 versus Rs 12.56. Management says aluminium price increases in March were not fully passed on, costing a conscious Rs 5 Cr, and that April price increases have since been passed to both aftermarket and OEM customers. Wheel assembly revenue goes to nil from 1 April 2026.

544029|2026-06.headline: Gandhar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 92% YoY to INR 1,732 crore and PAT hit a record INR 206 crore on a per-kilolitre spread of INR 28,145.
544029|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 92% YoY to INR 1,732 crore and EBITDA reached INR 281 crore, with margin at 16.2% versus 5.1% a year earlier. PAT of INR 206 crore was the company's highest quarterly profit and exceeded the full FY26 profit, per management. Management attributed the spread expansion to exceptional Middle East-driven market conditions, sourcing from domestic base oil producers and higher realisations, and said it expects margins to stay near these levels for one to two quarters. Volume grew about 8% YoY to roughly 131,000 KL, and an interim dividend of 100% of face value was declared.

segments.name: PHPO (personal care, healthcare, pharma, performance oil)
segments.commentary: Primary growth engine with 18% YoY growth, driven by volume and wider revenue from existing customers. Management expects it to remain the star segment and indicated it stays above about 50% of total sales.

segments.name: PIO (process and insulating oil / transformer oil)
segments.commentary: Grew 28% YoY; management said PIO manufacturing volume rose from 14,000 KL to 18,000 KL. Demand from transformer, power and rubber customers; growth expected to be strong going forward.

segments.name: Lubricants
segments.commentary: Broadly stable, described as a resilient revenue base. Price increase taken in automotive lubricants with some delay due to the dealer-distributor network.

segments.name: Texol (Hamriyah Free Zone, Sharjah subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Operations temporarily hit by regional supply constraints and vessel disruptions in Q1; logistics gradually normalising. Management calls it strategically important and margin-accretive. Borrowings sit here, mostly working-capital plus some term loan.

guidance_outlook: Management is hopeful margins stay at or around current levels for most of FY27, and anticipates stellar levels for at least the next 1-2 quarters; said it is not reverting immediately.
Volume growth target of 8-10% (up to 11%) for FY27; management said revenue growth from value would also be higher.
Exports expected to hold at roughly the current share level; the company is aiming to increase export metrics over the year.
Capex plans to be announced in about the next quarter; company says internal accruals can fund capex without term loans, with term loans possible if needed.
Tax rate: 25% in India; blended consolidated rate of roughly 23-24% implied by management.
Interim dividend of 100% of face value declared; about INR 20 crore of Q1 profit earmarked for it.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 597,000 KL; all 3 plants together ran at about 97% on a two-shift basis, with third shift used when required.
Capacity is fungible across PHPO, PIO and lubricants; no segment-wise capacity split is disclosed.
Capex plans not yet announced; management is drawing them up and will update in about the next quarter.
Management said it has a debt-free standalone balance sheet and sufficient internal accruals for own-funded capex.
demand_pricing: Price increases were taken across PHPO, PIO and lubricants (automotive lubricants with a lag), per management.
Management attributed the spread to a mix of higher demand, higher realisations and agile raw material sourcing, and said sourcing was the bigger contributor in some answers.
Main base oil supply was from Saudi Arabia and South Korea; Hormuz disruption delayed Saudi shipments, so the company bought more from South Korea and domestic base oil producers at different prices.
Export realisations are about 5-6% higher than domestic realisations, per management.
Management estimates customer stocking of roughly 10-15% at most in the quarter, not a doubling.
Industry growth cited at 5%+ CAGR (CRISIL report) and 6-7% CAGR in a later answer; company has over 4,000 customers and exports to 100+ countries.
Channel partner volumes fluctuate and are not tracked to end industry; PIO is tender-based.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion came from product mix versus inventory gains, and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory gains were minimal (raw material held 30-40 days); gains came mainly from higher selling prices. It is hopeful margins stay at or near current levels for most of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume and revenue growth expectations for FY27, and the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 8-10%, up to 11%, historically; value growth expected to be higher. Exports expected to remain at current levels, with an aim to grow export metrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread sustainable, and what was the gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects margins at stellar levels for at least 1-2 quarters and will not revert immediately. Consolidated gross margin for the quarter was 21.4%. It declined to give forward guidance on the INR 28,000 spread.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PIO and channel partner volumes appear to decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel partner volumes are lumpy and not tied to end industry. PIO manufacturing volume rose from 14,000 KL to 18,000 KL on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing position and trade payables outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone company is debt-free; borrowings are at Texol, mainly working capital plus declining term loan. Trade payables rose from INR 315 crore to INR 430 crore; about INR 600 crore of the INR 900-odd crore payables is not yet due and about 90% is within 90 days, with no rise in payable days.

qa_highlights.question: What are the tax rate and blended margin expectations for FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: India tax rate 25%; blended rate of roughly 23-24% implied. Management declined to give a sustainable margin run-rate beyond the current quarters.

risks_watch: Spread of INR 28,145/KL is far above the INR 8,274/KL normal level; management itself said it should be viewed in the context of exceptional conditions, and historical EBITDA margins were about 5-8%.

Receivables rose with revenue; watch working capital and Texol throughput as logistics normalise.
South Africa entry strategy not yet defined; revenue potential from Indonesia, Europe, USA and South Africa not quantified.
Customer concentration not disclosed; management said top-5 share is not significant across 4,000+ customers.

544030|2026-03.headline: Flair Writing Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR322.9 crore, FY26 revenue up 15.8% to INR1,250.1 crore; crude-linked raw material costs now a margin headwind in Q1 FY27.
544030|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 15.8% to INR1,250.1 crore, meeting the company's 15% guidance, with EBITDA up 21.5% to INR224.5 crore and EBITDA margin up 85 bps to 18%. Q4 revenue grew 8.4% to INR322.9 crore, with gross margin up 258 bps to 51.2% and EBITDA margin up 217 bps to 17.9%. Own-brand sales reached 91% of revenue, while OEM sales fell, and Creative and Steel Bottles & Houseware together reached 31% of revenue. Management flagged that crude-derivative raw material costs (about 35% of raw materials) rose sharply due to the West Asia crisis, with an expected ~4% margin hit in Q1 FY27 and ~1% by year-end, and retained 15% FY27 revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Debtors -4 days QoQ; creditors -3 days QoQ

segments.name: Own brand (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic own-brand sales INR264 crore, +17% YoY; FY26 INR1,017 crore, +20%. Own-brand exports Q4 INR34 crore (+31%), FY26 INR122 crore (+29%).

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: Domestic OEM fell from INR15 crore to INR9 crore in Q4; legacy domestic OEM at zero, with new Flomaxe-subsidiary engagements. Export OEM fell from INR32 crore to INR17 crore in Q4 on subdued client demand and West Asia disruption.

segments.name: Creative
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR86 crore, +80% YoY; FY26 INR298 crore, +74%. 29 new products in FY26 and six in Q4. Wooden pencil manufacturing started at Flomaxe Surat facility.

segments.name: Steel Bottles & Houseware
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR22 crore, +76% YoY (from INR12 crore); FY26 INR85 crore, +95%. 24 products; growth levers are portfolio expansion and general trade distribution.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR213.4 crore, -4% YoY (from INR221.7 crore), driven by Pen OEM down 65%; Pen own-brand grew 9%. Own brand now 95% of Pens revenue vs 80% a year ago.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% maintained despite West Asia crisis; management targets Pens ~5%, Creative ~50%, Steel Bottles ~40%.
Q1 FY27 margin impact: raw material cost inflation of ~13% weighted average on consumption, net ~4% margin impact in Q1, narrowing over the next three quarters to ~1% by end FY27.

Mitigation via scheme and discount rationalisation and selling price increases in household and steelware, plus premiumisation.
Inventory days expected to fall 5-7 days over the next two quarters as pre-stocking was a one-time event; working capital impact of ~9 days expected going forward.
Final dividend of INR0.50 per share (10% of face value), 20% of FY26 face value, same as prior year.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR104 crore, of which INR40 crore in Q4; INR20 crore spent on Flomaxe Surat facility (building and plant & machinery).
Valsad facility operations to commence Q1 FY27, with capacity ramp-up by Q3 FY27; Q4 start was reported as slightly delayed due to machinery and raw material delays.
FY27 capex expected at INR80-90 crore, including INR60-70 crore for Valsad; annual replacement capex around INR42 crore.
Management cites ~3x asset turnover; peak achievable sales from current and planned assets estimated at ~INR1,750 crore.
Plans to add a fourth steel bottle line; no asset-light model planned.
demand_pricing: Back-to-school demand described as very positive with no dent after price increases, per management.

Raw material mix: crude-linked derivatives ~35% of raw materials; weighted average input inflation ~13% (range 0% to 50% across items). About 4-5 weeks of raw and packing stock built up, representing ~40% of inventory.
Middle East exports ~25% of total export revenue; shipments to the region paused for past couple of months due to route closure.
Export reach is 100+ countries after four new countries were added.

Creative growth to come from pencils (mechanical, wooden, 2mm) and kids categories, plus geometry boxes and colouring range; growth expected to come from taking share from existing players rather than adding outlets.
Creative touch points ~65,000-70,000 outlets; management plans to deepen throughput per outlet rather than add outlets.
Receivable improvement attributed to collection process changes; management expects further improvement as Steel, Household and Creative grow.

qa_highlights.question: How much of raw material is crude-linked, how much price hike has been taken, and was there channel stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude derivatives are about 35% of raw materials; weighted input inflation is ~13%. Pre-stocking was done by buying at dips, which dampens the cost increase. Price hikes taken in household and steelware; schemes being rationalised.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Pens given it grew ~2% vs high-single-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ~5% annual Pens growth, ~50% for Creative and ~40% for Steel Bottles, with overall growth around 15% and mix of Creative and Steel rising to ~15% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steel bottle revenue moderate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 benefited from festive season; company is strengthening general trade, modern trade and e-commerce/quick commerce and launching new ranges.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact and normalisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Maximum ~4% impact in Q1 FY27, easing over three quarters to ~1% by year-end FY27; longer if conflict persists, with pricing actions needed to pass through costs.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from existing and planned capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR1,750 crore of sales from the facilities being built, including Valsad; asset-light model not under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone operating profit flat/declining while consolidated grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Machinery is fungible across entities; product allocation across Daman, Valsad, Dehradun and Surat drives standalone vs subsidiary profit. Management points to consolidated numbers as the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost trend versus gross profit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost plus job work is 20-21% of consolidated revenue and stable; other expenses declining as a percentage of sales.

Middle East export route closures (about 25% of exports) and weak export OEM demand (down ~47% YoY in Q4).

Pens revenue growth of ~2% in FY26 versus high-single-digit earlier guidance; new 5% target to be tracked.

544030|2026-06.headline: Flair Writing Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.6% YoY to INR319.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.7% on raw material inflation; FY27 15% growth guidance reiterated.
544030|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10.6% YoY to INR319.2 crore while gross margin held at 50% (down 31 bps YoY, down 151 bps QoQ). EBITDA rose 7.7% YoY to INR53.3 crore with margin of 16.7% (down 46 bps YoY), and PAT grew only 0.5% YoY to INR29.1 crore as other income fell. Management attributed margin pressure to West Asia-driven raw material inflation, and said price hikes, reduced schemes and discounts are working to offset it. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% and an EBITDA margin target of 17-18%.

544044|2026-06.headline: India Shelter Q1 FY27: PAT up 23% YoY to INR 143 crore and ROE 17.5%, but Stage 3 rose to 1.5% and reported AUM growth slowed to 24%.
