rows.why: About 33% of inventory sold since launch, with the commercial project named as the largest contributor to sales and collections over the next 2-3 quarters and a target of at least 1 lakh sq ft more to be sold.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, launch pipeline and presales targets, but cautious and evasive on cash flow, collections and debt, deferring OCF and collections targets offline and giving no de-leveraging path; analysts' questions focused on funding for Bandra and FY27 revenue and margin.

544055|2026-03.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q4 FY26: AUM ₹14,005 crore (+13% YoY), Q4 profit ₹71 crore, GNPA down to 3.89%; Vision 3030 targets ₹30,000 crore AUM by 2030.
544055|2026-03.overview: Management used its maiden Capital Markets Day (7 May 2026) to unveil Vision 3030: ₹30,000 crore AUM, ROA of 5%+, ROE of 20%+ and 10 million lives by 2030. FY26 showed a full-year loss of ₹222 crore in the prior year turning into a ₹170 crore full-year profit, with Q4 profit of ₹71 crore described as the best in seven quarters. Asset quality improved: GNPA 3.89% (from 4.85%), net NPA 1.14%, Q4 credit cost 2.8% and FY26 credit cost 3.5%. Diversification moved non-JLG to about 17% of the portfolio, and cost of funds fell to 10.27% from 11.02%.

financial_highlights.metric: Portfolio under management (AUM) at FY26 end

financial_highlights.change: highest in last seven consecutive quarters

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 credit cost / FY26 credit cost

financial_highlights.change: from 11.02% (about 75 bps lower); incremental borrowing cost ~9.9%

segments.name: JLG (joint liability group)
segments.commentary: About 83% of the portfolio at FY26 end (82.6% per CEO); yield ~24.5% effective. Management says JLG remains the entry point and the 2030 mix targets about 53% JLG.

segments.name: Muthoot Small Enterprise Loan (individual loans)
segments.commentary: Portfolio ~₹2,383-2,387 crore with near-zero delinquency; FY26 disbursement ₹2,536 crore; monthly disbursement ₹450-470 crore; ticket ₹60,000-3 lakh at 23-25% ROI; ~90% NACH clears same day; 97% of borrowers have bureau score above 730.

segments.name: Micro-LAP / MSME LAP
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursement ~₹26.5 crore, with monthly disbursement near ₹11 crore; average ticket ~₹4 lakh; 100% collection and no delinquency as stated; ROI 18-22%; Kerala is 45% of the book.

segments.name: Gold loans (via Muthoot FinCorp referral)
segments.commentary: Referral volume ~₹7 crore per month; co-lending with Muthoot FinCorp under consideration; yield ~17-21%.

guidance_outlook: Vision 3030: AUM ₹30,000 crore by 2030, implying ~21% CAGR from ₹14,000 crore; the company says it aims for >15% growth in FY27 (management earlier cited a 12-15% range in analyst questions).
Long-run credit cost target ~2.5%; FY30 ROA target 5%+ (~₹1,000 crore profit in FY30 confirmed); ROE 20%+.
NIM: management expects FY27 NIM of roughly 12.5% and 13.5-14% (13% 'across cycles') by FY30; no credit rating upgrade assumed for FY27.
Opex to fall to 5% or below by 2030 from 6.4%; weighted average portfolio yield to rise from 18.8% to 22-23%.
Balance sheet leverage target ~4x (3.3x on balance sheet now); about 12-15 months of current capital to fund growth before equity is needed.
NCD/ECB share of borrowings to rise from 22% to ~40% by 2030; digitally collected share of collections to reach 75% by 2030 (about 40% now).
capex_capacity: Network: 1,670 branches across 21 states and UTs, 390 districts; 91 branches merged or closed under branch-profitability review, while new branches opened in Assam, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
Workforce 15,735 employees, ~90% in field roles; ~12% of field roles are female ROs, with attrition about 50% lower than male counterparts.
Credit underwriting: dedicated team of ~1,800 (about 2,000 in the credit vertical) with generative-AI-assisted credit appraisal memos.
Vision 2030 product mix: JLG 53%, individual loans ~33%, MSME LAP ~10%, retail secured ~3%.
Contingency funding of ₹2,000-3,000 crore available at short notice; ₹700-800 crore free funds carried through the year, plus HQLA.
CGFMU / CGTMSE guarantee applied for, pending budget allocation; the new CGS-MFI scheme capped at ~₹300 crore for the company.
demand_pricing: Wallet-share study: for ~30 lakh overlapping customers, FY24 to FY26 microfinance exposure fell ~32% while total loan balances rose from ~₹40,000 crore to ~₹45,000 crore; gold exposure rose from ₹4,093 crore to ₹7,456 crore.
Yields: JLG effective ~24.5%, individual loans ~23.5%, LAP 18-22%, gold 17-21%; management says micro-LAP at 27-28% due to processing fees.
Rejections: post-MFIN guardrails the JLG rejection rate is ~60% (Karnataka ~65%); productivity per employee fell to ~₹7 lakh in Q1 due to rejections.
Rural focus: 98% of branches are rural; competition described as relatively limited in these areas.
Lending rates were cut multiple times in 2024; management says ~70% of FY26 disbursements were made at rates ~200 bps lower than the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 21% CAGR to ₹30,000 crore square with FY27 guidance of 12-15%, and what gives confidence growth accelerates from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 beat four of five guidance items (AUM growth 13% vs 5-10% guided, credit cost 3.5% vs 4-6%, mix 83:17 vs 85:15) and expects more than 15% growth in FY27, with the step-up from diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification shield the company from the microfinance cycle, and what is FY30 asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification and deeper household engagement should smooth the cycle, with long-run credit cost of about 2.5%; FY30 profit of ~₹1,000 crore was confirmed as the target.

qa_highlights.question: How is underwriting done without over-reliance on talent, and why a hybrid rather than centralised model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a human-in-the-loop model: field credit officers use AI-assisted appraisal memos and aggregator data, and a central team sets loan ceilings within which branches decide.

qa_highlights.question: How do individual loans differ in credit risk from JLG, and how can the bounce and delinquency record be trusted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 0+ and 30+ delinquency of zero on ~₹2,300 crore, ~10% NACH bounce collected within eight days, a 700+ bureau score floor, and 2-3 years of repayment track record with the company.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM rise from 12% to 13-14% when new-disbursement yields are similar to the new loan rates?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 NIM was 12.8% at the start of the year and about 12% in FY26; repricing benefits from the Q2 FY26 yield changes fall into FY27, with NIM back to about 12.5%. The 13%+ level rests on mix, cost of funds and yield, and FY27 excludes any rating upgrade.

qa_highlights.question: What are branch rationalisation plans and the benefit from the CGS-MFI guarantee scheme?
qa_highlights.answer: 91 branches have been merged or closed, while new branches open in new states. CFO said the CGS-MFI scheme caps the company at ~₹300 crore and adds little for a large MFI, with cost of funds already at ~9.9% on incremental borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company charge higher yields for lower-risk products, and why would credit cost fall as yields rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the yield rise is driven by higher-yield new originations and the shrinking of the defaulting denominator, and that Muthoot's brand and gold-custody service let it price slightly higher than peers.

qa_highlights.question: What are leverage and capital needs to reach 5% ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company targets about 4x leverage (3.3x on balance sheet now), with NIM +100 bps, opex -50 bps and credit cost around 2.5% sufficient for 5% ROA, plus about 1% of fee income.

risks_watch: Dependence on the JLG segment (about 83% of AUM) and on Southern states, where 55% of customers sit; state-level regulatory risk raised by a questioner, with management saying regulated entities are exempt from local rules.
Execution risk on the ~21% AUM CAGR and on yield uplift to 22-23%; the FY27 guidance of 12-15% is below the FY30 path.
Credit quality of new individual/MSME/LAP products over a full credit cycle, since they have limited seasoning (about 2.5-3 years of track record for the cohort).
Interest rate and inflation risk: management flagged a possible modest policy-rate increase.
Equity dilution: management said equity will be needed at some point, with the current capital covering about 12-15 months of growth.
Rising rejection rates (~60%) constrain JLG sourcing and productivity; watch employee productivity and attrition.
key_quotes: So we are confident that we will overachieve our guidance.
So effectively what is happening is that whenever we do a rate change or a yield change that is always a prospective impact.
So we'll be looking at four times leverage.
So I think the idea is to have a qualitative growth and a sustainable growth.
544055|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and funding, with the CEO and CFO stressing that FY26 beat most guidance items and that liquidity is ample. Cautious and hedged on the 2030 path: the 21% AUM CAGR, the 5% ROA and the 13-14% NIM are framed as targets, FY27 NIM is guided lower at about 12.5%, and no rating upgrade is assumed for FY27. Evasive on state-level political risk and on the pace of the JLG shift, where answers leaned on the brand and on "not moving away from JLG".

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 NIM about 12.5% from about 12% in FY26, rising to 13-14% by FY30; opex to fall from 6.4% to 5% or below by 2030 and portfolio yield to rise from 18.8% to 22-23%, though these are framed as targets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network is 1,670 branches after 91 merged or closed under profitability review, with only a few new branches in Assam, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; no new capacity is quantified and the branch count is being rationalised rather than expanded.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at 12-15% (midpoint 13.5%) and management says it aims for more than 15%, backed by Q4 FY26 disbursements of ₹2,876 crore (+46% YoY) and AUM of ₹14,005 crore (+13% YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed; the balance sheet is at 3.3x leverage against a ~4x comfort level, and management says current capital covers about 12-15 months of growth before equity is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 beat four of five guidance items (AUM growth 13% vs 5-10% guided, credit cost 3.5% vs 4-6%), but management kept FY27 at 12-15% and assumed no rating upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: JLG rejection rate is about 60% (Karnataka about 65%), productivity fell to about ₹7 lakh per employee in Q1, and management flagged a possible modest policy-rate increase; the FY27 guide of 12-15% is below the 21% CAGR path to 2030.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Individual loans (₹2,383-2,387 crore book, FY26 disbursement ₹2,536 crore), MSME LAP (FY26 disbursement ~₹26.5 crore, monthly ~₹11 crore) and gold referral (~₹7 crore per month, co-lending under consideration) are scaling, with the mix shifting to 17% non-JLG and a 2030 target of 53% JLG.

rows.label: Opex ratio decline to 5% or below by 2030
rows.why: Opex ratio fell to 6.4% in Q4 FY26 from a peak near 7% in Q1-Q2 FY26, and management targets 5% or below by 2030.

rows.label: Cost of funds decline and NCD/ECB mix shift
rows.why: Cost of funds fell to 10.27% from 11.02% (about 75 bps), incremental borrowing is about 9.9%, and NCD/ECB share is to rise from 22% to about 40% by 2030.

rows.label: Credit cost normalisation and asset quality
rows.why: GNPA fell to 3.89% from 4.85%, Q4 credit cost is 2.8% against FY25's ~9.4%, and the long-run target is about 2.5%.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, asset quality, funding and liquidity, but hedged on the 2030 path (21% CAGR, 5% ROA, 13-14% NIM) and kept FY27 NIM at about 12.5%; analysts pushed on the gap between the 21% CAGR and 12-15% FY27 guidance, JLG dependence in Southern states, and state-level r

544055|2026-06.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q1 FY27: record Q1 disbursement of INR2,644 crore, cost of funds down to 10.13%, credit cost 2.6%, and AUM growth guidance raised to 20%.
544055|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the start of an execution-led turnaround, with disbursements of INR2,644 crore (about 49% above Q1 FY26) and collection efficiency near 98%. Cost of funds fell 14 bps QoQ to 10.13% before the benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade, and credit cost eased to 2.6% from 2.8%. PPOP rose about 43% YoY and 3% QoQ, and AUM grew 18% YoY. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 20%, ROA to the upper end of 3.3%, and ROE to around 18%, and said NIM expansion would show from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: about 49% above Q1 FY26; highest Q1 ever

financial_highlights.value: Up about 43% YoY and about 3% QoQ
Flat QoQ; management cited about 50 bps YoY expansion in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Full-year FY27 NIM guided 12.3%-12.5%; management said 12.5% upper end is achievable

segments.name: Joint Liability Group (JLG)
segments.commentary: Yield on group loans about 24.85% after a rate hike from 23.5% at end of Q1. Remains one of three priority products.

segments.name: Individual loans
segments.commentary: About INR3,200 crore book with 0.02% 30+ delinquency and no 60+ or 90+. Yield about 23.5%. Built on a creamy layer of about 8.5-9 lakh customers with 700+ scores. Repayments are 100% digital.

segments.name: Gold loans (referral and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Disbursing about INR100 crore per month since April; about INR350-360 crore disbursed to date. Q1 was almost entirely referral business. Co-lending split is 60% on Muthoot Microfin's book and 40% on the parent's book. Referral earns 1.5%.

segments.name: Loan against property and consumer durables
segments.commentary: LAP yield 18%-22%. Consumer durable loans are a pilot of about INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield, funded through CP at about 8.1%-8.2%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance raised to 20% for FY27.
Disbursement plan exceeds INR12,000 crore for FY27, averaging about INR1,000 crore per month.
Cost of funds targeted to reach single digits by end of FY27, with AA- rating benefit still to flow through.
FY27 ROA guided at 3.3% (upper end expected), ROE around 18% (upper end). Management expects 4%-4.5% ROA within about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.
Credit cost guidance of 2.7%-3.5% for FY27, now expected to be better; long-term normalised range 2%-2.25%.
NIM guidance 12.3%-12.5%; NIM expansion expected from Q2 as liquidity drag eases.
Digital collection to reach about 75% by 2030, possibly earlier. Currently about 40%, improving about 6% per quarter.
Branch count to reach 1,740-1,750 by end FY27 from about 1,670 now.
capex_capacity: Branches about 1,670 now, targeted at 1,740-1,750 by end FY27. Expansion focus on Andhra Pradesh and Assam, plus north, east and west geographies.
AUM per branch rose to INR8.65 crore from about INR7 crore a year ago. Management targets INR12-13 crore per branch.
Gold loans use parent Muthoot Finance branches for storage and assessment, so no separate gold branch capex is needed.
Consumer durables pilot of INR500 crore to be expanded depending on results.
demand_pricing: Industry AUM contracted, but quality is improving. Management says larger, well-capitalised players are gaining share. Industry active customers have fallen from about 8 crore at peak to about 6 crore.
Muthoot's active customers fell 0.6% QoQ and declined YoY. Management attributes this to write-offs and closures and says new customer acquisition should lift the base from Q2.
Group yield raised to 24.85% from 23.5% at end of Q1, with no further hike planned for now. Management said the benefit should go to NIM rather than customers.

Liquidity is ample. About INR5,000 crore of sanctions are in hand, plus INR1,000 crore under CGFMU of which only INR200 crore has been drawn. About 20% of AUM is targeted for CGFMU cover; the application is pending.
Management said El Nino rainfall deficit fell from 43% to about 12%. Less than 2% of customers are directly exposed to agri activity in sensitive regions.

qa_highlights.question: Can disbursement return to INR1,000 crore per month, and can AUM growth exceed 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,000 crore per month is achievable, with FY27 disbursement above INR12,000 crore. Q1 at INR2,644 crore was the slowest quarter, and Q2 onward should rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended yield, given that the incremental cost of borrowing fell while NIM stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended portfolio yield is about 23%. Reported yield is diluted by non-performing assets in the denominator. Management said Q1 NIM is up about 50 bps YoY, and yield expansion will follow as collections from NPAs improve.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Assam flood or the broader monsoon risk affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no exposure to upper Assam, where floods are seasonal, and its lower-Assam portfolio is unaffected so far. Natural calamity insurance covers all customers, including drought.

qa_highlights.question: How do the direct assignment (DA) income and gold referral and co-lending work?
qa_highlights.answer: DA income is booked under net gain on fair value changes, not interest income. Q1 DA was about INR355 crore, and FY26 DA was about INR1,600 crore. Gold co-lending began only at quarter-end, so about 98% of Q1 gold business was referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 2.7%-3.5% has been beaten, with Q1 at 2.6%. Management expects FY27 to come in below 2.7%, with a long-term normal of 2%-2.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and ROA/ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM guidance is 12.3%-12.5%, with the upper end expected. FY27 ROA is guided at 3.3% (upper end) and ROE at about 18%. Management targets 4%-4.5% ROA in about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are the MFI vs non-MFI mix targets?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM mix is at 76:24 (JLG to non-JLG) now and is expected to end FY27 at about 70:30. Management's long-term target is 55:45 on AUM and 60:40 on balance sheet after DA.

risks_watch: Cost of funds must reach single digits by end FY27; benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade and CGFMU drawdown (only INR200 crore drawn of INR1,000 crore; about 20% of AUM targeted cover, application pending) are not yet in the Q1 numbers.
NIM expansion is guided from Q2, but Q1 NIM was flat QoQ with negative carry from excess liquidity; watch whether disbursement recovery consumes liquidity and lifts NIM toward 12.3%-12.5%.
Disbursement must average about INR1,000 crore per month (FY27 plan above INR12,000 crore) versus INR2,644 crore in Q1; AUM growth guidance of 20% depends on this ramp.
Active customers fell 0.6% QoQ and declined YoY; management expects base growth from Q2 but this depends on new acquisition in new geographies (Andhra Pradesh, Assam, north, east, west).

Credit cost of 2.6% is below the 2.7%-3.5% guidance; sustainability versus the long-term 2%-2.25% normal and exposure to El Nino and Assam floods are open questions, though management cites insurance cover and less than 2% agri exposure in sensitive regions.
Gold co-lending and referral and the consumer durable pilot (INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield) are early-stage; Q1 gold business was about 98% referral and co-lending only began at quarter end.
key_quotes: this is a turnaround that we have been talking about the quarter 1 performance actually reflects what strategy that we have developed and articulated, it is getting into motion and getting into execution.
In the quarter, we have reduced our cost of fund from 10.27% to 10.13%, 14 basis point reduction has already happened in the Q1 itself.
We feel that in the financial year, we should be able to come into single digits in terms of our cost of fund and availability of fund is already there.
So we are likely to overachieve that in terms of credit cost. We are looking at 2.7% at the lower spectrum, but we'll be better than that for sure, the way the asset quality is panning out.
544055|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat throughout, with management describing Q1 as the start of an execution-led turnaround and raising FY27 AUM, ROA and ROE guidance. Answers were more cautious on the specifics of blended yield, the DA income split and the CGFMU timing, and on the active customer decline, where management acknowledged a minor QoQ and YoY drop.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of funds fell 14 bps QoQ to 10.13% before the AA- benefit, incremental borrowing cost is 9.8%, and operating cost fell to 6.3%; management guides NIM to 12.3%-12.5% with expansion from Q2 as liquidity drag eases, though Q1 NIM was flat QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches guided to rise from about 1,670 to 1,740-1,750 by end FY27, about 5.5% more, with AUM per branch already at INR8.65 crore against a INR12-13 crore target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursement of INR2,644 crore in Q1 (+49% YoY) with FY27 plan above INR12,000 crore (about INR1,000 crore per month) and about INR5,000 crore of sanctions in hand; active customers fell 0.6% QoQ, so volume depends on acquisition from Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new plant or heavy capex is discussed; gold uses parent Muthoot Finance branches so no separate gold branch capex is needed, and branch growth is a small opex-led build.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: AUM growth was raised to 20% and ROA guided to upper end of 3.3%, ROE to about 18%; credit cost is already beating guidance, and AA- benefit and CGFMU cover are not yet in Q1 numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost of 2.6% in Q1 is already below the 2.7%-3.5% FY27 guide, management expects FY27 below 2.7%, and AUM guidance was raised to 20%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Consumer durable loan pilot of about INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield is to be expanded depending on results; gold co-lending only began at quarter end with about 98% of Q1 gold business referral.

rows.label: Group yield hike to 24.85% flows to NIM
rows.why: Group yield raised from 23.5% to 24.85% at end of Q1 with no further hike planned; management said the benefit goes to NIM, not customers.

rows.label: Cost of funds to single digits by end FY27
rows.why: Cost of funds at 10.13% in Q1 (down 14 bps QoQ) before the AA- CRISIL upgrade benefit, with CGFMU only INR200 crore of INR1,000 crore drawn and application pending for about 20% of AUM cover.

rows.label: Sanctions pipeline supports disbursement ramp
rows.why: About INR5,000 crore of sanctions in hand plus INR1,000 crore under CGFMU; Q1 was the slowest quarter at INR2,644 crore against the INR1,000 crore/month average needed.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement ramp, AUM guidance raised to 20%, ROA/ROE and cost-of-funds path, but more cautious on blended yield, DA income split, CGFMU timing and the minor QoQ and YoY decline in active customers, which analysts pushed on.

544057|2026-03.headline: Happy Forgings Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.4% YoY to Rs.424 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.5% and FY27 volume growth guided to late-teens.
544057|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.424 crore (up 20.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs.133 crore (up 30.4%) at a 31.5% margin, and PAT Rs.84 crore (up 23.6%). FY26 revenue reached Rs.1,546 crore (up 9.8%), with EBITDA of Rs.471 crore (30.4% margin) and PAT of Rs.302 crore (19.5% margin). Management guided to late-teens volume growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26, and flagged raw material and other manufacturing cost inflation linked to the US-Iran situation, which it is seeking to pass on to OEMs from 1 April. Management stressed a shift toward new PV, industrial and heavy-forging programmes at higher realisations (Rs.340-350/kg vs current Rs.245/kg).

financial_highlights.value: Rs.84 crore (19.7% margin) / Rs.302 crore (19.5% margin)

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 37% of FY26 revenue; domestic MHCV growth strong, but exports fell single digit for the year and about 25% in Q4. Management expects a market share gain and 35-40% CV growth in FY27.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of FY26 operating revenue, growing around mid-teens for the company; largely domestic. Market share targeted to rise from about 41% to about 45%.

segments.name: Industrials
segments.commentary: 14% of FY26 operating revenue; domestic grew about 59% and exports fell about 11% for the year (per Q&A). Q4 domestic growth about 32%.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue; domestic construction equipment sales fell 7% in the industry. Q4 domestic off-highway declined about 6% for the company.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: 6% of FY26 revenue; Q4 domestic PV growth about 35%. A large customer's share rose from 32% to 47%, with one more line added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at late-teens, with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 levels.
FY27 capex guided at Rs.450-500 crore; planned capex over next two years about Rs.800 crore including solar.
Forging capacity to rise from 147,000 t to 161,000 t by FY27 and 187,000 t by FY28; machining capacity from 69,000 t to 82,000 t by FY27 and 87,000 t by FY28.
Price hikes of about 3.5-4% sought from customers for non-steel cost inflation from 1 April; management expects confirmation from 70-80% of customers within about 10-15 days.
Captive solar plant of 35 AC MW (Rs.170 crore outlay): partial benefits from FY28, full benefits thereafter.
Rs.950 crore new-business order book to be executed over 2-3 years; Rs.250 crore of it is heavy data-centre forgings (700 kg-1.8 t).
capex_capacity: Forging capacity 147,000 t last year; 10,000 t forging line commissioned in Q4 FY26; 4,000 t press expected in H1 FY27 for passenger car programs.
Machining capacity expanded to 68,000 t in FY26, including 9,800 t added in Q3 FY26.
Large capex for data-centre and heavy-engine forgings to complete by end FY27; trials early FY28 and revenue from Q2-Q3 FY28 at Rs.800-1,000/kg realisation.
Wind pinion shaft capex expected to start from Q2 FY27; solar plant generation to begin from Q4 FY27 with 70-80% benefit next year.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand supported by GST rationalisation, infrastructure spending and fleet utilisation; domestic tractor industry strong in FY26; export CV, farm and off-highway markets weak.
Management says Rs.140 crore of new business won in the last four months (industrials and PV), and new order book for Q4 about Rs.150 crore per annum.
Realisation on new order book Rs.340-350/kg versus current Rs.245/kg; management attributes margin gains to higher-precision, higher-value programs.
Steel is a pass-through: domestic with one-month lag, exports with one-quarter lag. Fuel is about 1% of cost (up 30-40%); power about 7% of cost with no hike.
Crank shaft share about 50% of business in FY25 and FY26, expected to reach 58-60% by FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What new businesses and product mix shift are planned over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites Rs.950 crore new-business order book (Rs.250 crore heavy data-centre). Target mix: CV about 27% (from 37%), industrials 30-31% (from 11%), PV about 10% (from 6%). Typical product price moving from about Rs.60,000 to about Rs.25 lakh, heaviest part from 200 kg to 2 t.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike is being sought from customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel is passed through. Besides steel, about 3.5-4% selling price increase sought for freight, carbide and packaging cost inflation (2-2.5% of revenue). Confirmations received from some OEMs, hoped for from 1 April.

qa_highlights.question: Can the data-centre capacity be fast-tracked given the AI infrastructure boom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says customers are building infrastructure; the company expects infrastructure ready by Q4 FY27, with 6-9 months development lead time before revenue. Some OEMs have funded tooling, which management cites as commitment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving gross margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: PV, industrial and some new CV programs at higher realisation. The Rs.950 crore order book realises Rs.340-350/kg versus about Rs.245/kg now. Raw material prices fell about 6% this year while realisation held.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 volume growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CV volumes expected to rise 35-40% on market-share gains (32% to 42% in MHCV). Farm share expected to rise from 41% to about 45%. FADA April data showed tractors up 23% and MHCV up about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects European CV demand to grow single digit; North America ramp-up from Q2 FY27 for passenger cars, with an EV program from FY28 and a European industrial order starting FY29.

risks_watch: Raw material and fuel inflation linked to the US-Iran situation; pass-through depends on OEM confirmations and PO amendments.

544057|2026-06.headline: Happy Forgings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% to Rs.449 crore and PAT 39.2% to Rs.91 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.3%.

EBITDA rose 39.3% to Rs.141 crore, margin up about 275 bps YoY, the fourth straight quarter above 30%. Management says customer price revisions are partly in Q1 (about 30%) and will fully reflect from Q2. Exports were hit by transit delays, with the domestic CV business up about 18%.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of revenue; grew mid-20s. Domestic up over 20%; exports grew despite weak US and Europe tractor demand. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 16% of revenue; around 50% growth in both domestic and export. Export share about 9% of revenue. Drivers cited: power generation, wind, railways, oil and gas, digital infrastructure.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; over 40% growth in both domestic and export. Domestic construction equipment up about 9%. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: About 8% of revenue; growth over 70%, domestic over 40%, exports more than doubled as earlier-secured orders began executing. Export share about 8% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth trajectory hold across industrial, export and PV, and can the high gross and EBITDA margins sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to strength across CV, farm, PV; a ~Rs.950 crore order book; and new high-realisation products. It said the last price increase was three years ago, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price-revision benefit flow from Q2, and is it permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% came in Q1. Domestic: 2% taken in Q1 versus 4.5-5% total, with OEMs passing on from Q2. Increases are on a three-year-old base and described as permanent; currency gains supported exports.

qa_highlights.question: Will solar benefit come in Q4 FY27 and can margins stay above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar expected on stream from January, with some generation in Q4 and connection through April. Management is confident of upwards of 30% EBITDA margin, citing a 1-1.5% power benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV revenue grow only ~7% against ~10% industry production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV grew ~18% against ~10% production growth; exports fell ~12% because DDP contracts (Europe, Turkey) saw about a month of deliveries delayed by transit issues.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight cost impact and recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Container costs rose from about USD 2,000 to USD 6,000. About 75% of contracts are pass-through; company expects a 15-20% hit and is negotiating recovery of about USD 4,500 per container.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export mix by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate export share of revenue: CV ~7%, PV ~8%, farm ~5%, off-highway ~5%, industrial ~9%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the Rs.950 crore order book and the Rs.650 crore capex, and plant-level margins for the new industrial line?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book roughly 35-40% industrial, 25-30% PV, 25-30% CV, rest off-highway/farm; 60% export, 40% domestic. New heavy-line gross margins expected around 60-65% with EBITDA about 50% of gross; plant-level margins not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: receivable and inventory days as of June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days improved with no big change; inventory days about 50 as of date; overall working-capital days improved.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be revised given strong Q1 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is high-teen volume growth and it should perform better than that, without giving a revised number.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and high base in PV and CV as capex comes on stream in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not worried about a temporary six-month to one-year dip in asset turns, since capacity is being built for future growth; PV growth is from two to three customers with customer acquisition ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans and funding of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Open to acquisitions and JVs, mainly for technology in energy and aerospace; cautious on expensive valuations in farm/CV. Growth to be funded largely by internal accruals, possibly with a one-year bridge loan for LCs.

544058|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR162 crore with EBITDA flat at INR42 crore; management guides FY27 to flat store count and mid-single-digit same-store growth at best.
544058|2026-03.overview: Credo Brands (Mufti) reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 6% YoY to INR162 crore, with gross margin of 58.8% and EBITDA flat at INR42 crore (25.6% margin) as advertising was stepped up to about 8% of revenue. FY26 revenue was flat at INR592 crore, with EBITDA of INR154 crore (26% margin). The company closed 24 stores and opened 7 in the quarter, reducing the network by 17. Management said FY27 is a consolidation year with roughly 20 openings and 20 closures, with ad spend rising to 8-10% of revenue and margins likely lower.

segments.commentary: Store count fell by 17 QoQ: 7 opened and 24 closed in Q4. Same-store sales were flattish for the quarter, though lower for the full year; revenue per sq ft about INR11,700 (as cited by an analyst, stable).

segments.name: Online / omnichannel
segments.commentary: Online channel is about 9% of revenue, of which the company's own platform is about 5%. Website business grew about 75% YoY in FY26; online EBITDA margin is lower because it is still discount-driven.

FY27 growth: management would be happy with mid-single-digit same-store growth; FY27 described as a consolidation year, with visibility limited by West Asia conflict and inflation.
Advertising and branding spend to rise to about 8-10% of revenue; Raman KV's 9-10% framing was confirmed as the broad direction, but not fixed.
FY27 EBITDA margin may be about 23-24%, lower than FY26's 26%, because of higher marketing spend.
Gross margin expected in a 56-58% range, though management said it could fall to 55%.
Capex of about INR40-45 lakh per new store, depending on high street or mall location.

demand_pricing: Consumer sentiment was cautious through FY26, with uneven discretionary spend and weak footfall; management said near-term demand visibility is poor.

Pricing: management said Mufti has not raised prices, only premiumised brand perception. Gross margin is protected by passing on cost rises and favourable terms with vendors.

Input costs are very high: suppliers are quoting at astronomical levels, and cotton (candy) has risen to about INR62,000 per candy. No forward contracts are used; seasonal contracts are business commitments.
Online AOV is below store AOV; new stores have not yet stabilised after 6-7 months of operation.

qa_highlights.question: How many stores were opened and closed in Q4, and what are the same-store sales and premium-store productivity trends?

qa_highlights.question: What is the store growth and revenue outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20 openings and 20 closures, so the store count stays flat. Management would be happy with mid-single-digit same-store growth, but visibility is poor.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins hold at 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The CFO said FY27 EBITDA margin may be about 23-24% because marketing spend is rising. Gross margin is expected in the 56-58% range.

qa_highlights.question: How has the debtor-days position changed and is it overdue?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor days are in line with the business model and may move 5-10%. Receivables are not overdue, and the company expects to stay structurally above some peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will ad spend fall to 4-5% in FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not say. Ad spend should pay back more before it is escalated further, and it will respond to market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the gross margin expansion, and how is raw material inflation being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 gross margin expansion was mainly product mix. Management said it will pass costs through, with no forward hedging, and sees the 56-58% range holding.

Tier 3 rollout is slower and more cautious after post-COVID consumer behaviour changed.
Dividend: management said INR2 per share was announced, which an analyst had questioned.

544088|2026-03.headline: Medi Assist FY26: total income up 23.6% to INR923.2 crore, operating EBITDA margin 19.3%, company turned debt-free in Jan 2026.
544088|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong top-line growth with total income of INR923.2 crore (up 23.6% YoY) and operating income of INR904.8 crore (up 25.1%). Operating EBITDA reached INR174.6 crore at a 19.3% margin, with quarterly margin expanding from 17.1% in Q2 to 18.6% in Q3 and 19.9% in Q4. Reported PAT was INR89.3 crore, while adjusted PAT was INR68.8 crore after exceptional items. The group became debt-free in January 2026, and Paramount TPA operations were transferred into Medi Assist TPA effective 1 February 2026.

544095|2026-03.headline: EPACK Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 8% YoY to Rs 591 crore and EBITDA margin compressed to 4.37%, with a Rs 32.42 crore PLI reversal weighing on the quarter.
544095|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 591 crore, down about 8% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 25.8 crore (down about 64% YoY) and a 4.37% margin versus 11.21%. Net profit was Rs 2.4 lakh after a Rs 32.42 crore reversal of PLI income accrued in the first nine months and Rs 21.78 crore of RIPS 2024 incentive recognised in the quarter. For FY26, revenue was Rs 1,894 crore (down 12.7%), EBITDA Rs 113.9 crore (down 27.7%), margin 6.01%, and net profit Rs 3.3 crore. Management said early FY27 trends look better, with industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 and a strong order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the PLI benefit reversed and what were the eligibility conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the criteria were investment in the prior year and 5x incremental revenue growth for applicable components; capex was met but incremental revenue shortfall led to reversal of Rs 32.42 crore, pending auditor review and government clarification. The total FY26 eligibility was about Rs 56.5 crore, with only about Rs 32 crore accrued before Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is larger: the Rs 32.42 crore reversal plus Rs 24 crore of unrecognised Q4 PLI, leaving a difference of about Rs 35-36 crore versus the full eligibility, after Rs 21 crore of RIPS was booked.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RAC utilisation level in FY26?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Hisense JV exposed to China-related policy risk?

544095|2026-06.headline: EPACK Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR886 crore (+34% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 6.21% from 8.24% as PLI income dropped to nil.
544095|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 34% YoY to INR886 crore, the company's highest quarterly revenue, with RAC up about 44% (roughly 30% volume, 14% value). EBITDA was INR55 crore, up about 0.7% YoY, with margin at 6.21% versus 8.24%; management said the prior-year figure included INR13.31 crore of PLI income, and the like-for-like underlying margin was about 6.4% in Q1 FY26. Net profit was INR11.8 crore, and management cited a forex loss of about INR6-7 crore and higher wage costs as pressures. Management said FY27 is the last year of PLI benefit and is rolling back PLI discounts shared with brand customers, aiming to fully reverse them by year-end.

Washing machine and LDA capacity ramp flagged as fastest-growing; front-load washing machine pilot to mass production around end-Oct 2026.

demand_pricing: RAC: channel inventory considered largely liquidated after old-BEE-rated stock sell-through allowed until end-June 2026; management estimates industry inventory at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level.

Customer base: 72 customers and 19 product categories at FY26 close; ~73 customers and 19 product lines now, targeting ~75 customers and 20 product lines by end-FY27. Three new categories added in Q1, four more in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Top 2-3 execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AC tailwinds continuing and faster growth in SDA/LDA (washing machines) and components, with more customers added across categories. No specific risk list was given beyond the outlook commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the ~44% RAC growth between volume and value, and whether the volume growth is anchor-customer driven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% volume and about 14% value (AOP increases and commodity pass-through). Management confirmed the volume growth is largely from the anchor customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost escalation is still to be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts reset prices quarterly and the prior quarter's increase was already passed on; little remains. The main margin hit was forex, which produced a loss of about INR6-7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory levels and working capital trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry inventory estimated at 3.5-4 million units, the lowest acceptable level. Working capital days are about 50-60, with in-house inventory still slightly elevated due to BIS/QCO revisions; the company aims to normalise it.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor supply risk as BIS/QCO relief expires around March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed until end of calendar 2026, with domestic capacity installed and in pipeline (operational by end-December) judged sufficient. No plan for in-house compressor capacity in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for depreciation, finance cost and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation not expected to rise significantly over the next three quarters. Finance cost rose about INR3-4 crore QoQ on ~40% growth, with scope to reduce via inventory normalisation. Total capex budget ~INR450-470 crore, with ~INR330-350 crore booked and INR60-70 crore more over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue and EBITDA margin outlook; PLI impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal revenue guidance; industry AC growth ~20% expected and EPACK to outgrow it. Ex-PLI EBITDA ~6.5% in recent quarters; PLI worth roughly 1-2% of margin, shared ~50:50 with customers. Management is rolling back PLI discounts with the aim of full reversal by year-end, with normalised EBITDA from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Sri City utilisation, operating leverage and FY27 utilisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri City reached close to 50% in Q1 FY27 (from under 25%), while Dehradun and Bhiwadi ran above 85%. Management targets 55-60% average across the three plants for FY27, and said it is above 60% on average.

qa_highlights.question: Hisense progress and washing machine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60,000 ACs delivered Jan-Jun season for ~INR120 crore revenue; Q1 alone ~35,000 units for ~INR65 crore. Front-load washing machine pilot underway, mass production targeted by end-October. Management said the five-year ~INR8,000 crore plan is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity hedging policy, especially copper?
qa_highlights.answer: No forward booking in anticipation of orders; back-to-back booking against confirmed orders, with changes passed through in the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 PAT positivity and structural seasonality fix, and the INR5,000 crore FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 and Q3 have historically been loss-making; the company targets stopping this in 4-6 quarters and declined to guide on Q2 FY27 PAT. Top-load washing machines are in production for three national/multinational brands; management said it is largely on track for the FY29 INR5,000 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: Components revenue decline of about 23% and SDA/LDA margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the 23% figure but said components will keep growing; current components are AC-linked (controllers, cross-flow fans, copper tubing). SDA/LDA gross margin is about 1.5-2 percentage points above AC (the transcript says 'basis points'). Non-AC components are being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the spike in other expenses (>50%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a forex loss of INR6-7 crore, plus higher wage costs from the 35%+ rise in sales and production value.

544111|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.

544117|2026-03.headline: Signpost India FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore with EBITDA margin up ~590 bps to 25.5%; management guides 20%+ growth and 25-27% margin for FY27.
544117|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 46% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR162 crore, with operating EBITDA more than tripling YoY to INR42 crore at a 26.3% margin. FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore, EBITDA rose 65% to INR147 crore and net profit more than doubled to INR70 crore. Receivables rose about 80% YoY to INR317 crore, which management attributed to multi-city campaigns requiring regional compliance approvals, and it targets faster collections by Q3 FY27 through milestone-based billing. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

segments.commentary: Management cites DOOH as a higher-margin contributor; digital ad space reportedly rose from 25,000 sq ft to 80,000 sq ft between Q3 and Q4. Transit and digital together are about 48% of FY26 top line.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to multi-city campaigns where regional office approvals delay invoicing; milestone-based billing is being pushed with clients, targeting improvement by Q3 FY27. Bill discounting was explored but rejected due to added cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue cross INR1,000 crore by 2029?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 48% of FY26 revenue is already in the FY27 engine and it would be 'the first person to see that number in 2029', but it could not assure that target.

qa_highlights.question: What drives gross margin and how much can cost fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of services includes licence costs and production/display costs such as Wi-Fi and power; management sees a 7-8% scope to reduce these costs next year without hurting top line. Most licences are minimum-guarantee, not linked to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Sector split of revenue and receivable sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numbers; said PSU/government-linked and FMCG, education, MSME and BFSI are the main categories, not real estate or luxury brands.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin move to 30% in 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new geographies need 4-6 months to mature and gave no margin target beyond the 25-27% EBITDA range guidance; Bangalore Metro ramp was cited as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of recent contracts (Kolkata, Bengaluru Metro, OMC petrol pump hoardings)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata implementation expected at 60-70% by Sept-Oct 2026; Bangalore Metro stations now generating revenue, with some signed for 2-3 years; FY27 growth expected at 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited multi-city techno-commercial bidding track record, 7+ year contract tenures, direct advertiser relationships and the Captura AI planning platform; example of MSRDC bid where 27 agencies bid and few qualified.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on valuation; said Pressman promoters converted equity to non-promoter base due to family losses and age.

544118|2026-03.headline: Jana SFB met all Q4 FY26 guidance: PAT INR140 crore, net credit cost 0.47%, SMA 3.66%; FY27 guided to PAT growth of 80%+.
544118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered on every guidance point set in Q3: PAT of INR140 crore (guided INR140-160 crore), net credit cost of 0.47% (INR156 crore) against 0.79% in Q3, and SMA of 3.66% versus a guided ceiling of below 4%. Gross slippages of about INR334 crore were the lowest in roughly eight quarters, and management said the MFI stress is behind it. Advances grew 23% YoY to INR36,289 crore and deposits grew 23% to INR35,784 crore, with cost of funds down to 7.46%. FY27 guidance calls for gross loan growth of 19-21%, deposit growth of 23-25% and PAT growth of 80%+.

segments.commentary: Vehicle loans grew 79.6% YoY. Used car business launched October 2025, running at about INR25 crore disbursals per month in 15 cities, targeted to reach 35 cities by September 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Unsecured slippages were about INR150 crore in Q4, down 35% QoQ and about 50% YoY, and the SMA book fell about 24%. Management expects further lower slippages in FY27 but not a steep decline, since collections are at 99%.

qa_highlights.answer: Micro LAP was tightened in some geographies last year and management sees no signs of stress. MSME is being watched for Middle East war spillover, and nothing is visible yet.

qa_highlights.answer: No explicit guidance. Management pointed to the Q4 net credit cost of 0.47% as a signal, expecting the same range or slightly better.

qa_highlights.answer: Gold yields are competitive for about INR2 lakh tickets but below gold NBFCs. Yields should rise as MFI customers take smaller-ticket gold loans. Secured MFI book to grow 25-30% and unsecured MFI 10-12%.

rows.why: NIM recovered to 7.5% on a 60 bps YoY fall in cost of funds to 7.4%, but management says cost of funds is at its floor (7.3-7.4% for FY27) and cost-to-income must fall from 66.7-67% to 63-65%, so margin gains depend on cost cuts and mix rather than funding relief.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 78-branch FY27 plan (8 new, 30 splits, 40 relocations, 7 done) plus 50-75 gold branches over the next two quarters on a ~820-branch base, with the gold book up 13.5% QoQ to INR2,678 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 19-21% gross loan growth for FY27 with the secured book up 29% YoY (72.8% of book), gold up over 100% YoY and MFI up 18% YoY, though deposits were flat QoQ and the NBFC book is shrinking.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a standalone plan; the branch rollout is in motion and the INR728 crore capital raise (INR103 crore received, about INR80 crore pending RBI approval, balance over 18 months) is a funding step, not a capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only reiterated (19-21% loan growth, 23-25% deposit growth, PAT 80%+), while Q1 deposits were flat QoQ with bulk down about 6% against that 23-25% deposit target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Deposit growth is flat QoQ against 23-25% guidance, micro LAP shrank and the NBFC book is shrinking by design, and the 19-21% loan growth target depends on these turning positive; management defers the recovery evidence to H1 results.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Credit Line on UPI and loans against shares are set to go live in Q2 FY27; FCNR(B) is not ready, with a possible small offering in Aug/Sep, and the nostro setup starts in July for trade FX.

rows.label: Promoter-level stress and rating downgrade
rows.why: Holding company holds 16.9% (down from a peak of 44%) and was downgraded by India Ratings; management says no financial or operational impact, but the stress is unresolved and the merger rumour was not addressed.

rows.label: CGMFU guarantee claims and recovery
rows.why: INR196 crore of the INR214 crore unsecured net NPA is guarantee-covered; INR65 crore of claims are expected in Q3 with the balance later, and a first recovery is expected in Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Government deposit recovery
rows.why: Government CASA deposits lost in Q4 have not returned; the bank is back on a state empanelment list and expects some flow in Q2, but timing is unclear.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, credit cost (at least 0.45% each quarter) and guarantee cover, but cautious on deposits and liquidity with April-May described as difficult; analysts pressed on CASA sustainability, the CGMFU guarantee claim timing and the promoter rating downgrade, and man

544118|2026-09.headline: Jana SFB raised FY27 PAT growth guidance to 100% (from 80%) after Q2 posted its highest-ever PBT; H1 PAT of INR 326 crore equals full-year FY26 PAT.
544118|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the bank's highest-ever quarterly PBT, with H1 PAT of INR 326 crore equal to FY26 full-year PAT. NIM rose to 7.54% from 6.5% a year ago and cost of funds fell to 7.4% from 7.9%. Gross NPA improved to 2.17% but net NPA rose to 1.08%, which management expects to fall below 1% once INR 68 crore of CGFMU guarantee claims are realised. Advances grew 22% YoY to INR 38,752 crore, while CASA growth of 13% YoY lagged deposits at 17.5% TD growth and remains a focus area.

financial_highlights.change: down from 7.9% in Q2 FY26; stable QoQ
expected below 1% after INR 68 crore guarantee claim realisation
opex up 15% YoY; positive jaws of about 20%

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Largest secured book, growing 28.2% YoY with average ticket size INR 11.9 lakh; operates in about 220 cities with roughly 3,000 people in business roles.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Growing 20.6% YoY; management guides 25-30% growth for this year and next, citing PLI and Make in India demand.

segments.name: Vehicle loans (2-wheeler and used car)
segments.commentary: Grew 76% YoY; 2-wheelers offered in 135 cities and used cars in 50 cities; Q3 expected to be strongest on Diwali demand.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Up 81% YoY but only 0.3% QoQ; 65-70% of the Jan-Mar 2026 6-month loans came up for renewal in Q2. Management expects growth of about 10% a quarter from Q3.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to about 3% (management expects 7-8% at best); no loosening of credit criteria.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Now 26% of gross loan book; collections at 99% including BC book; growth subdued given weak bureau histories among borrowers. 97% of customers have two or fewer MFI lenders vs 93% industry.

segments.name: Unsecured advances
segments.commentary: Up 17% YoY but down 0.3% QoQ; all new disbursements placed under the CGFMU guarantee programme. Uncovered gross NPA of INR 296 crore sits under guarantee cover of INR 319 crore.

segments.name: NBFC term loans
segments.commentary: Growth of 0.7% YoY; management does not expect significant growth.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: CASA up 13% YoY; TD up 17.5% YoY; 96.1% of deposits have contractual tenor of 1 year and above.

guidance_outlook: PAT growth guidance raised to 100% YoY for FY27 from earlier 80%; management expects H2 PAT at least equal to H1 for this to hold.
Advances growth guidance maintained at 19-21%; deposit growth guidance maintained at 23-25%.
Full-year credit cost expected below 2%; H2 credit cost expected lower than H1's 0.92%.
Secured share of book expected to reach about 75% by year-end, versus 73.7% at Q2 and a long-term target of about 80%.
Cost-to-income targeted toward 60% over coming quarters; management says FY27 achievement is unlikely, with 57% (March 2024 level) as the first goal.
NIM expected to stay around current levels (about 7.5%) in H2 with cost of funds around 7.4%.
Guarantee claims of INR 68 crore expected to be received within about 2 months (by end-November); remaining INR 251 crore to be lodged in Q3 next year.

Branch expansion: 78 branches planned, 40 opened so far; launches planned for credit line on UPI (Q2 proof of concept), loans against shares and mutual funds (November), and trade FX via AD-1 licence (December).
capex_capacity: About 820 branches across India; 78 branch openings planned for FY27, with 40 completed by the call date.
Digital onboarding for non-face-to-face CASA accounts expected by January.
AI-led processes introduced in collections, welcome calling and cross-sell, reducing headcount and cost.
Headcount in September 2026 lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth.
demand_pricing: Q2 disbursements of INR 4,414 crore, up 7% YoY and 5% QoQ.
Affordable housing average ticket size INR 11.9 lakh; top seven states make up 67% of concentration, top three 37%.
Insurance income for H1 about INR 45 crore; 80-90% linked to credit life and 10-20% to retail products. IRDAI consultation impact not yet fully assessed.
Management says deposit pricing is fairly competitive; interest rates were harder in Q2 than Q1 and the market shows no sign of weakening rate regime.
Customers in the petroleum supply chain and related MSMEs show marginal impact; some export-linked sourcing paused because of higher shipping costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will slippages trend up or down in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower slippages in Q3 and H2. Q2 had one-offs: a secured loan slippage adding about 0.2% and drought-related MFI slippage of about 0.3%. SMA has graduated down in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 insurance income is credit life and what is the IRDAI consultation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: 80-90% is credit life, 10-20% retail products. Initial IRDAI assessment done; full assessment pending. Management will push penetration and AI-led cost efficiency to offset lower commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cost-to-income decline sustainable and can it fall below 60%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost-to-income expected to stay at or below the September level; management is cautious that sub-60% is unlikely this year. Drivers are productivity, RPA/AI processes and more direct sourcing over DSA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASA outlook and cost of funds risk from rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: CASA fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms but grew 13% YoY; management targets about 20% CASA in H2 via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January. Cost of funds targeted to stay near 7.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guarantee scheme cover the full book and what if it does not?
qa_highlights.answer: Claims of INR 68 crore lodged; NGC expected to pay within about 2 months. CGFMU is not open for fresh guarantees yet, but 1% cover cost has been accrued. If the scheme fails, the accrual becomes a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold loan and micro LAP flat, and when will growth pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold flat due to 6-month loans from Jan-Mar 2026 renewing in Q2 and gold price drop; growth expected to resume in Q3 at about 10% a quarter. Micro LAP may reach 7-8% growth but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Any risks to achieving 100% PAT growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no visible constraint on H2 profit matching H1; credit costs, asset growth and liability growth were all cited as on track.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM move in H2 amid rising rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM around current levels, as MFI share is not rising faster and secured share only reaches about 75%; cost of funds should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook by segment and do drought and geopolitical risks affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME 25-30% growth, affordable housing and vehicles continue strongly. Drought declared in 29 Karnataka districts and 34 Maharashtra districts; slippage impact expected to be immaterial. No material impact from the Iran war so far.

risks_watch: CGFMU guarantee scheme not yet open for fresh guarantees; if it does not reopen, the INR 296 crore uncovered unsecured NPA and future MFI risk rest on the bank's own buffer.
Net NPA at 1.08% is above the 1% comfort level until the INR 68 crore claim is received, expected by end-November.
CASA ratio fell and CASA growth (13% YoY) trails TD growth; deposit growth of 17% YoY is below the 23-25% guidance.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra may lift slippages and moratorium requests; geopolitical oil and shipping cost impact on MSME exporters.

IRDAI insurance commission consultation could cut non-interest income; full impact not yet assessed. Media speculation about a merger, which management said it would evaluate if strategically sensible.
544118|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and cost trajectory, with raised PAT guidance. Management is cautious and candid on CASA, deposit growth shortfall, gold and micro LAP growth, and the cost-to-income target, which it says is unlikely to reach 60% this year.
key_quotes: Q2 has been the highest ever PBT we had in our history.
So rather than provision now and then work around the whole accounting system next quarter again once this claim comes, we have chosen that we will go to 1.08%.
CASA is not our strength at this point of time, and we are doing everything which is possibly available in our heads and efforts to make sure that we bring it up.
I don't see a challenge in the asset growth piece because our products have been in the market for the last 7, 8 years and we've met with good success.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 NIM 7.54% vs 6.5% a year ago and cost-to-income down to 64.3% from 67.0% in Q1; management guides NIM around 7.5% in H2 with cost of funds held at ~7.4%, and cost-to-income toward 60% (57% first goal), though FY27 sub-60% is unlikely.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 78 branches planned for FY27 with 40 opened so far (about 820 branches total), so roughly 38 more openings are still due in H2 FY27.
