rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex or plant discussed; growth runs through branch openings and digital channels already planned, with capex not in the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 PAT growth guidance was just raised to 100% from 80%, and management sees no visible constraint on H2 PAT matching H1 (H1 PAT INR 326 crore), but it is conditional on H2 PAT at least equal to H1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Deposit growth of 17.5% TD and 13% CASA trail the 23-25% deposit guidance, and drought in 29 Karnataka and 34 Maharashtra districts plus the uncovered INR 296 crore unsecured NPA with CGFMU not reopened add risk to the raised PAT target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Credit line on UPI (proof of concept in Q2), loans against shares and mutual funds (November) and trade FX via AD-1 licence (December) are all guided with dates.

rows.label: Net NPA below 1% after guarantee claim
rows.why: Net NPA is 1.08%, and INR 68 crore of CGFMU claims expected within about 2 months should bring it below 1%, with the remaining INR 251 crore lodged in Q3 next year.

rows.label: CASA ratio recovery to ~20% in H2
rows.why: CASA grew 13% YoY and fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms; management targets about 20% CASA via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January, but rate environment is tough and deposit pricing is competitive.

rows.label: AI-led headcount and cost reduction
rows.why: Headcount in September 2026 was lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth, and cost-to-income fell from 67.0% to 64.3% QoQ, with opex up 15% YoY against NII up 35%.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability (raised PAT guidance to 100%), asset quality and cost trajectory, but candid on CASA, deposit shortfall, gold and micro LAP growth, and sub-60% cost-to-income being unlikely this year; analysts probed the sustainability of cost-to-income, CASA and NIM in a r

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

financial_highlights.change: Described as healthy vs prior-year outflows

segments.name: PES (Personal computing / enterprise)
segments.commentary: About 58% of business; grew 37% YoY in FY26, aided by higher H2 PC demand and ASPs. Management expects ~20% average price increase in this category going forward.

segments.name: LIT (Lifestyle IT)
segments.commentary: About 42% of business; grew 24% YoY in FY26. Price increases described as routine only; management says LIT is growing about 2x the industry.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Grew 131% YoY from a small base; customers include large automotive, robotics and IoT manufacturers. Operations moved into a newly created subsidiary; management says meaningful P&L impact is a few years away.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a ~20% CAGR (sustained for 20 years) and expects to maintain this trajectory in FY27; regular-business growth aspiration of 15-20% YoY.
Management estimates PES unit market could degrow 5-10% in CY26 (IDC concurs), but with 20-25% price growth, PES revenue could still grow 10-15% on an as-is basis.
Consumer demand could soften in H2 FY27 on affordability; management is discussing 24- and 36-month interest-free EMI schemes with vendors.
Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).
Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% considered applicable to the industry absent mix change; margins described as intact despite price hikes.
Management said the super cycle could continue for another 1-2 years.
Project business (AI data centre) planned for FY27 subject to viability and ROI; funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores under consideration.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches added (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra); 10,000-plus customers across 700-plus towns.
Working capital was increased on inventory to capture demand; management said inventory days cannot fall while regular business grows ~30%.
Project business: FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores of AI data centre project (Yotta, 512 servers, 4,000 GPUs); no substantial project business in FY26; FY27 plans subject to ROI.
Semiconductor business moved into a separate subsidiary to focus operations and accelerate partnerships and customer acquisition.
Management says it has post-IPO capacity to pick up data centre projects on a selective ROI basis without compromising regular growth.
demand_pricing: Price increases began mainly in H2 FY26; management estimates roughly half of H2 growth (46-47% H2-on-H2) came from pricing, i.e. ~20-22 percentage points.
Management says FY26 growth ex the one large AI project was 31%; FY26 growth without large deals was 15% reported.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 growth reported at 42% and 51% respectively (non-project business).

AI PCs are about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India; NVIDIA DGX Spark and Dell (server, storage, PCs, monitors) partnerships cited; Dell described as at low-single-digit share of revenue, expected to reach close to double digits next FY.
IDC: India traditional PC shipments 15.9 million units in CY2025 (+10.2%); IDC flags possible 5-10% dip in CY2026 shipments.
Enterprise refresh delayed by some large corporates during price hikes is reversing as buyers see 30-40% higher prices a year later.
Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

risks_watch: Possible 5-10% unit decline in PC market in CY26 and H2 FY27 consumer softness from affordability as prices rise further.
Potential supply shortages in PES due to component (DRAM, NAND, GPU) pricing firmness.
Data centre project participation is capital-intensive with lower margins; scale of funnel conversion uncertain.
Inventory days (56) unlikely to fall while regular business grows ~30%; slow-moving inventory provision taken in Q4.
Semiconductor working capital cycle of 100-plus days; benefits to margin a few years away.
Dependence on Dell ramp-up (low-single-digit share now, expected near double-digit next FY).
544119|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the PC super cycle and multi-year growth, with growth targets reiterated. Evasive on specifics: declined to give Dell revenue numbers and deferred distribution-channel and margin-trajectory questions offline, and clarified several analyst misreadings of its figures.
key_quotes: So we are very confident to maintain our trajectory of 20% CAGR in the coming year as well.
This is not a 1-quarter tailwind. It is a structural multiyear upgrade super cycle.

Rashi will pick up proportionate to our capacity amongst these opportunities and obviously not run after everything because they are, one, capital intensive, and second, the margins are also lower on this front.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says distribution PAT margin of 1.5-1.75% is the industry-applicable range absent mix change; FY26 EBITDA margin 2.90% (+72 bps) was driven by price hikes, and Q4 gross margin was dented by slow-moving inventory provisioning, so further expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur) already commissioned, taking the network to 55 city branches; no plant or fixed-capacity capex is described, and the AI data centre project is subject to ROI with FY27 timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IDC flags a possible 5-10% dip in CY26 PC shipments and management flags H2 FY27 consumer affordability softness, so unit volumes are expected to fall even though revenue grows about 10-15% on 20-25% price increases.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held at a ~20% revenue CAGR and 15-20% regular-business growth, with no raise, and FY26 growth was 15% reported (31% ex the large AI project).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer affordability risk and a possible 5-10% PES unit decline in CY26 could weigh on the 20% CAGR, and DRAM/NAND/GPU component pricing could cause supply shortages.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dell ramp (low-single-digit share now, near double digits next FY) and AI PC mix (about 25% of Indian PCs/notebooks) are rising, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: AI data centre project funnel
rows.why: Funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration, but projects are subject to ROI and FY26 had no substantial project business (FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores Yotta project).

rows.label: PES price increases of ~20-25%
rows.why: Management expects ~20% average price increase in PES going forward; H2 FY26 pricing added about 20-22 points to H2 growth of 46-47%, and this supports PES revenue growth of 10-15% even as units fall 5-10%.

rows.label: Working capital days held
rows.why: CFO expects working capital days in a similar range (inventory 56, debtors 46, creditors 44, net 58 days), since inventory cannot fall while regular business grows about 30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the PC super cycle, the 20% CAGR and the 1.5-1.75% PAT margin range, but evasive on Dell revenue numbers and deferred channel and margin questions offline; analysts probed price vs volume split, the Q4 gross margin dip and the AI data centre funnel.

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

financial_highlights.change: up 55% YoY (CEO cited 50% on the opening remarks)

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,102 crore and PAT Rs 105 crore; management stated all-time highs on topline, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE.

segments.name: Commercial vs consumer (B2B mix)
segments.commentary: Management estimates 30-35% consumer-centric and 60-65% commercial (SMB and enterprise). Consumer demand is slowing on affordability, with laptop prices reportedly about 2x year-on-year.

segments.name: Semiconductor / embedded
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue in Q1 grew about 70% versus the Q1 FY26 base (not 70% of full-year revenue, per clarification). Growth is described as near double-digit and sometimes higher.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (acquired)
segments.commentary: Majority stake (67% in year one) in a pan-India system integrator; FY26 revenue was about Rs 850 crore. Management expects integrated services and value-added solutions to be about 5% of revenue, with Q2 as the next update point.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 growth expected to be similar to Q1 (about 60%), with price increase speed roughly halving; management described Q2 as on a strong footing.
Management expects the price uptrend to continue through FY27, with some slowdown in trajectory.
Management cited third-party reports of about a 10% unit decline in the overall PC market, offset by price increases.
Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record over 20 years; cited about Rs 3,000 crore as 20% of a Rs 16,000 crore base.
Semiconductor JV targets more than US$100 million revenue within three years; the JV numbers will be reported with Q2 results.
Large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs; management said the pipeline should last at least three quarters.
capex_capacity: Two new branches planned in Udaipur and Dhule to extend reach into C and D class cities.
Presence across 57 towns in India, per management.
Semiconductor JV Rashi Restar Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited to be formed as a step-down subsidiary; Restar to take 26% stake, with the existing embedded business moving into the JV.
Plans to add 50+ local engineering hires over the next two years for the semiconductor JV.
Debt-to-equity ratio cited at around 0.5; management said large data centre projects could push it to at least 2x.
demand_pricing: Memory, hard drive and CPU shortages are pushing prices higher; management expects the uptrend to continue through FY27.
Management said about 10% market share gain contributed to growth; unit growth ex-SanDisk was about 20%, with SanDisk unit declines pulling reported units lower.
Entry-level laptops face about 50% shortage per management; medium and premium notebooks available if prices are accepted.
T2 partners are holding elevated channel inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern given demand.
Refurbished PCs are seen as small: management estimated the refurbished pool at 0.5-1 million units against a 15-16 million PC TAM in India.
Management said Dell commercial business contributed about 5% of revenue in the quarter, and is above target for FY27.
Management said the company has allocations from NVIDIA, Intel and AMD; supply risk is tracked weekly ('orange alert').

qa_highlights.question: Why is India demand strong relative to global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price 30-35%, quantity 20-25%, new products and brands 5-10%, market share about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 should show a similar trend (about 60%), but the speed of price increases should roughly halve.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline: price or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and to last year's hived-off subsidiary whose service cost sat in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is potential risk, but allocations so far are good given supplier relationships; the company tracks it weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised run-rate business with higher ROCE and working-capital needs; it still participates through smaller Rs 20-70 crore supplies and focuses on neo-clouds and smaller operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record and cited VDA and the Restar JV as longer-term growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor JV economics and Restar's investment amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Restar's investment depends on fair valuation at SPA signing, so it is not quantified; management targets over US$100 million JV revenue in three years and said the JV margin profile is higher than co-distribution.

544120|2026-03.headline: Capital SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose 17% YoY to ₹40 crores, with NIM up to 4.06% and FY27 ROA guided to 1.35%–1.4%.
544120|2026-03.overview: Gross advances reached ₹8,687 crores (+20.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ) and total deposits crossed ₹10,000 crores (+20% YoY). Q4 PPOP rose 28% YoY to ₹62 crores and cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ, with NIM at 4.06% versus 4.01% in Q3. Asset quality was broadly stable: GNPA 2.54%, NNPA 1.24%, with Q4 credit cost of 0.26% driven by higher provisioning (PCR 51.89%) rather than losses. Management guided to FY27 advances growth of 22%+, ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, and credit cost of 0.15%–0.25%.

segments.commentary: 24% of advances at March 2026 vs 21% a year earlier; growing more than twice the Punjab rate YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 secured advances growth of 22%+; advances above ₹16,000 crores by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Gross NPA additions and provisioning: are provisions increasing?

qa_highlights.question: Agri NPA stickiness: will it fall back toward 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not target 2%; it expects agri NPA to stay range-bound with a lower bias. Recoveries concentrate in Q1 and Q3 cash-flow periods.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new ECL framework on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial view is P&L neutral to positive, as current provisions are considered sufficient against the ECL requirement; detailed evaluation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending / BC model and FLDG cover?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank runs a business correspondent lending model (not co-lending) with more than one partner, and the FLDG cover is 5% per regulation. Branches are to remain 90–95% of disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the NII margin expansion and CD ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposit repricing (53% repricing in Q1–Q2) and an improving CD ratio are the two NIM levers; management expects an opex/average assets ratio of 2.9%–3.0% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost for FY27 is 0.15%–0.25%. The Q4 credit cost of 0.26% was provisioning-driven, linked to NBFC-MFI slippage. Cost-to-income is expected to improve, with opex/average assets at 2.9%–3.0%.

Pace of deposit repricing and whether NIM reaches the guided improvement in Q1–Q2 FY27.

ECL transition impact, which management expects to be P&L neutral to positive but is still under evaluation.
Growth outside Punjab through business correspondent partners, which is early-stage and carries FLDG exposure.

544120|2026-06.headline: Capital SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 41.3 crore, with NIM at 4.21% and GNPA down to 2.47%.

NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why PCR has been rising over recent quarters and whether it will stay stable

qa_highlights.question: Headroom for cost of deposit repricing and ROA path

544122|2026-03.headline: Entero FY26 revenue rose 31.5% like-for-like to INR6,591 crore with 4% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance is 23% growth and 5% margin excluding new acquisitions.
544122|2026-03.overview: FY26 met all three initial targets: like-for-like revenue growth of 31.5% (organic 15.6%, inorganic 16%), 4% EBITDA margin (+67 bps) and operating cash flow of INR96.2 crore. Q4 revenue grew 42.6% YoY, with organic growth of 17.1% and acquisitions contributing 26%, and Q4 EBITDA margin reached 4.5%. Minority interest jumped sharply in Q4 (about 38% of PAT) due to an abnormal, pulled-forward MedTech sale at a partly-owned subsidiary, which management says will normalise. FY27 guidance is 23% consolidated revenue growth excluding new acquisitions (about 11 points from calendarisation), 5% EBITDA margin, and at least 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Now above INR1,000 crore annualised revenue after 3 MedTech acquisitions in FY26 (Anand Chemiceutics, Ace Cardiopathy, Bio de Technology). Management says MedTech is over 15% of revenue, could reach about 20% in 2-3 years, and earns higher margins than pharma due to commercial/agency role.

segments.name: Pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Remains the core business with about 100,000 retail pharmacies, 3,600 hospitals, 97,500 SKUs and 3,300+ manufacturers. Management expects pharma and MedTech to contribute equally to FY27 organic growth.

segments.name: GLP-1
segments.commentary: Management says current GLP-1 sales are about INR10-12 crore per month, roughly 5% of industry GLP value, with a share above its overall India share due to cold-chain warehouses; included in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23% YoY excluding new acquisitions; about 11 points from calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions and the rest organic (management also cited about 22% in one answer).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 5%, about 50 bps above Q4 FY26's 4.5%, from MedTech mix, operating leverage and exiting low-margin businesses.
EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion of at least 50% in FY27.
Tax rate of about 22-23% for FY27.
Minority interest to be about 25-27% of PAT before minority interest in FY27, down from about 38% in Q4.
Finance cost to stay relatively stable for a couple of quarters, then decline over the next couple of years as IPO funds were used up.
No new acquisitions assumed for the next 6-8 months; guidance would be revised upwards if acquisitions are made. Acquisitions are priced at 5-7x EV/EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Seven acquisitions closed in FY26, including 3 in MedTech; management says no new acquisitions are planned for the next 6-8 months, focusing on organic growth.
Some MedTech IVD machines are placed at customer sites on 5-year reagent rental contracts and are depreciated; cardiology and other MedTech lines carry little depreciating equipment.
Cold-chain facilities in all warehouses support GLP-1 distribution.
Depreciation rose about 50% QoQ in Q4, and interest costs rose because acquisitions were debt- or investment-funded after IPO proceeds were used up.
demand_pricing: Organic growth outperformed IPM by 1.6x for FY26 (15.6% vs IPM); Q3 and Q4 multiplier fell to about 1.4x as IPM grew about 12% versus 7-8% earlier, while organic growth stayed at 16-17%.
FY27 like-for-like growth is about 15% (1.5x IPM) per management; some low-ROIC businesses are being exited and some are now booked on a net-revenue basis, lowering reported revenue.
Gross margin gains come from scale purchasing and a commercial/agency role; full commercial role accounts for 10-15%+ of sales, with margins at least double normal distribution margins.
Management pointed to the 8-15% gross margin band on slide 28 for distribution; Q4 gross margin was 10.9%.

544133|2026-03.headline: Exicom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 388 crores and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR 0.3 crore for the first time since Tritium acquisition.
544133|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 282 crores with EBITDA of INR 29.9 crores (10.6% margin), driven by Critical Power (+23% YoY) and EVSE (+60% YoY). Consolidated revenue of INR 388 crores (+46% YoY) included Tritium, and consolidated EBITDA turned marginally positive. For full FY26, consolidated EBITDA was still negative at INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT was negative at INR 258 crores, with higher finance cost and one-time exceptional costs (VRS, Tritium retention, labour code). Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Hyderabad ramped up alongside Gurgaon.

segments.name: EVSE / EV charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 60% YoY in Q4 and 40% for FY26; record quarterly EV charging revenue of INR 88 crores (management figure, basis not specified). Full-year EVSE consolidated growth 72%; Q4 consolidated EVSE +83% YoY.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about $10 million (sales $9.7 million), record order intake $10 million; EBITDA losses down about 30% QoQ. Management targets ~3x revenue and 25% lower EBITDA losses, with EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tritium: revenue to scale about 3x and EBITDA losses to fall about 25%; EBITDA breakeven targeted in Q4 FY27. Management said losses fall less sharply than revenue because low-cost acquired inventory is being used up, with margins normalising after about one quarter.
Exports: target to lift Critical Power export share to 20% in FY27 from ~10-15%.
Non-telecom BESS: internal target of over INR 50 crores business in FY26 from pilot-stage orders; management sees BESS possibly reaching ~30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years if successful.

Three Tritium products (TRI-FLEX inverter and two others) launching May-July 2026; management cites about INR 850 crores of combined FY28 revenue potential, subject to pilots. TRI-FLEX hyperscaler factory acceptance test ongoing, potentially $30-35 million FY28 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What charging infrastructure is needed for commercial EV adoption and where is it happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is in fixed-route captive use such as ports, cement distribution and mining with 200-300 trucks; intercity commercial electrification is still about two years away.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product and revenue potential of the TRI-FLEX inverter and its applications?
qa_highlights.answer: TRI-FLEX converts grid power to high-voltage DC for DC microgrids, BESS integration and 800V data centres. A hyperscaler pilot is in testing and, if successful, could unlock significant FY28 revenue ($30-35 million cited).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development was done with existing strategic customers, and it has line of sight to long-term contracts once pilots succeed.

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Exicom is the largest home charger maker, with about a 50% chance a new EV in India comes with an Exicom charger, and it has OEM partnerships for home and fast chargers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets commercial and industrial modular BESS, not utility, transmission, distribution or home. About 10-20 small projects were deployed in Q4, with an FY26 target above INR 50 crores, and BESS could reach about 30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.

Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?

The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

544134|2026-03.headline: Platinum Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 132 crore, EBITDA up 95% to INR 15.3 crore; FY27 guidance above 40% revenue growth.

Full-year consolidated revenue was INR 450 crore (+15%), but EBITDA (INR 59.8 crore, +4.2%) and PAT (INR 51.2 crore, +3.7%) grew far slower. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 40% and a 35% CAGR over FY26-29, with the Egypt plant slated for Q3 FY27 and oleo chemicals sales starting April 2026. Raw-material inflation from the March geopolitical events created a temporary margin pressure that management expects to pass through over time.

544134|2026-06.headline: Platinum Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR 108.9 crore (from INR 115.4 crore) and PAT to INR 11.13 crore as Palghar ramp-up weighed.
544134|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue declined about 5.6% YoY to INR 108.9 crore while EBITDA fell to INR 13.44 crore at a 12.34% margin, versus INR 15.16 crore at 13.14% a year earlier. qa_highlights.answer: CPVC margin is about 18% now and management targets 20-21% by Q4 FY27. Recovery depends on demand, since supply currently exceeds demand, and on local raw material sourcing, which is adding cost.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Oleo target is INR 65-70 crore and the three-year target is INR 150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6,000 tpa stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026 from August due to a delay in one equipment item. Management said it would not materially affect FY27 revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

Capacity remains the focus, with the Dahej (Gujarat) plant due for commissioning in H1 FY27 and Naidupeta debottlenecking targeted for December 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on record revenue (INR315.7 cr, +44.8% YoY), margin structure and the Dahej ramp, but evasive on the size of the inventory gain, capex figures and TUR economics, which were deferred offline; analysts probed margin sustainability and the cut in Dahej FY28 utilisation.

544140|2026-03.headline: Gopal Snacks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 409.6 cr; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% with Rajkot plant fully commissioned.
544140|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 409.6 crore, up 29% YoY and 2.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 31.5 crore (7.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 29.9 crore (7.3% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 2.7% to Rs 1,508.2 crore, EBITDA was Rs 101.3 crore (6.7%) and PAT Rs 73.7 crore (4.9%). Management said supply was restored after the fire-related disruption, with Rajkot commissioned (installed capacity 1,05,000 MT) and the Modasa plant fully integrated. Insurance receipts reached about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26, with a further claim expected to be settled around Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 17.5 crore in Q4; about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26

segments.name: Gathiya
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 410 crore; FY27 growth target 18-20%. Management estimates Gujarat Gathiya industry growth at 15-20%.

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 350 crore; FY27 growth target 15%. Gujarat Namkeen industry growth estimated at 14-15%.

segments.name: Fryums / Pellets
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 250 crore; FY27 growth target 15%, in line with industry.

segments.name: Wafers
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 155 crore; FY27 growth target 40%.

segments.name: Others (papad, besan, spices, bakery, noodles, rusk)
segments.commentary: FY27 growth target of 30%. New products (kaju biscuit, popcorn) grew from Rs 25 crore to Rs 63 crore in FY26, with about Rs 50 crore of the Rs 38 crore delta from core states (as stated).

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% on an annualised average basis; exit run-rate expected near double digit.

FY27 incremental revenue target of Rs 330-350 crore: Rs 170-180 crore from core market (Gujarat), Rs 125-130 crore from focus states, Rs 35 crore from other states, quick commerce, railways and modern trade.
Advertisement spend projected at 2.2-2.3% of revenue in FY27 versus about 1.7% in FY26; trade spend cuts to be gradual, not major in FY27.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 40-45 crore, including a corporate office building at Rajkot; the rest is maintenance.
Finance cost expected to be slightly higher in FY27, about Rs 10 crore versus about Rs 7 crore in FY26.
Insurance balance claim expected to be Rs 35-40 crore (higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, as restatement cost exceeds WDV write-off), with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Rajkot plant commissioned; installed capacity 1,05,000 MT. Gondal facility to be discontinued.
Plant roles: Rajkot makes gathiya, namkeen, snack pellets and extruded snacks; Modasa makes all namkeen and wafers; Nagpur makes gathiya, namkeen, pellets and wafers.
Third-party manufacturing used in Kashipur (UP; four SKUs making 76-77% of UP sales) and Chhattisgarh (wafers only) to cut transport costs in those markets.
FY27 capacity utilisation expected at about 43-45%, per management in response to a question; Q4 utilisation near the full-year level shown on slide 11.
demand_pricing: Core market (Gujarat) run-rate about Rs 85-90 crore per month; about 300 distributors; line-wide coverage at 29% of beats on twice-a-week service by end-Q4, targeting 40% by end-Q1 FY27.
Focus states run-rate about Rs 400 crore annualised across 600 distributors; 65-70 dealers added in Q4 and 69 new distributors in Q4 against an annual target of 250.
Per-day run-rate has improved since March; Uttar Pradesh H2 was 26% above H1; monthly UP sales about Rs 6.5 crore with 72% from two SKUs, target exit Rs 8.5-9 crore.
Grammage cut of about 4% taken in mid-April 2026 on small packs, with price hikes on larger SKUs; further action depends on competitor response.
Raw material basket: palm oil 26-27%, chana 21-22%, laminate 18-19%, potato about 6%. RM inflation impact about 4-4.5% so far, largely offset by grammage cuts, price increases and BOM changes.
Chana stock sufficient to about November 2026; H2 purchases to be made from market or imports if cheaper.
Distributor count 953 at end-Q4 versus 884 at end-Q3; 97% of business through direct distributors; DMS live at 90% of dealers.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 top line shape up now that supply is restored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Rs 330-350 crore revenue delta in FY27: Rs 170-180 crore core Gujarat, Rs 125-130 crore focus states, Rs 35 crore other channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did focus states grow more slowly than core states in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Core states were hit harder by the fire, depleting the base. Q4 beat Q3 this year, reversing the usual 6-7% seasonal dip, and focus-state growth is expected to rebuild on distributor additions. Growth is expected at par near term and higher on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held the 8-9% average guidance, citing raw material volatility. Exit run-rate is expected near double digit. Trade spend will be cut only gradually, with no major cut in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much more insurance will be received?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance claim expected at Rs 35-40 crore, higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher chana inventory bought ahead of expected price rises raised bank borrowing. Receivable days rose by 9 days, but the working capital cycle is within the comfort zone.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut prices or pack sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: A 4% grammage cut was taken in mid-April 2026. Further action depends on how the industry responds.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation in palm oil and packaging (cited as 15-20% basket increase); H2 FY27 chana purchases exposed to pulse prices, with El Nino raising rain-deficit risk to rural demand.
Unorganised Rs 5 price-point players under pressure; no action seen yet. Industry pricing discipline may change.
Insurance balance claim timing (Q2 FY27 expected) and asset restatement progress.
Focus-state growth recovery and distributor additions versus the target of 250 for CY26.
Rising debt and finance cost (about Rs 10 crore expected in FY27) on higher inventory.
Trade spend and advertising step-up (2.2-2.3% of revenue) could compress margins if market-share recovery needs more spend.
544140|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and specific on recovery metrics, distributor adds and capacity; more cautious and hedged on margin drivers and raw material inflation, with the 8-9% margin guidance held despite analyst pressure to raise it. Some answers were vague on pricing and on how industry players will react.
key_quotes: Rigan Raithatha: Yes, next year for the margin front as we have been guiding, we still speak to the same guidance that is 8% to 9%.
Rigan Raithatha: So, as far as trade spend is concerned, we would be obviously looking on that front but that our reduction on the trade spend would be in a very gradual phase wise manner.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, exit run-rate near double digit
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% for FY27 versus 6.7% in FY26 and 7.7% in Q4 FY26, with exit run-rate near double digit; offset risks are ad spend rising to 2.2-2.3% of revenue from about 1.7% and 4-4.5% raw material inflation so far.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Rajkot already commissioned (installed 1,05,000 MT) and utilisation is only about 43-45% for FY27, so no new capacity is needed in the window; Gondal is being discontinued, not expanded.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets Rs 330-350 crore incremental revenue (about 22-23% on Rs 1,508 crore), with Gujarat run-rate Rs 85-90 crore per month, 953 distributors (up from 884), and 69 new focus-state distributors in Q4; no firm order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 43% (FY26 level, FY27 guided 43-45%) is far below the 80% threshold, and FY27 capex is held at Rs 40-45 crore, mostly maintenance plus a Rajkot corporate office.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 8-9% margin guidance despite analyst pressure to raise it, citing raw material volatility, and its revenue target is described as aspirational.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Palm oil (26-27% of basket), packaging and chana (21-22%) inflation, plus rising ad and trade spend, could compress the 8-9% margin if pricing does not hold; El Nino raises rural demand risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Others segment (papad, besan, spices, bakery, noodles, rusk) targets 30% growth, and kaju biscuit and popcorn grew from Rs 25 crore to Rs 63 crore in FY26, but no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.label: Insurance balance claim Rs 35-40 crore
rows.why: Management expects a balance claim of Rs 35-40 crore, above the Rs 10 crore gap, which would add a one-off cash inflow once received.

rows.label: Chana inventory and debt build
rows.why: Chana stock covers only to about November 2026 and bank borrowing rose on pre-bought inventory, with finance cost guided to about Rs 10 crore in FY27 from about Rs 7 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Focus-state and UP expansion
rows.why: Focus states run at about Rs 400 crore annualised across 600 distributors, UP H2 was 26% above H1, and the focus-state target is Rs 125-130 crore incremental in FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on distributor adds, supply recovery and the Rajkot capacity, but cautious on margin drivers and raw material inflation, holding 8-9% EBITDA guidance despite analyst pressure to raise it; analysts pushed on focus-state growth, pricing discipline and the margin outlook.

544140|2026-06.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
544140|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue from operations of INR 422.3 crore, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA more than doubled YoY to INR 31.5 crore (7.4% margin vs 4.7%), and PAT was INR 12.8 crore. Rajkot main facility restarted after the Gondal consolidation, though April saw about 5-6 working days of disruption (gas shortage and plant shift) that cost INR 12-13 crore of revenue in core markets. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ growth (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue) and 8-9% EBITDA margin with exit near double digits.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5.3 crore in Q1 FY26
No exceptional items in Q1; prior quarter had insurance gain, so QoQ not comparable
May and June at this level

segments.name: Core market (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Flat sequentially in Q1 due to April disruption that cost INR 12-13 crore; management targets INR 100-plus crore per month from here. Gathiya is the leading product, followed by namkeen, snack pellets and potato wafers; wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets. About 65% of Gujarat Gathiya market is still unorganised.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% YoY; 100% of UP top line comes from two SKUs, Champakali Gathiya and Papdi Gathiya.

segments.name: Focus and other states
segments.commentary: Focus-state distributors rose from 440 (Q1 FY26) to 530 (Q4 FY26) to 567 (Q1 FY27); other states rose from 110 to 129. Maharashtra distributors went 194 to 205 to 198, with focus on Marathwada and the Nagpur belt.

segments.name: Other snack products
segments.commentary: Revenue in the other snacks bucket went from about INR 10 crore last year to about INR 23-24 crore per quarter, including Shot Go noodles, rusks, wafer biscuits, wafer rolls, jeera biscuits and washing bar.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce was INR 2.79 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26. Modern trade was flat at INR 1.85 crore.

segments.name: Nagpur plant
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation is below 30%; 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, of which about 60 have moved to Modasa for logistics reasons. Third-party units at Kashipur (about INR 2 crore per month) and Manendragarh support other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,800-1,900 crore (20%+ growth), reaffirmed; management says it has held the stance on 20%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin 8-9% for the full year, with exit run rate near double digits.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% with exit near 11%; sustainable target 11-11.5%; average reaching that level around mid-FY28-29.
FY28 PAT margin around 7-7.5%; minimum 20% revenue CAGR over the medium term.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss expected in Q2 FY27; management says documents are submitted.
Seven NPIs planned across Q2 and Q3, five of them non-palm-oil with better margins; 6 lakh outlets targeted by end of CY2026 (from 5.25-5.5 lakh).
capex_capacity: Rajkot main facility restarted; production consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, with expected savings in power, fuel, logistics and operating costs as utilisation improves.
Modasa and Nagpur plants contribute to the network; Nagpur utilisation is below 30%.
Double-service coverage now reaches 38% of outlets; run rate up 14-25% where it has been rolled out. Pilot of ARS (auto replenishment) started; DMS covers most of the distributor network.
Retail touchpoints on DMS at 4.24 lakh; another 60-70k outlets are served but not on DMS.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation was 5% in Q1; 4.2% passed on through price hikes and grammage cuts, 0.8% absorbed in P&L. Another 0.2-0.3% hit is pending and will be passed through.
Q2 inflation is slightly lower than 100 bps additional, per management.
Management says the company now runs at par or lower grammage than competitors and relies on distribution automation rather than grammage to drive volume.
Management expects roughly 75-80% of growth from volume and about 20% from price in the rest of FY27.
Chana stored till Q3-end; potato stored; palm oil and laminate are bought from the market with no major near-term increase foreseen.
INR 5 price point remains about 60% of sales (down from ~80% in FY22); management says no visible industry shift.
Regional brands in core states (Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari) remain present; Miraj and Star brands shut, and Miraj has restarted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 330-350 crore FY27 incremental revenue guidance still intact, and what is the festive run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is INR 150 crore+ per month, April was lower due to the Gondal to Rajkot shift, and 20%+ growth guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable target is 11-11.5%. FY27 exit near double digits, FY28 exit near 11%, and an average of that level around mid-FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core market run rate target and how is the Gujarat business growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of INR 100-plus crore per month in core markets. Double service is being scaled up, and more products are planned to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the A&P and trade spend trends?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P was about 1% of sales in Q1 against a 2.2% annualised budget; trade discount is 2.5% of sales versus about 3.5% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Nagpur utilisation below 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, about 60 were moved to Modasa for logistics, and the 250-distributor-a-year addition is below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an FMCG business with no order book, and daily run rate is steady with no month-end billing.

risks_watch: April disruption (gas shortage at Gondal plus Gondal-to-Rajkot shift) cost INR 12-13 crore of core-market revenue; watch whether May-June run rate of INR 150 crore+ per month holds and core Gujarat reaches the INR 100-plus crore per month target.

Raw material inflation: 0.8% of 5% Q1 inflation absorbed in P&L, another 0.2-0.3% pending pass-through, and management said Q2 inflation could be slightly below 100 bps additional; margin delivery depends on further price hikes and grammage cuts.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss is expected in Q2 FY27 from a PSU insurer; timing has slipped before and any delay affects reported profit.
Nagpur plant utilisation below 30% for over two to three years, with about 60 of 159 mapped distributors moved to Modasa; distributor additions below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

Execution of FY27 guidance (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue, 8-9% EBITDA) and FY28 ramp to 10-11% depends on Rajkot savings, double-service coverage (38% of outlets) and seven NPIs in Q2-Q3, five non-palm-oil.

Competitive intensity: management says it now runs at par or lower grammage than peers, and A&P is about 1% of sales versus a 2.2% annualised budget, so any step-up in spend ahead of festive season could move margins.
key_quotes: So we strongly stand by our earlier guidance given of, you know, minimum 20% growth in this financial year over last year.
As of now, we are either at par or we are giving lesser grammage versus competition, but still we are able to maintain our revenue momentum because distribution automation is helping us a lot
So from May onwards, there is 0% disturbance in terms of operations.
So, we are FMCG company, Adarsh-Bhai, and typically we are not B2B company.
544140|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and the 20%+ growth and 8-9% EBITDA guidance, which management reaffirmed several times. More cautious and less specific on the April disruption, Nagpur utilisation, Maharashtra distributor count and the insurance claim timing, where answers were partial and follow-ups were promised.

544144|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue up ~28% YoY and FY26 EBITDA up 16% to INR203.4 crore, but FY26 reported PAT still a loss of INR12.5 crore.
544144|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 28% YoY and total income reached INR1,758.8 crore (up 27.8%), with EBITDA of INR57.5 crore (margin about 3.3%) and a loss of INR5 crore versus INR13.7 crore loss a year earlier. FY26 total income was INR6,401.1 crore (up 15.1%) and reported EBITDA INR203.4 crore (margin 3.2%), while PAT was a loss of INR12.5 crore against INR10.5 crore loss in FY25. Management said the FY26 revenue and EBITDA were hit by acquisition costs, a cess provision and the new labour code impact, and it apologised for an error in the April 17, 2026 business update that misstated Q4 growth figures. Management guides FY27 to high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 4.8-5%, with sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR13.7 crore in Q4 FY25
up 28% YoY, after adjusting Honda/Piaggio divestment, acquisition impact and one-off provision

financial_highlights.value: loss of INR13 crore (before exceptional items loss of INR27 crore on reported basis)
financial_highlights.change: adjusted PBT loss about INR5 crore; adjusted PBT before exceptional items positive INR8.8 crore
vs loss of INR10.5 crore in FY25
up 19% YoY; organic INR4,493 crore, up 16%
up 7% YoY; organic INR868 crore, up 8%

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 8,090 units (up 20%), income INR654 crore (up 18%). FY26 volumes 32,572 units (up 9%), income INR2,551 crore (up 9%). Management cited entry-level supply shortages and OEM supply constraints in Keralam.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 1,80,989 units (down 14%), income INR154 crore (up 2%). FY26 service income INR607 crore (down 2%) with volumes 7,39,794 (down 12%); ASP growth offset the volume decline.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 3,716 units (up 59%), income INR645 crore (up 46%). FY26 volumes 12,546 units (up 30%), income INR2,125 crore (up 32%); BharatBenz Punjab acquisition contributed.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 52,443 units (up 13%), income INR97 crore (up 75%). FY26 volumes 2,02,647 (up 10%), income INR351 crore (up 28%).

segments.name: EV (Ather 2-wheelers) new and services
segments.commentary: Q4 new vehicles 3,079 units (up 138%), income INR50 crore (up 113%); service volumes 11,261 (up 81%), income about INR3 crore. FY26 new vehicles 8,154 units (up 89%), income INR137 crore (up 72%); service volumes 39,659 (up 79%), income about INR9 crore (up 18%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin moving to about 4.8-5%; PAT approaching FY24 levels.
Sustainable profitability expected from Q2 FY27; Q1 FY27 still expected to be loss-making due to Maruti and JLR supply constraints.
PV service volumes guided to grow at least 10-12% in FY27, with ASP growth of about 12-13%; CV service volumes guided up 7-8% with ASP up 8-10%.
Standalone sales margin guided at about 3-4% in FY27; spare parts margin guided back to 5.5-6% with revenue growth of 6-8% (ex-BKT).
JLR volume guidance of 550-600 vehicles in FY27 after about 380 Audi/JLR volume shortfall in FY26 (guided about 450); Audi expected to break even this year.
Non-Keralam revenue share to exceed 50% in FY27 from about 47% in FY26; no high-value acquisitions planned in FY27, focus on consolidating FY26 acquisitions.
Inventory to be held at or below 30 days for passenger cars; debt increase attributed to acquisitions, with ~INR520 crore of INR600+ crore debt inventory-linked.
capex_capacity: Three acquisitions in FY26: BharatBenz dealership in Punjab, Maruti Suzuki dealership in Telangana, and Audi dealership operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; Honda and Piaggio businesses divested (volumes counted to August 2025).
JLR Nagpur operations commenced April 1, 2026; new Maruti touchpoints and multiple Ather touchpoints opened in Q4.
Bank loan facilities increased from INR468 crore to INR643 crore; CRISIL A/Stable rating extended to March 2027.
Management said capex spends will be more monitored and no additional debt is planned beyond what is needed to run the current business.
Acquired Audi and Telangana assets totalled about INR85-90 crore of equipment and showroom assets, with acquisition cost approximately equal.
demand_pricing: Management said demand improved in H2 FY26 after GST reforms in September 2025, with stronger footfall, conversion and entry-level recovery; discounting moderated.
Shortages of entry-level vehicles in Jan-Mar 2026 eased in April-May; Baleno and Fronx have waiting periods.
Post OEM price increases, management reported no noticeable change in demand so far; some pre-ponement of bookings was seen.
Luxury segment: Q4 delayed by UK FTA price-cut expectation; price cuts applied to Range Rover SP and Autobiography, with bookings rising from April.
Service volume: running repair fell about 17-18% as the company deprioritised low-value jobs; collision repair volumes flat; free service volumes recovered in last 6 months.
Maruti share of service volumes about 65-70%; Maruti service volume decline narrowed from -7% (to Q3) to -2% in Q4.
Overall Maruti ASP up about 13% YoY; PV new vehicle weighted ASP up to about 6.5% from about 5.5% three years earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did service volumes fall and what service volume and ASP growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 service volumes fell about 6% and ASP rose about 14%, with revenue up over 8%. For FY27 it guided 10-12% PV service volume growth and matching ASP growth; CV service volume growth of 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the service EBITDA margin gap versus peers close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated margin will not reach 18% because of CV and Ather mix, but the Passenger Car business should reach 18-19% service margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone margins move from about 3% to 5% consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin drag to acquisitions and Telangana expansion; growth is to come from PV service volumes and ASP, plus JLR and Audi ramp-up, with consolidated EBITDA guided to 4.8-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add acquisitions and how will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: No high-value acquisitions planned in FY27. About INR520 crore of the INR600+ crore debt is inventory-linked; term loans will be repaid on schedule, and debt will fall if inventory release generates free cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory under control and what is the demand reaction to OEM price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 49 to 36 (FY25 to FY26); management aims to keep it below 30 days. Post price hikes, demand was flat and supply has normalised in April-May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn sustainably profitable and what happened in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27. Q1 remains affected by Maruti and JLR supply constraints; service volumes expected to grow Q1 over Q1.

risks_watch: Reported FY26 PAT loss of INR12.5 crore; Telangana loss of about INR26-27 crore and cess provision weigh on profitability, with Ind AS depreciation on acquisitions.
Debt rose after acquisitions; management says inventory debt is about INR520 crore of INR600+ crore total, with inventory days to stay below 30.
Error in April 17, 2026 business update, which misstated Q4 revenue growth; management apologised and promised process fixes.
CEO Raj Narayan has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the industry; successor not named on this call.
JLR cyber-attack and supply constraints cost about INR70 crore of top line and INR8-9 crore of bottom line in FY26; Q1 FY27 supply still constrained.
Service volumes in running repair down 17-18%; management needs to show Q1 FY27 volume growth.
Fuel price and geopolitical uncertainty (referred to as a war situation) flagged as demand risks.
key_quotes: Before moving to the business performance, I would like to sincerely apologize for the error in the business update published on April 17 , 2026, for the quarter and the year ended March 31 , 2026, and take this opportunity to clarify the same.
Post the price increase announcement by the OEMs, we have not seen much of a change actually.
In terms of profitability from Q2 of FY '27, we should be having sustainable profitability.
Out of the INR600 odd crores, around INR520 crores is related to the debt on inventory.
544144|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery post GST reforms, FY27 guidance and the Q2 FY27 profitability timeline. Cautious and defensive on standalone margins, acquisition losses (Telangana, Audi), debt levels and the April 17 business update error, which management apologised for repeatedly. Evasive on successor CEO and on exact Q1 FY27 profitability, which it framed only as loss-making.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Guided consolidated EBITDA margin to about 4.8-5% in FY27 versus 3.2% reported in FY26, with sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27 and PV service margin targeted at 18-19%, though standalone sales margin is guided only 3-4% and Q1 FY27 remains loss-making.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: JLR Nagpur operations commenced April 1, 2026 and new Maruti and Ather touchpoints opened in Q4, but these are minor dealership adds with no capacity size or capex figures disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27, with Q1 FY27 still constrained
rows.why: Guided PV service volumes up 10-12%, CV service up 7-8% and JLR volumes of 550-600 versus about 380 shortfall in FY26; FY26 service volumes fell 6% to 9.82 lakh and Q1 FY27 supply remains constrained by Maruti and JLR.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex will be more monitored, no additional debt beyond current business needs, and no high-value acquisitions in FY27, with debt above INR600 crore and about INR520 crore of it inventory-linked.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of high double-digit top-line growth and 4.8-5% EBITDA margin is new and ambitious versus FY26 margin of 3.2%, and FY26 PAT was still a loss of INR12.5 crore, so upgrades look unlikely in the near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 is guided loss-making due to Maruti and JLR supply constraints (JLR cyber-attack cost about INR70 crore of top line in FY26), Telangana losses of about INR26-27 crore and fuel/geopolitical demand risks could delay the Q2 FY27 profitability timeline.

rows.label: Sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27
rows.why: Management guided sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27 after FY26 reported PAT loss of INR12.5 crore and Q4 FY26 loss of INR5 crore, with Audi guided to break even this year.

rows.label: Inventory days to stay at or below 30
rows.why: Inventory days fell from 49 (FY25) to 36 (FY26), and management targets below 30 days for passenger cars, with about INR520 crore of INR600+ crore debt inventory-linked.

rows.why: Total debt is above INR600 crore, with term loans repaid on schedule and debt to fall only if inventory release generates free cash; no timing or amount given.

544144|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
544144|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (ex-luxury)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR836 crore (+73% YoY reported, +54% excluding luxury per call); new vehicles 10,475 units (+83%); service volumes 1,90,801 (-5%) while service income INR169 crore (+11%). Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.
New vehicle inventory ~32 days vs ~50 days a year ago; absolute inventory up only ~14% YoY despite higher revenue; sequential build ahead of festive season and OEM launches.
Audi inventory elevated, expected to fall to ~20-25 days in August-September.
Ather inventory ~5 days, JLR supply somewhat constrained.
Keralam revenue share fell below 50% for the first time (49%), state mix: Tamil Nadu 22%, Karnataka 12%, Telangana 8%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 4%, Andhra Pradesh 0.3%.
demand_pricing: Pre-festive inquiries up ~20% YoY over recent days, ~17-18% over the last month; bookings up ~22% YoY.
Keralam inauspicious period ends 16 August; retail expected to pick up from 17 August (Onam-Chingam).
CV demand weak in construction: tipper segment low to negative growth; SCV and cargo holding.
Maruti price increases modest (INR5,000-7,000 for most models; INR10,000-15,000 for some), with no major impact on demand or margin.
Entry-level cars recovered: Alto K10 and WagonR strong; S-Presso slowing; Arena returned to growth.
Spare parts short supply in the market, causing vehicles to stay in workshops.
Running repairs up ~8.8% in July; free service turned to growth in Q1.
Commercial ticket size ~INR16-17 lakh is pulling blended margin down.

qa_highlights.question: How are inquiries and bookings trending into the festive period, and what is the H2 FY27 growth outlook for PV, CV and EV?
qa_highlights.answer: Inquiries up about 20% YoY over recent days and 17-18% over the last month; bookings up about 22% YoY. Keralam is in an inauspicious period until 16 August, with retail expected to pick up from 17 August. PV H2 growth running about 80-90% YoY in most months, likely to moderate on high base; Q3 seen as key with Audi launch. CV construction demand weak (tipper low to negative), SCV and cargo holding.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin move toward 4-5%, and how will the acquisitions' turnaround affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% will take a long time because CV mix is rising (average CV ticket ~INR16-17 lakh). Blended margin hoped to reach ~4% and ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% not expected unless mix changes considerably. Acquired businesses are EBITDA-positive in aggregate at ~INR9.4 crore; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end Q3, Olympus possibly one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the INR11.2 crore adjusted PBT vs INR1.9 crore reported PBT?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is acquisition effects: acquisitions contributed ~INR9.4 crore EBITDA (Globe ~INR2.1 crore, RKS ~INR7.4 crore, Olympus neutral), offset by ~INR12 crore depreciation and ~INR6.8 crore finance cost. At PBT, RKS was about negative INR5.3 crore and Olympus about negative INR4 crore; Globe roughly neutral.

qa_highlights.question: What are the segment margins, ex-acquisitions, for PV and Luxury?
qa_highlights.answer: JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA roughly nil, dragging luxury margin. PV EBITDA about 4% now, up from INR9.4 crore to about INR35 crore on Maruti, with Honda a negative INR4.2 crore in Q1. Maruti margin ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at the model level, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Service volume guidance: is the 10-12% growth target on track after PV service volumes fell 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer expects 15%; PV service volume growth guided at ~6-7% from Q2 as Honda base drops out. Maruti service volumes up ~8% YoY, expected to reach double digit from Q2. Service ASP up ~15% in PV; Maruti ASP INR6.6 lakh to 6.7 lakh and JLR INR1.07 crore to INR1.26 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is new vehicle sales business profitable after interest cost, and what is the split of the INR30 crore finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Maruti sales EBITDA ~1.7% (vs about -2% a year ago), ~0.85% after interest; JLR ~5%; TCV/BharatBenz ~3% with interest under 1%; Ather ~4.2% with negligible interest. Split of the ~INR30 crore finance cost was not given on the call; to be emailed to the analyst.

PV service volume recovery to ~6-7% growth from Q2 (vs earlier 10-12%/15% guidance) and running repairs reaching growth in Q2; spare parts short supply keeping vehicles in workshops.

Debt higher YoY from FY26 acquisitions; finance cost ~INR30 crore and below-EBITDA depreciation (~INR12 crore in Q1) continue to hold reported PBT near breakeven.
Audi inventory elevated (expected to fall to ~20-25 days in Aug-Sep) and Audi margin at nil until Q3 launches; JLR supply constrained and Ather inventory ~5 days.
CV construction demand weak (tipper low to negative); Keralam market sentiment tied to Onam-Chingam timing; leadership transition as CEO Raj Narayan departs after August 2026.
key_quotes: So we might not inch to 5% this year, though the focus is to build that up. We will be closer to about 4.3%, 4.4% this year at the end of it.
But in terms of volume, we are hoping to grow from Q2 onwards. July numbers have come in pretty strong in terms of growth. So we're hoping to maintain that.

544149|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 12% YoY to INR364.94 crore on selective bidding, while PAT rose 11% to INR18.85 crore; FY26 consolidated order book is about INR2,500 crore+.
544149|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR364.94 crore, down nearly 12% YoY but up 19% QoQ, as management deliberately skipped low-margin bids. EBITDA excluding other income fell 11% YoY to INR23.78 crore, yet margin edged up 3 bps to 6.51% and PAT grew over 11% YoY to INR18.85 crore. For FY26, revenue rose 5.32% to INR1,277.28 crore, EBITDA rose 7.5% to INR83.53 crore (6.54% margin), and PAT was INR64.35 crore (up nearly 3%). Management guided to upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth in FY27 and announced the 100% acquisition of Citelum India, its first acquisition, for smart lighting and urban infrastructure.

financial_highlights.change: increased during year; management expects meaningful reduction

segments.name: Government business
segments.commentary: Management is being more selective in bidding; 2 new contracts in Q4 FY26 and 17 for the full year. Mix was about 70:30 government to corporate, with a stated aim to rebalance toward corporate.

segments.name: Corporate business
segments.commentary: Management says corporate margin profile has improved since the pandemic. Management cited 177+ new customers and 250+ new sites added in FY26, with INR300 crore of multi-year new business value.

segments.name: Waste management
segments.commentary: Currently managing more than 350 TPD. Qualification allows bids for about 480-500 TPD by fiscal year-end, with a target of 800-1,000 TPD over 18 months. Vasai Virar MSW win was among top 3 qualifying agencies with technology partner MTS.

segments.name: Citelum India (acquisition)
segments.commentary: Board approved 100% acquisition of Citelum India Pvt Ltd from Citelum S.A.S. (EDF Group). Company is in smart lighting, street lighting, and city O&M, with smart city presence in Ahmedabad, Noida and Chennai. Financial terms and closing timeline were not disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Taskmaster (B2C)
segments.commentary: Start-up B2C residential deep-cleaning platform with FY26 revenue of about INR46 lakh. Management expects traction to begin from Q2 FY27 and will not give a 2-3 year revenue guidance yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth.
Margin appreciation expected, led by corporate mix and higher-margin emerging verticals.
Management says the INR180 crore of business skipped on margin grounds and delayed government decisions will shift into FY27.
Waste management qualification target of 800-1,000 TPD over the next 18 months.
Working capital and loans/advances expected to normalise as new contracts reach steady state.
capex_capacity: Waste management capacity: more than 350 TPD currently; qualified for about 480-500 TPD by end of FY27; target of 800-1,000 TPD over 18 months.
Workforce of over 41,676 on-site staff, with a shift toward skilled and semi-skilled manpower to support higher-value pricing.
Pan-India network of 31 branches, serving 570+ customers across 4,000+ locations.
Bioenzyme waste treatment remains in pilot (Mira-Bhayandar, Vasai Virar) with VPRC Chennai; no commercial cost set yet.
Rooftop solar PV project for government hospitals and medical colleges in Maharashtra marks entry into renewables. No capex quantum disclosed.
demand_pricing: Consolidated order book is about INR2,500 crore+ at 31 March 2026 (about INR2,600 crore cited in Q&A over full contract tenure); standalone order book is about INR1,220 crore.
RFP participation rose from 5-6 corporate RFPs in FY24/FY25 to about 30-31 in FY26.

Key wins: MSEDCL substation O&M (33 kV and below), airport FM at Patna and Vijayawada, Tamil Nadu 167 government hospitals FM, 25 AP government hospitals sanitation, Vasai Virar MSW, Maersk, Fortis, Livspace, Indira IVF, Adani hospitals.
Management says it wins corporate deals against CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo by offering direct service delivery rather than outsourced services.
Q4 revenue decline attributed to about INR180 crore of business not bid for on margin grounds, plus tender decisions pending from previous fiscal.

qa_highlights.question: How does Krystal differentiate from global players such as CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo in large corporate mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the services are similar but Krystal is the direct service provider, while global players are property managers that outsource services. Many new customers were won against these players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year vision and business mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebalancing the government/corporate mix from about 70:30 by adding corporates, with government growth in waste management, O&M and city infrastructure. Management aims to be a diversified player with all verticals revenue-making and profitable within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue has Taskmaster contributed and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue was about INR46 lakh. Pilots are ongoing and traction is expected from Q2 FY27, but no 2-3 year revenue guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What quantifies the Q4 revenue drop of 11.7% YoY, and is it due to exits, slower orders or tender delays?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR180 crore of business was not bid for to protect margins, and some government tender decisions are pending, which pushed business into later periods. Management says the order book covers this and the shortfall will be made up in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for commercialising bioenzyme technology?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the technology is still in pilot with VPRC Chennai in Mira-Bhayandar and Vasai Virar, and no commercial cost or revenue timeline has been set yet.

risks_watch: Government tender decision delays could keep revenue shifting between quarters; the company says INR180 crore was deferred.
Working capital is stretched: receivables and loans/advances rose during FY26 to INR146.45 crore, and normalisation is not yet evidenced.

Citelum acquisition: deal value, funding, closing timeline and integration risk were not disclosed on the call.
Waste management scale-up to 800-1,000 TPD and bioenzyme commercialisation are still early-stage or unproven.
