544150|2026-03.headline: KP Green Engineering FY26 revenue rose 78% to INR1,250 crore and EBITDA 117% to INR249 crore, with INR1,831 crore order book slated for FY27 execution.
544150|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue of INR1,250 crore (up 78%), EBITDA of INR249 crore (up 117%, margin ~20% vs 16%) and PAT of INR136 crore (up 85%). H2 FY26 consolidated total income was INR714 crore (up 64% YoY) with PAT of INR77 crore (up 68%). Capacity utilisation remained low at about 30-34% on 4,00,500 MTPA capacity, with management guiding to 40-60% in FY27. Working capital rose sharply on inventory build-up tied to geopolitical fuel and raw material risk, and short-term borrowings increased. Management reiterated 40-50% annual growth and a 16-20% EBITDA margin range for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +117% YoY vs INR115 crore; margin from 16%

segments.name: Telecom (BSNL)

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book INR1,800 crore plus INR500 crore, and when will it execute?
qa_highlights.answer: Total order book including the INR500 crore is about INR1,800 crore as on date, and the entire book is to be executed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY26 capacity utilisation and FY27 outlook? What is the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 utilisation was 1,24,500 MT of 4,00,500 MTPA. FY27 growth minimum 40-50%; EBITDA margin to be kept in 16-20% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise from about 96 to 195 days and what happened to cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up as a hedge against geopolitical price and availability risk, using working capital limits. Cash fell because FDs over one year were reclassified to other financial assets (around INR59 crore FY26 vs INR52 crore FY25); operating cash flow was INR155 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt rising and is the company planning to become debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase is mainly short-term working capital; long-term debt has not risen. Average cost 8.5-9%, rated A. No plan to become debt-free currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why are related-party royalties charged at 2% and what is the cricket sponsorship?
qa_highlights.answer: Royalty at 2% of top line is paid for group brand building that is done by the promoter; cricket sponsorship is brand-level and is expensed by the promoter, not the company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cable and conductor plan, and will revenue come from outside the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable and conductor is aimed primarily at external power and transmission customers, with group supply as a secondary use.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to quarterly reporting, and when is Main Board migration?
qa_highlights.answer: Half-yearly reporting is mandatory; management will review quarterly reporting with the board. Main Board listing to follow once SEBI criteria are met.

risks_watch: Working capital and inventory: inventory days rose sharply to about 195 days; utilisation of working capital limits is fully drawn.
Fuel and gas supply for galvanizing and machinery under geopolitical stress; management says it is the main execution concern.
Margin dependence on raw material pass-through; only contracts above 5% escalation are passed on and other contracts rely on inventory hedging.
Related-party royalty at 2% of revenue paid to promoter-linked entity; group orders 20-25% of order book.
Revenue visibility depends on conversion of pipeline (INR2,000-3,000 crore) and on LOA timing versus win disclosure.
Reporting: only half-yearly results; cash and other financial asset reclassification may confuse comparability.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to commit beyond 40-50% growth ('no upper limit if capacity allows' but declined to commit to 100%), and the margin range is held at 16-20% with pass-through only above 5% escalation, so there is no clear basis for raising guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged fuel and gas supply under geopolitical stress as the main execution concern, inventory days rose from about 96 to 195, and working capital limits are fully drawn, so the 40-50% growth or 16-20% margin guide could slip if fuel or raw-material costs spike.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cable and conductor, aluminium extrusion, fasteners, containers and offshore tubular towers are in the pipeline, but none has a date or size, and the rolling mill is described as nascent.

rows.label: INR1,800+ crore order book fully executed in FY27
rows.why: Management confirmed the entire INR1,800+ crore book (INR1,831 crore at 31 March 2026 including INR500 crore won around 1 May 2026) is to be executed in FY27, with bidding pipeline above INR3,000 crore at a 60-70% success ratio.

rows.label: Inventory build-up and fully drawn working capital limits
rows.why: Inventory days rose from about 96 to 195 and the cash conversion cycle is around 150 days, with working-capital limits fully drawn; a release of inventory would help cash, but management gave no quantified plan.

rows.label: Main Board migration and quarterly reporting
rows.why: Half-yearly reporting is mandatory and quarterly reporting is only under board review; Main Board listing follows once SEBI criteria are met, with no date given.

tone.note: Management was confident on order visibility (INR1,800+ crore to execute in FY27) and 40-50% growth, but cautious on margin (held at 16-20%), fuel and gas supply, and inventory build-up (days from 96 to 195), and declined to quantify capex size or commit to 100% growth; analysts probed the order-boo

544158|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 96% YoY to INR446 crore and FY26 PAT rose 102% to INR111 crore; FY27 guided to 45-55% revenue growth.
544158|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR446 crore (+96% YoY), EBITDA of INR80 crore (+96%) and PAT of INR54 crore-equivalent growth of 120%, with FY26 revenue of INR1,026 crore (+94%), EBITDA of INR95 crore (8.1% margin) and PAT of INR111 crore (+102%). Order book was stated at about INR1,884 crore at March 2026, with management later citing about INR3,000 crore in hand as of the call date and a FY27 bid pipeline of about INR6,000 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 45-55%, EBITDA margin of 16-18% and PAT margin around 11%. Several answers were inconsistent on figures (order book scope, PAT margin, guidance ranges), and the reclassification of expenses across quarters drew repeated analyst questions.

INR111 crore, PAT margin stated as 10.8%

Order book expected to be around INR4,000 crore by end FY27 per management, and about INR6,000 crore including execution, with revenue around INR3,000 crore in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did COGS jump sharply in Q4 FY26, and are the high Q2/Q3 gross margins sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book execution timeline, and what is the difference between INR1,800 crore and INR3,000 crore?

The INR3,000 crore is order book in hand, all unexecuted, to be executed over about two years; the INR1,800 crore is the March 31 figure. INR6,000 crore pipeline conversion is expected at 60-70%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahajan said the increase is equipment financing: INR130 crore of the INR152 crore FY26 fixed-asset additions was debt-funded, for mobilisation on new and old projects. Management said debt is project-specific and is repaid when the project moves out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for debt and equity funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex of about INR250 crore will be funded by equipment debt, and the rest from internal accruals. qa_highlights.question: Why were some Q4 orders not notified to the exchanges?

qa_highlights.question: What is the clarification on the reclassification of expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the change of auditor led to reclassification of wages and subcontractor costs between COGS and other expenses; FY26 numbers are restated on a consistent basis. Other expenses of INR68 crore for FY26 comprise INR48 crore operational and INR16 crore admin expenses (as stated).

risks_watch: Gross margin volatility: Q4 gross margin of about 21% vs 53-54% in Q2/Q3; reclassification of expenses across quarters makes quarterly comparisons less reliable.

544161|2026-03.headline: D.P. Abhushan Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87% YoY to INR1,338.9 crore, with PAT up 101% to INR50.6 crore; FY26 PAT INR211.8 crore (+88%).
544161|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,338.9 crore (+87% YoY), EBITDA INR73 crore (+72%, margin 5.45%) and PAT INR50.6 crore (+101%, margin 3.78%). For FY26, revenue grew 23% to INR4,070.3 crore, EBITDA rose 77% to INR309.7 crore (margin 7.61%, +234 bps) and PAT rose 88% to INR211.8 crore (margin 5.20%, +180 bps). Growth was mainly value-led, with volumes down about 20% per management. The QIP has been put on hold due to market conditions, and expansion has been slowed to 5-6 stores in FY27 from earlier guidance.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in full-year terms; diamond declined ~5% YoY

segments.name: Gold
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 gold revenue grew ~80% YoY and was the primary growth driver; FY26 gold revenue was INR3,702 crore (+~21%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of around 20%+ targeted; management cites wedding demand and old gold exchange; FY27 revenue planned at ~INR4,800 crore and FY28 at ~INR5,500 crore (per Q&A).
EBITDA margin guidance of 6%-6.5% for FY27; gross margin expected at ~10%-11%.
FY30 EBITDA margin vision of 8%-8.5%, via product mix, hedging, GML and leasing, plus store maturity.
Long-term topline growth target of ~25%-30% annually through FY30 (by end-2030).
Store network target of ~51 stores by 2030; FY27 openings now 5-6 stores if conditions allow, possibly 3-4 on a conservative basis; some expansion may slip by one or two quarters.
Omni-channel to contribute 3%-5% of revenue over the next 3-5 years, with an incremental INR25-30 crore annual profit.
QIP on hold; equity raise of 5%-8% dilution considered later, with promoter holding post-dilution at ~65%-68% from ~75%.
Management says Q1 FY27 may beat the INR36 crore standalone profit from Q1 FY25 ("We are trying").

Old gold exchange is 35%-40% of sales; new stores (Ajmer, Neemuch, Ratlam, Dhar) contribute 12%-15% of the business.
April to mid-May demand described as good before the PM's comments on gold spending; management expects June-July to be seasonally weaker, with recovery from Raksha Bandhan.
Silver demand seen as intact and shifting from gold; the company is bullish across gold, diamond and silver.
Competition from Titan and Kalyan viewed as healthy; the company positions itself as a regional player with customer depth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin compression?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to gold price volatility from geopolitical factors; FY26 gross margin ~10% vs ~7.72% in FY25, up ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Will GML and hedging affect steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there may be a slight margin impact, but GML, futures and leasing should help working capital and gradually lower finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Demand in April and May?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth was good in April and mid-May, before the PM's comments, with no pressure at showrooms and walk-ins continuing.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was mostly value-led; volumes fell ~20%; SSG ~20% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the FY26 and FY27 store and revenue guidance numbers revised down, and is the QIP the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is unchanged but the pace has slowed; some expansion may slip 1-2 quarters because of the PM's comments; long-term ~50-51 stores by 2030 remains.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory days at ~100 and what is normal?

544161|2026-06.headline: D.P. Abhushan Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR853.6 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR64 crore, but volume growth was only about 1-2%.
544161|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 58% YoY to INR853.63 crore, with EBITDA up 70% to INR93.99 crore and margin up 80 bps to 11.01%. PAT rose 77% to INR64 crore (7.55% margin). Management attributed most of the growth to higher gold prices and making charges rather than volume, with volume growth of about 1-2%. Expansion was briefly moderated in May after the gold import duty hike, and management says it has now returned to an aggressive expansion mode with a target of about 10% volume growth for FY27 and FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +58% YoY vs INR541 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Gold
segments.commentary: Revenue INR781 crore, up 59% YoY; management said only 10-15% of growth came from inventory gains and most of the rest from higher making charges.

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crore, up 150% YoY from INR16 crore, described as a fast-growing category.

segments.name: Diamond / studded
segments.commentary: Revenue INR29 crore vs INR31 crore a year ago (down about 6%). Studded mix is 6-7% of sales; target 12-15% by March 2028, with diamond business targeted at 2x-3x current levels.

segments.name: Product category mix
segments.commentary: Wedding-related purchases 62% of sales, festive and lightweight 18%, and gifts/other 20%.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth target of approximately 10% for both FY27 and FY28 (internal planning target).
Store network target of 51 stores by FY30 (vs about 12 currently), with roughly 5-6 new stores planned in FY27 and 6-8 per year thereafter.
Internal store mix target: about 5-7 COCO-to-FOCO split indicated as 6-7 COCO and 1-2 FOCO in one answer, while another answer said 5-7 FOCO; the mix was not clearly consistent.
Studded share targeted to reach 12-15% of overall sales by March 2028.
Management expects gradual volume improvement in FY27 as gold prices settle, and festive sales from August to be disclosed.
capex_capacity: New showrooms finalised at Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh, about 3,750 sq ft, first FOCO store, franchisee-owned company-operated) and Dahod (Gujarat, about 3,200 sq ft, COCO, entry into Gujarat); fit-out underway and openings expected soon.
Two new locations already finalised, two more under planning, and 2-3 more expected to be finalised by end of July 2026.

Store formats: small-to-medium at 3,000-5,000 sq ft and large at 8,000-10,000 sq ft; management cited breakeven in 6-9 months and mature turnover of INR150-200 crore (small) and INR350-400 crore (large) after 3-4 years.
Inventory turns: stores reach 3x inventory turnover in 2-3 years and 4.5-5x after 4-5 years. Company-wide inventory turnover is about 4.7x-5.0x annually.
demand_pricing: Footfall-to-conversion ratio of 81%; average ticket size about INR157,000.
Old gold exchange contributed about 25% of Q1 FY27 sales.
D.P. Swarna Plus SIP scheme launched April 2026 (minimum INR5,000 per month, 10-11 month tenure); about 50 customers contributing above INR1 lakh per month per scheme.
Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026; gold prices corrected in June to about INR1,45,000-1,50,000 per 10 gm from peaks of about INR1,70,000-1,75,000.
Fresh gold procurement at INR1,45,000-1,50,000; weighted-average inventory cost about INR1,20,000, roughly 20% below market, which management said will narrow as new purchases come in.
Inventory mix: about 80% 22-karat, 15% 18-karat, balance lower karat. Management said customers still prefer 22-karat, with lightweight 22-karat designs as the affordability response.
Management said FY26 had no meaningful industry volume growth; competition noted from national brands with multiple stores in Indore.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the DP Swarn Plus scheme and how is it being received?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched April 2026 as a SIP-based gold scheme with a INR5,000 minimum monthly contribution; about 50 customers contribute above INR1 lakh per month per scheme. Revenue contribution was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FOCO model plan and the FOCO vs COCO mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Jabalpur is a pilot revenue-sharing FOCO store with DP retaining full operational control. Plan is 2-3 franchisee stores a year over the next four to five years, with the 51-store mix described as mostly COCO and a smaller FOCO share.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reconcile the 51-store target with 3-4 stores added per year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets 6 stores in FY26-27 and 6-8 per year from FY28 to FY30; it acknowledged FY27 was slowed by the May developments and said the pace is now back to aggressive expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company hedge gold and silver as it expands?
qa_highlights.answer: Uses real-time replenishment (3-4 bookings a day with vendors), exchange-based old gold purchases, gold metal loans for extra inventory, and MCX hedging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth and what is the gold-price effect on sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 volume grew about 1-2% YoY; the balance of revenue growth came from higher gold prices and making charges. Inventory gains were about 10-15% of growth. Management said volume was not growing meaningfully in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does operating cash flow stay negative and how will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 95-98% of assets are inventory, so operating cash flow is linked to inventory build. It expects working capital efficiency to improve as the business scales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory carrying value versus market price, and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted-average cost is about INR1,20,000 vs market of INR1,51,000-1,52,000 per gram (a gap of about 20%); the gap will narrow as fresh purchases at INR1,45,000-1,50,000 enter inventory. Management said profitability depends on making charges.

qa_highlights.question: What volume and revenue growth should be expected for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 10% volume growth for both FY27 and FY28; revenue growth will depend on gold prices.

risks_watch: Volume growth of only 1-2% against 58% revenue growth; the gap depends on gold prices and making charges.
Operating cash flow has been negative for three years, per an analyst; management attributes it to inventory build.

544162|2026-03.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9%, with Q4 revenue at Rs 2,414 Crores (+2.3% QoQ) and EBITDAaL margin of 47.9%.

544162|2026-06.headline: Bharti Hexacom Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% QoQ to Rs2,510 Cr with EBITDAaL margin of 48.2%, while homes net adds slowed to 75k.
544162|2026-06.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs2,510 Crores, up 4% sequentially, with EBITDAaL of about Rs1,210 Crores at a 48.2% margin. Mobile added about 210,000 net customers on a 29 million base, with ARPU at Rs259 helped by one extra day. Homes, office and other business net adds were 75k and revenue grew about 8% sequentially; management attributed the slower homes intake to a deliberate tightening of acquisition quality. Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) was about Rs830 Crores and net debt excluding leases was about Rs960 Crores (0.2x EBITDAaL). The call was a joint Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom webinar, and most Q&A addressed group-level topics.

Homes, office and other net adds

Rajasthan was described as extremely competitive, while the Northeast position is comfortable; intensity on customer acquisition is said to be no different from other circles.

qa_highlights.question: Has the homes outlook changed given acquisition-policy changes and rising chipset costs?

qa_highlights.question: How many of the 400 relevant cities are in Hexacom's circles, and how big is the homes opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray estimated about 15-17 of the 400 cities are in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, and said the figure would be confirmed later. Wireless plus wired is the chosen strategy in these terrain-heavy circles.

544166|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR113 crores and EBITDA 28% to INR23 crores (~20% margin), with PAT near INR8 crores held back by H2 hiring.
544166|2026-03.overview: Emmforce reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about INR113 crores, up 27% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR23 crores (up 28%) and PAT of about INR8 crores. Management attributed the PAT moderation to manpower hired ahead of the US export programme and higher depreciation from EMSPL and capacity capex. The US OEM export order contributed only about INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026, after production started in December 2025 and final customer go-ahead came end-February. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR195 crores (INR165 crores automotive plus INR30 crores agri) and FY28 of about INR240 crores, with EBITDA margins of 20-22% and PAT near 10%.

544167|2026-03.headline: JNK India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 69.2% YoY to Rs 344.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2%; FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%.
544167|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 344.6 crore (+69.2% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 52.3 crore (+89.9%) at a 15.2% margin and PAT of Rs 33 crore (+149.5%). FY26 revenue reached Rs 838 crore (+68%), PAT Rs 64.8 crore (+114.6%), and the order book ended the year at Rs 1,961.4 crore after Rs 1,694.4 crore of FY26 inflows. Management attributed margin expansion mainly to project mix (legacy orders completed in Q1-Q2) and guided 14-15% EBITDA margin as sustainable. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 25-30%, with Dangote refinery and fertilizer reformer awards as key near-term catalysts.

segments.commentary: Contributed 3.1% of FY26 revenue and 1.3% of order book; described as a new segment.

segments.name: Flares, incinerators and others
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.3% of FY26 revenue and about 1.2% of order book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 25-30% YoY, implying roughly Rs 1,050-1,090 crore on the FY26 base; management also called 25-30% feasible for FY28.
EBITDA margin expected in the 14-15% range going forward, based on Q3 and Q4 FY26 run-rate, with conservatism due to commodity price risk.
Revenue phasing: Q1 expected to be lowest, Q4 highest; H2 expected at roughly 40-60% of FY27 revenue.
Order book expected to cross about Rs 2,000 crore by end of FY27.
Operating cash flow expected to remain positive in FY27, though not on a large scale.
Dangote refinery fired heater award expected in Q1 FY27 and reformer award in Q2 or Q3 FY27; fertilizer reformer bid submission in Q1 with finalisation in Q2 or Q3.
Waste gas handling package at export expected to close within one to two weeks; clean aviation fuel bid lost (not lowest bidder).
Chemdist expected to add 10-15% of group revenue in the first couple of years.
capex_capacity: No major capex planned; management said FY27 growth needs little capex.
Planned smaller domestic facility for critical fabrication and storage, capex about Rs 10-15 crore; current facility is mainly export-oriented.
About 120 in-house engineers; fabrication outsourced to approved shops near sites, specialised bought-out items sourced from approved Indian suppliers.

Current order book expected to be executed over roughly two years.

Export opportunities of about Rs 4,000 crore in Africa, Middle East and Russia; Middle East fertilizer/petchem opportunity of $200-300 million over two to three years.
Domestic refinery/petchem projects (BPCL Andhra, IOCL Paradip, Haldia) expected to take six months to a year due to crude pricing pressures; cracking furnace order opportunity likely in FY28.
Commodity pricing: generally no pass-through clauses except limited PSU contracts; procurement placed within one to two months of contract award.
Royalty: technical fee up to 2% of order value on exports booked in JNK India's name for items common with JNK Global.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion was project mix, and what is the normalised EBITDA run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA was about 7% in Q1, 12% in Q2, 14% in Q3 and above 15% in Q4 due to legacy project completion and new projects on input accounting; 14-15% is the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Has EIL issued RFQs for Dangote Phase 2, and is JNK prequalified?
qa_highlights.answer: Both inquiries received and prequalified for fired heaters and reformers, plus flares; fired heater award expected Q1 FY27, reformer Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow is already positive, though modest; improvement driven by private and export customers with better down payments versus PSU orders.

qa_highlights.answer: Unbilled revenue mainly from new cracker furnace and process plant projects with private customers; expected to convert to cash in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Can execution capacity support Rs 2,000-2,500 crore annual revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth needs balancing capability, handling and working capital; 25-30% annual growth appears feasible, with capacity built year on year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chemdist green hydrogen technology and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology produces hydrogen as a by-product from green ethanol to ethyl acetate using a special catalyst; first project from Hydrogen Valley Pune, Rs 70 crore backlog; commercial-scale proof targeted next year. Standalone solar EPC not planned.

risks_watch: Commodity price volatility and geopolitical disruption to imports and exports; limited pass-through clauses on contracts.

Dangote and reformer award timing (Q1-Q3 FY27) and competition from European and other bidders; clean aviation fuel bid lost.

Chemdist technology not yet commercially proven; margin uplift from JV deferred by a couple of years.

rows.why: Management says FY27 growth needs little capex and no utilisation metric exists; only a Rs 10-15 crore domestic facility is planned, so a major capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.why: Domestic refinery/petchem projects (BPCL Andhra, IOCL Paradip, Haldia) are delayed six months to a year by crude pricing pressure, and clean aviation fuel bid was lost, with H2 carrying 40-60% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Chemdist green hydrogen technology is not commercially proven; commercial-scale proof targeted next year, and cracking furnace opportunity is likely in FY28, with Chemdist adding 10-15% of group revenue in the first couple of years.

rows.label: Dangote Phase 2 refinery awards
rows.why: JNK is prequalified for fired heaters, reformers and flares, with a combined bid with JNK Global as main bidder against European and Chinese competitors, and the Rs 4,000 crore bid pipeline converts at 25-30%.

rows.label: Operating cash flow positive but modest
rows.why: Management says operating cash flow is already positive, but it was negative for three years, and unbilled revenue from cracker furnace and process plant projects is expected to convert in about three months.

rows.label: Export pipeline and Middle East fertilizer opportunity
rows.why: Export opportunities of about Rs 4,000 crore in Africa, Middle East and Russia and a $200-300 million Middle East fertilizer/petchem opportunity over two to three years, while the waste gas export package is expected to close within one to two weeks.

544167|2026-06.headline: JNK India Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore; EBITDA margin 11.8% after Chemdist losses, PAT up 8.5x to INR 9.6 crore.
544167|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore and EBITDA rose 3.1x to INR 21.9 crore, with margin at 11.8% versus 7% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA margin was 14%, with the gap explained by an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore at the JNK Chemdist JV. Order book stood at INR 1,801 crore as of 30 June 2026, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin was reiterated. An export order received on 8 June 2026 was cancelled before any costs were incurred, due to licensor technical approval not materialising.

segments.name: Heating equipment (core)
segments.commentary: About 60% of the current opportunity pipeline; management targets heating at about 60% of revenue in the medium term. Export bids (about INR 3,000 crore) are mainly heating, largely routed through JNK Global.

segments.name: Non-heating / adjacencies (process plants, metals & minerals, offshore, renewables)
segments.commentary: About 40% of pipeline, with domestic bids of INR 3,000-plus crore. Target is about 40% of revenue from non-heating within 3-5 years; hit rate expected 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist Technologies (JV)
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.8% of group revenue in Q1 FY27 with an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore on high fixed costs. Guided to 10-15% of JNK India revenue and about 20% gross margin; expected to turn profitable by year-end. Current green hydrogen orders about INR 50 crore.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of about 20-25% for FY27 maintained.
Full-year EBITDA margin guidance of about 12-14% maintained; management said there is no change, though the company later said it would recheck the figures it had announced.
Pipeline of more than INR 6,000 crore (about 50:50 export and domestic); management expects these bids to be finalised in FY27 with a hit rate of 20-25% in heating.
Refinery and fertiliser order finalisation expected in Q2-Q3 FY27.
BPCL Bina execution to occur uniformly in FY27 and FY28; EBITDA in line with guidance.
Chemdist expected to be EBITDA-positive by year-end FY27 (full year, not a specific quarter).

Non-fund-based (bank guarantee) limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; no significant debt raising expected in the next 4-6 quarters, per management.
Revenue seasonality: Q1 is 10-15% of full-year revenue, H1 30-35%, H2 60-70%.
demand_pricing: Order book INR 1,801 crore at 30 June 2026; pipeline above INR 6,000 crore, up from about INR 4,000 crore previously.
Export pipeline about INR 3,000 crore, mainly Africa (Nigeria, Ethiopia) and Middle East; Dangote Phase 2 under discussion, described as a likely repeat order.
Non-heating TAM in India cited as USD 300-500 million (offshore) and USD 500 million-1 billion (metals and minerals); target project size USD 30-60 million, up to about INR 1,000-2,000 crore.
Commodity prices fluctuating; management said ongoing projects are costed and sub-vendor orders placed on fixed-price basis, so no major margin impact.
Working capital: large customers (Reliance, private companies, BPCL Bina) have friendly payment terms; JNK Global bank guarantees on back-to-back export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue target beyond FY27 and capacity to ramp non-heating business?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth of 20-25% annually; non-heating to reach about 40% of revenue in 3-5 years. Management said diversification will not ramp within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export order cancelled and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancelled due to end-user licensor technical approval not materialising; EPC contractor was confident, and no costs had been incurred. The licensor has since qualified JNK for future projects but not ongoing ones. SOPs being tightened.

qa_highlights.question: Margin decline in Q1 despite gross margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Chemdist operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore; standalone EBITDA margin was 14% on lower Q1 revenue of about INR 170 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Hit rate and TAM in new non-heating segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected hit rate of about 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating; target bids of USD 30-60 million, and EBITDA margin in line with 12-14% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: JNK Global cooperation agreement renewal (3-year term in DRHP)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not formally renewed yet; management believes it is in force or continues automatically, with no change in terms.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and accounting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue recognition moved from output to input method; unbilled revenue about INR 200-221 crore at end Q1. Management said working capital cycle is unchanged as customer payment schedules are unchanged.

risks_watch: Export order cancellation (8 June 2026 order) shows licensor approval risk on international EPC contracts.
Chemdist JV losses until break-even; management expects year-end profitability but gave no quarterly guidance.

Unclear reconciliation of EBITDA guidance (12-14% now vs 14-15% previously cited by an analyst) and corrections to the presentation, including a revised filing for standalone profit-after-tax margin rows.

544172|2026-03.headline: Indegene Q4 FY26 revenue crossed ₹1,000 crore for the first time (+32.8% YoY); FY26 revenue ₹35,105 million, up 23.6% in INR.
544172|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first quarter above ₹1,000 crore revenue, up 6.5% QoQ and 32.8% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.2% YoY to ₹1,889 million, but after a ₹241 million forward-contract hedge charge the reported EBITDA was ₹1,648 million. Reported Q4 PAT was ₹797 million after a ₹203 million one-time provision for a 2020 US TCPA class action; management says adjusted PAT grew 12.7% YoY for FY26. Management declined to give formal revenue guidance but said the pipeline is larger and better qualified than at any prior year end.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹4,419 million in FY25 (162% of PAT)

financial_highlights.change: ₹1,258 million lower YoY after ₹7,253 million acquisition outflows

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial (ex-BioPharm)
segments.commentary: Grew about 17% YoY; BioPharm (acquired October 2025) grew 15% QoQ in Q4. Q4 included a Tectonic engagement with the largest customer for Germany.

segments.name: Enterprise Medical Services (EMS)
segments.commentary: Grew about 16% YoY. Q4 wins included a MedInfo engagement with a biotech, and a GenAI pharmacovigilance win with a medical devices client using NAEM.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America 71.6%, Europe 25.5%, Rest of World 2.9%; North America rose about 2 points on BioPharm, which is entirely US-focused.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance; management said the pipeline entering FY27 is stronger, more balanced and better qualified than any prior year end.
Management expects profitability and EBITDA margins to improve in FY27, with the second half of FY27 reverting to earlier higher margin levels as the ~150 bps investment drag is absorbed.
Margins are expected to stay within the historical range; any leverage above that will be reinvested.
PAT in FY27 expected to rise significantly, helped by higher interest income on cash, amortization stabilizing in the latter half of FY27, and fading one-offs.
The $10 million+ ACV omnichannel deal signed in Q3 has started but will be fully recognized in FY27 because of outcome-based pricing.
Tectonic is expected to become a material growth driver for enterprise commercial in FY27; the largest customer is targeted to cross $50 million.
BioPharm G&A synergies expected to show from the next quarter, with data subscription and go-to-market synergies phasing in through FY27.
Final dividend proposed at ₹2.25 per share, up from ₹2 (12.5%), subject to AGM approval.
capex_capacity: R&D spend rose to slightly above 2% of revenue in FY26, with GTM and domain-expertise investments continuing.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cohort is stable, with one client at $9.9 million placed in the lower bucket. Some large clients are taking longer to change operating models, but management expects the cohort to grow.

qa_highlights.question: How defensible is the domain-knowledge moat against LLM commoditization?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the moat is domain expertise plus proprietary data, with multiple frontier models and specialist AI partners orchestrated together. It said LLMs are not reliable enough for regulated operating-grade work over the next 3 to 5 years, so human-in-the-loop remains necessary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk that AI investment keeps margins from recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are expected to recover within a few quarters because investments are absorbed, and that it will reinvest any excess above the current margin range rather than expand margins beyond it.

qa_highlights.question: What is Cortex, and is the AI in-house or a wrapper?
qa_highlights.answer: Cortex is a knowledge engineering platform for building agentic workflows for life sciences with enterprise security. It sits on frontier models plus specialist AI such as computer vision and large action models, with the domain layer decoupled from the technology layer.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth drivers and what would be different?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described FY27 as a year of scaling FY26 initiatives, pointing to Tectonic with two customers in long-term engagements, the $10 million deal converting in FY27, and consistent $1 million+ wins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a strategy for small and mid-size pharma and generics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is expanding rapidly in mid-size and small companies, with launch models for small biotechs. Generics contribute some revenue, but innovator pharma is prioritised because of the $100 million client opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What was the constant-currency organic growth in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said 12% YoY organic in constant currency and a little over 3% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook after integrating BioPharm?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said integration finished ahead of schedule in late February, with G&A synergies expected from the next quarter and data, operations and GTM synergies phasing in through FY27.

rows.label: $10M+ ACV omnichannel deal fully recognised in FY27
rows.why: Deal was signed in Q3 FY26 and has started; outcome-based pricing means full recognition in FY27, with Q4 bookings including seven $1M+ ACV deals and one $3M+ clinical deal.

rows.label: BioPharm G&A and data/GTM synergies phasing in
rows.why: Integration finished ahead of schedule in late February 2026, with G&A synergies expected from the next quarter and data and GTM synergies phasing in through FY27 after the ₹7,253m acquisition outflow.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI differentiation, the FY27 pipeline and Tectonic, and cautious on margins, which it framed conservatively with reinvestment; analysts pushed on the $10M+ client cohort staying flat at 10, AI commoditisation risk, and whether AI spend would keep margins from recovering.

544172|2026-06.headline: Indegene Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.7% YoY to INR10,631m, with EBITDA margin at 16.9% and guidance for a return to 19–20% by Q4 FY27.
544172|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR10,631 million, up 39.7% YoY in rupee terms and 6% QoQ, with USD revenue of $112.5 million up 26.5% YoY and 2.5% QoQ. Reported EBITDA was INR1,795 million at a 16.9% margin, up 50 bps QoQ against a prior quarter hit by roughly 240 bps of undesignated forex mark-to-market. PAT rose 45.9% QoQ to INR1,162 million (10.9% of revenue). Management reiterated that margins will normalise to the 19–20% band by Q3/Q4 FY27, driven by a large outcome-based omnichannel deal recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and workforce productivity gains.

financial_highlights.change: +50 bps QoQ reported; prior quarter hit ~240 bps from MTM on undesignated hedges

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 70.6% of revenue in Q1 FY27; segment mix described as stable QoQ.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: 75.1% of revenue; mix described as stable.

segments.name: Accounts beyond top 20
segments.commentary: Contribute 33.4% of total revenue; almost doubled YoY in rupee terms; management says this drove growth.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected back in the 19%–20% range in H2 FY27; management confirmed 19–20% for Q4 FY27 when asked, pulling forward the earlier 6–8 quarter normalisation window (from Oct 2025) to 6 quarters, i.e., by Q4 FY27.
Organic growth in FY27 expected to be better than FY26, with acceleration in H2.
Outcome-based omnichannel engagement (north of $10 million ACV) starts recognising revenue from Q3 FY27; costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, so most revenue expected to drop to bottom line.
Q2 wage hike cycle expected to be offset by workforce transformation savings and Tectonic-related revenue ramp, keeping margins stable rather than declining as in historical Q2.
Undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026; management says hedge accounting adoption removes future MTM volatility from operating margins.
capex_capacity: Management said proprietary tech investment (data layer, Cortex context layer, apps and workflows) has been ratcheted up, but costs continue to be expensed rather than capitalised, though management acknowledged a technical case for capitalisation.
Workforce transformation and Gen AI productivity initiatives across operations and support functions expected to widen progressively.
demand_pricing: Active client count rose 14 QoQ to 105; customers in $10M–$25M bucket increased by 2 to 9; $1M+ clients rose from 36 to 54 over two years (per management, since Q1 FY25).

Q1 deal wins: one $3M–$5M deal with a top-5 customer (content platform migration); four $1M–$3M annual contracts (three commercial, one medical), including Tectonic extension from Germany to Spain; several sub-$1M lead-in deals.
Large Tectonic (Gen AI) engagement in Germany showed measured offtake on existing scope but expanded to Spain.

Outcome-based (pure) contracts are a small part; about 60% of revenue is output-plus-outcome based, with the rest largely hybrid FTE contracts. Hybrid deals typically take 3–4 quarters to ramp to full output revenue.
Renewals run on Jan–Dec cycles; net revenue retention stated above 100%; no major enterprise renewal loss historically.
Industry: top 20 global pharma revenue growing roughly 10%–12% YoY in calendar Q1 2026; immunology, oncology and mental health growing double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a delay to margin normalisation, given Q4 vs H2 wording, and what is the nature of the investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delay: the normalisation is now targeted within 6 quarters from Oct 2025 (by March 2027), not the 6–8 range. Investments were in onsite commercial, medical, consulting and tech staff, plus large strategic deals (Tectonic; a >$1B US brand portfolio physician-outreach contract). Management confirmed this holds despite these deal investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic growth and BioPharm contribution; what was constant-currency growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer splits BioPharm organic vs inorganic; it is now well integrated and both are in the base sequentially. Constant-currency growth was estimated at about 2.6%–2.7% QoQ, versus USD growth of 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of contracts are outcome-based and how does revenue and order book flow?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of contracts are output or outcome based; dedicated FTEs outside this are specialist roles supporting those contracts. Hybrid deals start FTE revenue within a month and ramp output revenue over 3–4 quarters. The large omnichannel deal is pure outcome-based with about 3 quarters of revenue deferral; the client has shared revenue upticks for 5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Gen AI strategy, IP protection, and data ownership concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a layered stack: Indegene data universe at the base, Cortex knowledge layer that is model-agnostic, agent layer (Content Super App, Medical Writing platform), and Transform AI workflows. Management said clients keep data ownership via contract and expect larger pharma to move toward on-prem open-weight models.

qa_highlights.question: What percentage of revenue is AI-led, and what are the margin drivers beyond already-incurred costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify AI-led revenue, saying AI is embedded across all work; content volumes rose 5–7x with falling unit costs. Other margin drivers are growth on fixed GTM and leadership costs and the Tectonic revenue uptick.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 19–20% margin target for Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes for Q4 FY27 when asked directly.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the outcome-based omnichannel deal recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and on the Tectonic and other large deals ramping; delays would push back the 19–20% target.
Enterprise AI adoption described as measured; Tectonic offtake on existing scope is slow.
Undesignated hedges remain material until December 2026, with residual accounting volatility.
US policy and drug pricing / MFN decisions flagged as the key external watch item; management currently sees the policy outlook as stable.
Receivables: DSO up 4 days to 67; management sees credit risk as minimal, but biotech and emerging-pharma contracts and outcome-based milestones are being monitored.
Q2 wage hike cycle could pressure margin before offsets kick in.
key_quotes: Nothing we have seen in this quarter changes that expectation. And if anything, our conviction that we are on track for this has increased.
What we are also seeing is that while the enthusiasm is real, enterprise adoption remains measured and the pace of change on the ground is slower.
No, there is no delay. In fact, what we said is 6 to 8. We had got a range over there. We are saying we don't need this range.
We're not breaking up organic and inorganic growth from a BioPharm perspective, anymore.
544172|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on margin recovery and deal pipeline, repeatedly saying nothing this quarter changes the 19–20% expectation and that conviction has increased. More guarded on enterprise AI adoption (described as measured and slower), and declined to quantify AI-led revenue or split BioPharm organic vs inorganic growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated 19-20% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 (confirmed when asked) from 16.9% in Q1, driven by the omnichannel deal (>$10M ACV) recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 with costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, plus workforce productivity savings.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 organic growth better than FY26 with H2 acceleration; Q1 USD revenue up 26.5% YoY to $112.5m and 2.5% QoQ, with active clients up 14 QoQ to 105 and $1M+ clients up to 54.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation not disclosed and no capacity additions discussed; proprietary tech spend is expensed rather than capitalised, and no new plant or capex plan was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides FY27 organic growth better than FY26 with H2 acceleration; USD revenue grew 26.5% YoY to $112.5m, but no numeric FY27 revenue guide was given to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery to 19-20% by Q4 FY27 depends on the >$10M ACV omnichannel deal starting revenue in Q3 FY27 and on Q2 wage hikes being offset; Q1 EBITDA margin was only 16.9%, so a slip of the deal ramp would push the target back.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gen AI stack (Cortex knowledge layer, agent layer with Content Super App and Medical Writing platform, Transform AI workflows) is described, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Omnichannel outcome-based deal revenue from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Deal above $10M ACV recognises revenue from Q3 FY27 with about 3 quarters of deferral, and costs already incurred since Q4 FY26, so most of the revenue should drop to margin.

rows.label: Workforce transformation and Gen AI productivity savings
rows.why: Savings are expected to offset the Q2 wage hike cycle and keep margins stable, versus the usual Q2 decline.

rows.label: Tectonic Gen AI expansion from Germany to Spain
rows.why: Tectonic extended to Spain in Q1 via a $1-3M annual contract, but offtake on existing German scope is measured and hybrid deals take 3-4 quarters to ramp.

tone.note: Management was confident that the 19-20% EBITDA margin is back by Q4 FY27 with no delay, backed by the omnichannel deal and workforce savings, but was guarded on enterprise AI adoption and declined to quantify AI-led revenue or split BioPharm organic versus inorganic growth.
